title: Psalms 119:82
text: Fail for thy word; pine away in looking for the fulfilment of thy word of promise.

title: Psalms 119:83
text:
Bottle in the smoke; dried up and withered. 
 
By great and long-continued afflictions the soul may be deprived of rest, peace, and joy; yet it will still cleave to God's service.

title: Psalms 119:84
text: How many are the days of thy servant? the meaning of this question in the original seems to be, To what do his days amount?  He pleads the shortness of life as a reason why God should speedily deliver him. Compare  Job 10:20 .

title: Psalms 119:88
text: The effect of God's grace bestowed upon the righteous is an increase of the fruits of obedience.

title: Psalms 119:89
text: Settled in heaven; established in God's presence beyond the possibility of change.

title: Psalms 119:90
text: Abideth; remaineth unmoved.  The stability of the earth is the effect of God's unchangeableness, and the same unchangeableness is shown in the fulfilment of his word.

title: Psalms 119:96
text:
An end of all perfection; of himan excellence. 
 
  Exceeding broad; searching the heart and motives, and requiring every thing that is excellent. 
 
Nothing merely human is perfect; perfection is attained only by perfect obedience to the revealed will of God.

title: Psalms 119:103
text: The law of God is the delight of his people, and shows them the path of duty, safety, and blessedness.

title: Psalms 119:105
text: A lamp unto my feet; showing the way in which I should go.

title: Psalms 119:109
text: My soul is continually in my hand; my life is constantly in danger.

title: Psalms 119:113
text: Vain thoughts; the original word, which occurs only here, seems to denote divided, or inconstant thoughts, now inclining to obedience, and now to disobedience.  Compare  I Kings 18:21 James 1:8 .

title: Psalms 119:117
text: The only safety of believers is in being kept by the mighty power of God through faith unto salvation.

title: Psalms 119:122
text: Be surety for thy servant for good; be surety for me, that in the cause between me and my adversaries I shall receive justice.  See note to  Job 17:3 .

title: Psalms 119:127
text:
vv 127-128. 
 
  Therefore; because of the excellence of thy word, which the psalmist has been setting forth throughout the whole psalm.  See  Psalms 119:129 .

title: Psalms 119:130
text:
The entrance of thy words; more literally, the opening of thy words, that is, the unfolding of Scripture to my soul through the illumination of thy Spirit. 
 
The reception of divine truth illuminates and purifies the soul.

title: Psalms 119:147
text:
I prevented the dawning of the morning; cried unto God during the night season and before the dawn of day. 
 
The way to the throne of mercy is always open, and God sees the wants of his people amidst the darkness of midnight, as well as in the splendors of noonday.

title: Psalms 119:155
text: Without seeking for the pearl of great price we shall not be likely to obtain it.

title: Psalms 119:160
text: Thy word is true from the beginning; or, the sum of thy word is true; that is, the whole of it taken as a body.

title: Psalms 119:164
text:
Seven times; many times, often. 
 
The righteous pray with all prayer and supplication in the Spirit, and watch thereunto with all perseverance.

title: Psalms 119:165
text:
Nothing shall offend them; they shall have no stumbling-blocks, their way shall be safe and prosperous. 
 
Obedience to God's law is the only way of peace and safety.

title: Psalms 119:168
text: All my ways are before thee; thine omniscient eye is upon all my ways, so that if in any thing I depart from thy commands, thou seest it, and wilt treat me accordingly.

title: Psalms 119:175
text: Thy judgments; by which thou sustainest the righteous and overthrowest the wicked.  See above in  Psalms 119:149 Psalms 119:156 .

title: Psalms 119:176
text: Gone astray; wandered from the fold, and thus become exposed to misery and ruin.   Ezekiel 34:6

title: Psalms 120:1
text: Title, A Song of degrees; or, A Song of ascents, the title of this and the fourteen following psalms: probably so called because they were arranged to be sung on the occasion of the ascent of the Israelites to Jerusalem to keep the yearly festivals.   Deuteronomy 16:15

title: Psalms 120:2
text: When the slander of false tongues is directed against the faithful servants of God, they ought to bear it patiently, remembering that he will in due time deliver them, and punish their caluminiators.

title: Psalms 120:3
text: What shall be given unto thee? what reward shall God give unto thee for thy wickedness.

title: Psalms 120:4
text:
Sharp arrows--coals; God will give these to the false tongue.  As it has wounded others like sharp arrows, and burned them like coals of fire, so will God do to it. 
 
  Arrows of the mighty; such as the mighty warrior shoots. 
 
  Juniper; a shrub, different from our juniper, from the roots of which charcoal was made anciently, as it is at the present day.

title: Psalms 120:5
text:
Mesech; a barbarous people east of the Black sea. 
 
  Kedar; an Arabian tribe. Mesech and Kedar are put generally for foreign and hostile nations.

title: Psalms 120:7
text: The friends of God are friends of peace, and it is a great grief to them to be compelled to dwell with persons of a contentious spirit.

title: Psalms 121:1
text:
I will lift up mine eyes; an expression of longing desire and faith. 
 
  Unto the hills; the hills of Jerusalem, where God had his earthly abode.  Lifting up the eyes to these hills, was lifting them up to God.  Psalms 20:2  
 
Looking to God for help is a mark which distinguishes the true believer from all other men.

title: Psalms 121:5
text: Thy shade; thy protection.   Isaiah 25:4

title: Psalms 121:6
text:
The sun shall not smite thee by day, nor the moon by night; no hurtful influence of the day, which the sun rules, nor of the night, which the moon rules, shall harm thee. 
 
When God grants us his protection, we are safe in the midst of the greatest dangers.

title: Psalms 121:8
text:
Thy going out and thy coming in; all the daily employments of life, in the pursuit of which we go out and in. 
 
The righteous have an almighty Friend and Keeper ever present to help them in trouble, support them in temptation, guide them in perplexity, and defend them from all injury.  For this reason it is both their privilege and their duty to be always cheerful and tranquil.

title: Psalms 122:1
text:
Into the house of the Lord; into the courts of the temple; for into the temple itself none but the priests could enter. 
 
All good men love the church of God and her ordinances, and will not fail to be found in their place in his sanctuary whenever he gives them an opportunity.

title: Psalms 122:3
text: Compact together; having its fortifications and houses closely joined together.  This describes its strength and populousness, and the close identification of interests among its inhabitants.

title: Psalms 122:4
text:
Whither the tribes go up; to keep the annual festivals. 
 
  Unto the testimony of Israel; more literally, [which is] a testimony for Israel; that is, an ordinance which God gave to Israel,  Deuteronomy 16:16 . 
 
The public worship of God is expressly commanded in the Bible, and no family, community, or nation that neglects it can expect permanent prosperity, either temporal or spiritual.

title: Psalms 122:5
text: Thrones of judgment; seats where judges dispensed justice.  These are called the thrones of the house of David, because the judges who sat in them acted under David, or under the kings of his family who succeeded him.

title: Psalms 122:6
text: They who pray for and seek the peace of God's church always have true prosperity.

title: Psalms 122:8
text:
For my brethren and companions' sakes; all the pious Israelites, whose peace lay in the peace of Jerusalem. 
 
In the welfare of God's church is included the welfare of each one of God's children.  Gor his own sake, then, and for the sake of his brethren and companions, he should seek her peace.

title: Psalms 122:9
text:
Because of the house of the Lord our God; because Jerusalem contained the house of the Lord, that is, because it was the seat of God's worship. 
 
The institutions of religion are to every city or nation its most precious and valuable possession.

title: Psalms 123:1
text: When affliction leads us to seek help and comfort from God, it has the effect for which it is sent.

title: Psalms 123:2
text:
Unto the hand of their masters--unto the hand of her mistress; because it is the hand upon which they are dependent; the hand which supplies, governs, and protects them. 
 
Since all our trials come upon us by God's appointment for our profit, we should look to him alone for deliverance, and use no means to this end but such as are consistent with his revealed will.

title: Psalms 123:4
text: "The Lord seeth not as man seeth."  They whom he most loves and honors are very often the objects of scorn and derision to the proud and luxurious.

title: Psalms 124:2
text: When men rose up against us; the men here spoken of are the enemies of Israel, the true visible church of God; the men who sought to destroy the nation, and with it the institutions of religion.

title: Psalms 124:3
text: Quick; alive, as men are devoured by wild beasts, or swallowed up by earthquakes.   Numbers 16:33

title: Psalms 124:5
text:
Proud waters; swelling waters, but with an allusion to the pride of Israel's enemies. 
 
God's church hath no power of her own to withstand the assaults of Satan and wicked men.  Were it not for his continual presence and protection, these would soon utterly destroy her.

title: Psalms 124:7
text:
Our soul; our life; that is, we have escaped alive. 
 
God can easily break all the snares which wicked men spread for the feet of his people; and he will do so, for the sake of his own glory and their good.

title: Psalms 124:8
text: Since God who made heaven and earth is the Helper of his people, their cause must prosper, until the whole world shall be brought to the knowledge and obedience of the gospel.

title: Psalms 125:1
text: God always rewards the confidence of his people, and will in due time deliver them.  The whose faith in him is unshaken, cannot be moved by any assaults of the wicked.

title: Psalms 125:2
text:
As the mountains are round about Jerusalem; Jerusalem is surrounded by hills higher than itself. 
 
  Round about his people; protects them on every side. 
 
It is impossible that any scheme for the overthrow of God's church should prosper; for his omnipotence is round about her from age to age.

title: Psalms 125:3
text:
The rod of the wicked; the septre of wicked rulers. 
 
  The lot of the righteous; the inheritance which God has given to them. 
 
God will not allow the wicked perpetually to oppress the righteous, lest, through despair of his mercy, they should be driven into sin.

title: Psalms 125:5
text:
Lead them forth; to destruction. 
 
They who choose to go with the wicked in life, must have their portion with them in death.

title: Psalms 126:1
text:
The captivity of Zion; her captivity in Babylon. 
 
  We were like them that dream; our deliverance was so surprising that it seemed to us a dream, and not a reality. 
 
It is an easy thing for God to grant to his people great and surprising deliverances, and he has often done so in the hour of their deepest distress.

title: Psalms 126:2
text: God will so order his dealings with his church that ungodly men shall be compelled to see and acknowledge his presence with her, and his wonderful interpositions in her behalf.

title: Psalms 126:4
text:
Turn again our captivity; the work of restoring the captive Jews to their home had been begun,  Psalms 126:1  and here the psalmist prays that it may be completed. 
 
  As the streams in the south; the south of Palestine, bordering on the desert.  These are, as in other hot and desert regions, dry during the summer; but when the rainy season returns, they are again filled with water.  The psalmist prays that God would work a like change in the condition of his people. 
 
God's past favors should encourage us to hope and pray for more.

title: Psalms 126:6
text: The most successful undertakings have often been commenced in the midst of great difficulties and with much weeping.  The spiritual seed that is abundantly watered with godly tears, will bring forth a rich harvest of golden sheaves.

title: Psalms 127:1
text: In all our undertakings it is our duty to use with diligence and prudence the means of success; but unless God add his blessing, our labor will be in vain.

title: Psalms 127:2
text:
The bread of sorrows; bread earned by hard and painful toil.  Genesis 3:17  
 
  So; by aiding in building the house and keeping the city. 
 
  His beloved; the man whom he loves and takes under his protection. The meaning is, that they whom God loves and helps, accomplish easily and successfully the business of the day, and enjoy quiet sleep after it. 
 
Unbelief and practical atheism, by filling the mind in God has a tranquillizing influence, which is equally conducive to comfort and success.

title: Psalms 127:3
text: A heritage of the Lord; an inheritance given by the Lord.

title: Psalms 127:4
text: Children of the youth; born in the youth of the parents, and consequently of sufficient maturity and vigor to defend them in their old age.

title: Psalms 127:5
text:
They shall not be ashamed; the children, when they defend their parents; for they shall be successful. 
 
  In the gate; where causes were heard and decided by the judges. 
 
Well-trained and virtuous children are the best earthly defence and comfort of old age.

title: Psalms 128:1
text: God withholds no real good from them that fear and obey him.  With all spiritual blessings, he gives also every earthly comfort that is consistent with thier highest welfare.

title: Psalms 128:2
text: For thou shalt eat the labor of thy hands; what is earned by the labor of thy hands, thou shalt thyself enjoy; others shall not plunder thee of it.

title: Psalms 128:3
text:
By the sides of thy house; in the inner apartments.  I Samuel 24:3 Jonah 1:5  
 
A numerous offspring is one of the many temporal blessings promised to the righteous in the Old Testament.  When God withholds this or any other earthly good from his faithful servants, or takes it away after it has been enjoyed, he does so for the trial of their faith and patience.

title: Psalms 128:5
text: Out of Zion; the earthly residence of God.   Psalms 20:2

title: Psalms 128:6
text: To the "Israelite indeed," God can promise no higher good, apart from his own favor and friendship, than to see "the good of Jerusalem" and "peace upon Israel."

title: Psalms 129:1
text: My youth; the youth of the nation.

title: Psalms 129:2
text: The history of God's church from the beginning is a continuous fulfilment of the primitive prophecy, "It shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel."  She is always afflicted by her enemies, and always prevailing against them.

title: Psalms 129:3
text: Ploughed upon my back; furrowed my back with stripes.

title: Psalms 129:4
text: The cords of the wicked; the cords with which the wicked, the enemies of Israel, bound him.  The figure in this and the preceding verse is that if a captive bound and scourged.

title: Psalms 129:6
text:
Upon the house-tops; the flat roofs, which in the East are often covered with earth.   Isaiah 37:27  
 
  Afore it groweth up; or, afore one plucks it; before it is fit to be gathered for use. 
 
The prosperity of the enemies of God's people is always short-lived.

title: Psalms 129:8
text: Say; to the reapers, according to the custom of the age.  See  Ruth 2:4

title: Psalms 130:1
text:
Out of the depths; of affliction. 
 
The right effect of distress, whether outward or inward, is to produce sincere and earnest prayer to God, and such prayer will always be heard and answered.

title: Psalms 130:3
text:
Mark iniquities; for the purpose of punishing them. 
 
No man can stand before God on the ground of his innocency.  His only hope is in God's forgiving mercy.

title: Psalms 130:4
text: That thou mayest be feared; that is, with holy filial fear. Without the assurance that God will forgive the penitent, no man could approach him with such fear.

title: Psalms 130:6
text: When deliverance is long delayed, it is good to wait upon God in quiet submission and humble obedience.  When the right time has come, he will cause the morning to shine.

title: Psalms 130:8
text:
From all his iniquities; from sin and the suffering that follows sin. 
 
God's work in behalf of his people will not be complete till he has abolished sin in their souls, and all the consequences of sin in their souls, bodies, and estate.

title: Psalms 131:1
text:
Exercise myself in; employ myself about. 
 
Contentment in a humble sphere is a high attianment, and one peculiarly pleasing to God.   I Peter 5:6

title: Psalms 131:2
text:
Behaved; composed. 
 
  As a child that is weaned of his mother; as a weaned child lies quietly upon its mother's bosom. 
 
When God withholds or takes from us comforts of any kind, it is good to lean our souls upon him in quiet faith and submission, and let him do with us as seems good in his sight.

title: Psalms 132:1
text: Good men prefer the glory of God and the welfare of his people to their own personal ease and emolument.

title: Psalms 132:5
text: A place for the Lord; a place for the ark of the Lord, the symbol of his presence.  David transferred the ark from Kirjath-jearim to Zion, and had in mind to build a temple for it there.

title: Psalms 132:6
text:
We heard of it; of the ark.  These words are supposed to have been spoken by David and his associates when the ark, of which formerly they had only heard, was now with them on mount Zion. 
 
  Ephratah; either Bethlehem Ephratah,  Micah 5:2 , the place of the hearers, or Ephraim, to which tribe belonged Shiloh, the place of the ark in Eli's day. 
 
  In the fields of the wood; in Kirjath-jearim, which signifies, "City of woods."

title: Psalms 132:8
text: Arise, O Lord, into thy rest; thy resting-place on mount Zion. This verse and the two following coincide with Solomon's prayer at the dedication of the temple.  The psalmist prays for a renewal of God's presence and power on mount Zion.

title: Psalms 132:10
text:
Turn not away the face of thine anointed; refuse not his request. 
 
  Anointed; a common term for David, as anointed by God's appointment.

title: Psalms 132:11
text: God is well pleased with the recital of his promises, and when we comply with the conditions annexed to them, he will certainly fulfil them to us and our children.

title: Psalms 132:16
text: In the institutions of the gospel, God has made abundant provision for all the wants of his people, and he would have them always happy and joyful in his service.

title: Psalms 132:17
text:
There will I make the horn of David to bud; to make the horn of David to bud, is to continue the strength and prosperity of his kingdom. 
 
  Ordained a lamp for mine anointed; given him always a successor on the throne.   I Kings 11:36 I Kings 15:4 II Kings 8:19  
 
The recital of God's promise to David,  Psalms 132:11-18 , is in reality a prayer for its fulfilment.

title: Psalms 132:18
text: In the Lord Jesus, the last and greatest of David's line, all the promises made to David's house are fulfilled in their highest sense. His enemies God will clothe with shame, but upon himself shall his crown flourish.

title: Psalms 133:1
text: In all the relations of life, harmony is equally pleasant and promotive of strength and prosperity.  In the household of God, it is the indispensable condition of his presence and blessing.

title: Psalms 133:2
text: The precious ointment; used at Aaron's consecration as high-priest.  Leviticus 8:12

title: Psalms 133:3
text: Hermon; the high southern part of the range of mountains that runs east of Lebanon and nearly parallel with it.  It lies around the sources of the Jordan.

title: Psalms 134:1
text: In this last of the song of degrees, the people call upon the priests who minister in the temple at night to bless God,  Psalms 134:1-2 ; and the priests, in their turn, bless the people,  Psalms 134:3 .

title: Psalms 135:4
text: God's church is peculiarly dear to him, because it is in her that he displays his glory, and through her that he overthrows the kingdom of Satan.

title: Psalms 135:7
text: Since God is the author of nature, all the powers of nature are under his control, and through them he does whatsoever he pleases.

title: Psalms 135:11
text: The Amorites--Bashan; these kingdoms lay on the east of the Jordan, and are therefore not reckoned to Canaan.

title: Psalms 135:12
text: The destruction of God's enemies always tends to the enlargement and comfort of his people.

title: Psalms 135:13
text: Thy memorial; the remembrance of thee; thy mighty deeds will always be remembered and mentioned with praise and thanksgiving.

title: Psalms 135:18
text: The folly of idolaters consists in their trusting for salvation to the work of their own hands.  All who rely on their riches, wisdom, or alliances with the great and powerful, are guilty of the same folly with idolaters, and will come to the same end.

title: Psalms 135:19
text: A heart full of praise and thanksgiving towards God is most excellent and becoming in all his servants.

title: Psalms 136:1
text:
The present psalm is peculiar in its structure, the last half of each verse consisting of the burden of refrain, "for his mercy endureth for ever." 
 
"God is love."  All his acts are done in mercy and loving-kindness; and they all work together for the good of those who love him.

title: Psalms 136:15
text: God's mercy insures the overthrow of his enemies, not less than the salvation of his friends.

title: Psalms 136:23
text: In our low estate; when we were captives in Babylon.

title: Psalms 136:24
text: From our enemies; from those who carried us captive.

title: Psalms 137:1
text: When God punishes a nation for its sins, good men share in its calamities.

title: Psalms 137:5
text: Cunning; skill to act.

title: Psalms 137:6
text: The true children of God prefer the welfare of his people above their chief; and are more grieved for the calamities that come upon his church, than for any private losses and sufferings of their own.

title: Psalms 137:7
text: In the day of Jerusalem; in the day of her overthrow.  The sin here laid to the charge of the Edomites is that of rejoicing in and helping forward the destruction of Jerusalem.   Obadiah 1:10-15

title: Psalms 137:8
text:
Daughter of Babylon; the people of Babylon represented under the figure of a woman. 
 
  Happy shall he be; because he has executed God's purpose.  Ezekiel 29:18-20  
 
  That rewardeth thee as thou hast served us; a prophetic announcement from God of the coming doom of Edom.  See  Obadiah 1:15 .

title: Psalms 137:9
text: God is displeased with all who rejoice in the affliction of his servants, and will recompense their iniquity into their own bosom.

title: Psalms 138:1
text:
We have here the first of eight psalms composed by David and arranged together near the close of the book of Psalms.  The first two celebrate the glorious attributes of God as manifested in his dealings with the psalmist; the next four are prayers for deliverance in the midst of deep distress; then follow two closing psalms, in the first of which he anticipates, in the language of triumph, a complete victory over all his foes, and in the second celebrates the goodness of God after this victory is now achieved. 
 
  Before the gods; probably, in the face of all false gods. 
 
Every new mercy should excite us to new gratitude and praise; and on all suitable occasions we should publicly acknowledge God's goodness to us.   Psalms 66:16

title: Psalms 138:2
text:
Thy word; thy word of promise. 
 
  Above all thy name; above all hitherto known of thy perfections. The name of God is the sum of his perfections as they are manifested to us. 
 
God will more than fulfil the highest expectations of all who put their trust in him.

title: Psalms 138:3
text: God's servants never ask help from him in vain.

title: Psalms 138:5
text: The Old Testament prophets rightly anticipated the conversion of all nations as the final result of what God did for his ancient people.

title: Psalms 138:6
text: Nothing brings us so near to God as humility; nothing removes us so far from him as pride.

title: Psalms 138:7
text: Though God often suffers his people to be troubled by their enemies, he does not allow them to be destroyed.  He will interpose at the right time for their salvation and for the shame of their persecutors.

title: Psalms 138:8
text:
Forsake not the works of thine own hands; the works of mercy which thou hast begun in my behalf, carry on to completion. 
 
God would have us urge his past mercies towards us as an argument why he should bestow more.

title: Psalms 139:1
text: In this remarkable psalm the divine omniscience and omnipresence are set forth with wonderful vividness and power; not, however, as abstract truths, but with particular reference to the psalmist's own case.  The all seeing God, who formed him in the womb, has watched over and shaped his course every moment,  Psalms 139:13-18 .  He knows his servant's uprightness of heart, and will distinguish between him and the wicked,  Psalms 139:19-22 .  He knows his servant's weaknesses and failings also; David therefore prays that God will reveal them to him, and lead him in the way everlasting,  Psalms 139:23-24 .

title: Psalms 139:2
text: Afar off; to God's omniscience there is no limit of distance or time.

title: Psalms 139:3
text: Compassest; or, winnowest; narrowly examinest, as one examines wheat by sifting it.

title: Psalms 139:4
text: With God concealment and hypocrisy can have no place.  All within us and around us is "naked and opened unto the eyes of Him with whom we have to do."

title: Psalms 139:9
text:
If I take the wings of the morning; fly westward on the beams of the morning sun. 
 
  The uttermost parts of the sea; the most remote regions of the west, the same as "the islands of the sea."   Isaiah 11:11   From the position of the Mediterranean, the Hebrews were accustomed to speak of the west as the sea.  Thus in  Genesis 13:14 , where the four cardinal points are enumerated, the last mentioned is seaward, that is, westward.

title: Psalms 139:10
text: God's power over us is as absolute as his knowledge of us.  His omnipotence and omniscience alike compass us about, so that there is no escape from either.

title: Psalms 139:13
text: Hast possessed my reins; hast them in thy knowledge and control, as their Maker.

title: Psalms 139:14
text:
Fearfully and wonderfully; in a manner adapted to excite astonishment and awe. 
 
Our bodies are such a wonderful exhibition of God's incomprehensible skill, power, and goodness, as should inspire us with the deepest feelings of admiration and awe.

title: Psalms 139:15
text:
My substance; my frame. 
 
  Curiously wrought; literally, embroidered; a description of the delicate and complicated tissue of the human body. 
 
  In the lowest parts of the earth; hid from view, as if in the depths of the earth; the same as "in secret," and "in my mother's womb."   Psalms 139:13

title: Psalms 139:16
text:
Yet being unperfect; before my birth. 
 
  Written; as an architect has before him a written description and plan of the house which he is building. 
 
  Which in continuance were fashioned; were fashioned by a continuous growth that went on day after day.

title: Psalms 139:17
text: Meditation on God's wonderful dealings with themselves and others, is one of the sweet and blessed employments of the righteous.

title: Psalms 139:18
text: I am still with thee; I am with thee, in thy care, and in my meditations.

title: Psalms 139:22
text: God hates the character and ways of the wicked, and the feelings of all righteous men are in harmony with his.

title: Psalms 139:24
text:
The way everlasting; the old way appointed by God from ancient times; the same as "the old paths, where is the good way."  Jeremiah 1:1-52:34 Jeremiah 6:16  
 
Wicked men love self-delusion, and willingly remain ignorant of themselves.  But the good man earnestly desires and prays that God would search his heart, show him all his hidden faults, and help him to repent of them and forsake them.

title: Psalms 140:2
text: Imagine mischiefs; devise wicked plans.

title: Psalms 140:3
text: The kingdom of Satan began in this world by falsehood and guile, and it is perpetuated by the same means.  The men whom God raises as he didi David, to eminent stations in his church, must be prepared to encounter calumny and crafty assaults of every kind.  But if they put their trust in God, and go straight forward in the path of duty, he will defend and deliver them.

title: Psalms 140:7
text: Covered my head; protected it as with a shield.

title: Psalms 140:8
text: If we commit our cause to God in true humility and faith, he will not suffer the wicked ultimately to triumph over us: his glory is concerned in the exaltation of the humble and the overthrow of the proud.

title: Psalms 140:9
text: Let the mischief of their own lips cover them; let the mischief which their lips have done to me fall upon their own heads, and cover them with shame.

title: Psalms 140:10
text:
Burning coals--fire--pits; the tokens of divine wrath.  Psalms 11:6  
 
Slander and malice fall at last, like burning coals, upon the head of their authors, and consume them.  When the righteous man falls, he rises again; but he wicked fall into deep pits, to rise no more.

title: Psalms 140:11
text: Shall hunt; as an avenging enemy.

title: Psalms 140:13
text: Though for a season the course of events may seem to favor the cause of the proud and violent, God's afflicted servants have only to wait in faith and patience till his time comes, and he will deliver them, and fill their lips with songs of praise.

title: Psalms 141:2
text:
As incense--the evening sacrifice; sweet incense was burned every morning and evening on the altar of incense.   Exodus 30:7-8   The evening sacrifice was, like the morning sacrifice, which it seems here to include, a daily offering.  The psalmist beseeches God that his prayer may be like the daily incense and offering, in both permanency and acceptableness. 
 
It was an ordinance of the Levitical law, that sweet incense and sacrifices should be offered every morning and evening.  By this God teaches us that we should worship him daily and at stated seasons; and that our prayers, offered through faith in the atonement of his Son, are fragrant and pleasant to him, like the incense offered by Aaron and his sons.

title: Psalms 141:4
text:
Eat of their dainties; eating of the dainties of the wicked would imply that he had been seduced by them, and was in fellowship with them. 
 
To keep our lips from wicked words, and our hearts from the seduction of wicked men, are two very difficult undertakings.  That we may be successful in them, constant watchfulness is necessary, with a plentous supply of divine grace.

title: Psalms 141:5
text:
Which shall not break my head; many prefer to render this clause, My head shall not refuse it; that is, the reproof of the righteous, which is compared to oil. 
 
Reproof administered by righteous men is most excellent and precious in its effects.  The Christian who receives it will remember and requite it with his prayers, and if God gives him the opportunity, with his benefactions also.

title: Psalms 141:6
text:
Their judges; the judges of David's enemies, their leaders. 
 
  Overthrown in stony places; cast down among rocky precipices, and so destroyed.  This is probably a figurative way of describing their destruction. 
 
  They shall hear my words; my enemies shall then listen to my words. 
 
  For they are sweet; pleasant to all the upright in heart, because they are conformed to truth and righteousness.  The general idea is, that the overthrow of the leaders among David's persecutors shall bring them to reflection and a better state of mind. 
 
The overthrow of ringleaders in wickedness is often made the means of bringing those whom they had suduced and misled to reflection and repentance.

title: Psalms 141:7
text: Our bones are scattered; by the persecution of the wicked.

title: Psalms 142:1
text: Title, when he was in the cave; probably the cave of Adullam, to which he fled from Achish king of Gath in a friendless condition.  It was there that he began to collect a band.   I Samuel 22:1-2

title: Psalms 142:2
text: The more our troubles are multiplied, the more earnest and importunate should we be in our prayers.  God loves to have us bring before his throne all our sorrows, perplexities, and dangers.

title: Psalms 142:3
text: Knewest my path; knewest it as a friend, able and willing to direct, defend, and help.

title: Psalms 142:4
text: I looked on my right hand--cared for my soul; or, Look thou on [my] right hand, and see; for there is no man who will know me: refuge has failed me; no man careth for my soul.  He mentions his right hand, because it is there that a helper should naturally stand.  Psalms 16:8 Psalms 110:5

title: Psalms 142:5
text: When all earthly succor fails, we are called to stay our souls upon God, who always cares for us and will help us.

title: Psalms 142:6
text: God's help makes the weakest of his servants stronger than the mightiest among their foes.

title: Psalms 142:7
text:
Out of prison; David was so hemmed in by his enemies that he was like a man in prison. 
 
  The righteous shall compass me about; as my sympathizing friends. 
 
When God delivers a righteous man from trouble, all the good rejoice with him.

title: Psalms 143:1
text: In thy faithfulness--in thy righteousness; God had entered into covenant engagements with David as his servant; his faithfulness and righteousness bound him to fulfil these in delivering him from his persecutors.

title: Psalms 143:2
text:
In thy sight shall no man living be justified; the best of God's servants are sinners, and can hope for acceptance and salvation only on the ground of Christ's atonement. 
 
The true servants of God in all ages have been deeply conscious of both past and present sinfulness, and have rested their hope of acceptance and salvation, not on their own goodness, but on God's forgiving mercy, which he bestows through Christ's atoning sacrifice.  To be destitute of this feeling is to be without grace.

title: Psalms 143:3
text:
Hath persectued my soul; pursued me with the intention of taking my life. 
 
  Hath smitten my life down to the ground; as a wounded roe is smitten down by the hunter, and lies bleeding and ready to be destroyed. 
 
  In darkness; in caves and desolate places, if the words are to be taken literally; but perhaps he put darkness for a desolate, lonely, and sorrowful condition.

title: Psalms 143:5
text:
The days of old; when God displayed his saving power. 
 
When our spirit is overwhelmed within us, it is good to encourage ourselves by the remembrance of what God has done for us and for others in the days of old.  What he was then, he is now--a God able and willing to hear and answer prayer.

title: Psalms 143:7
text: Into the pit; the grave.

title: Psalms 143:8
text: In the morning; early, in good time.

title: Psalms 143:10
text:
Into the land of uprightness; or, in a level land, where my feet shall not stumble.  Compare  Psalms 27:11 , "Lead me in a plain path," where the original word is the same as here. 
 
Two principal marks of the true believer are prayerful anxiety to learn the will of God, and dependence on God's Spirit for strength to perform it.

title: Psalms 143:11
text:
Quicken me; make me live both spiritually and temporally. 
 
God's own glory and faithfulness are concerned in delivering his people from trouble.  Prayers that lay hold on these always sooner or later prevail.

title: Psalms 143:12
text:
For I am thy servant; sincere and upright: since David was by God's appointment the head of his visible church, and was acting in her behalf, the destruction of his enemies was the destruction of her enemies. 
 
The persecutors of God's servants place themselves in a dreadful situation; remaining such, they make it necessary that he should manifest his mercy in their destruction.

title: Psalms 144:1
text: This psalm was probably composed near the time of  Psalms 18:1-50 , with which the first part of it has a striking agreement.

title: Psalms 144:2
text:
My people; all the people subject to David, both Israelites and foreigners. 
 
All the success of kings and military leaders is from the Lord, and he would have them acknowledge his hand in it.

title: Psalms 144:3
text: Takest knowledge of him--makest account of him; by bestowing upon him such wonderful mercies as I have received.  Compare  II Samuel 7:18 .

title: Psalms 144:4
text: The consideration of our littleness and unworthiness enhances our view of God's wonderful loving-kindness towards us.

title: Psalms 144:5
text: Bow thy heavens; bend them aside like a curtain,  Psalms 104:2 , to make way for thy descent.  The same as "rend the heavens,"  Isaiah 64:1 .

title: Psalms 144:7
text: Strange children; people of foreign nations.

title: Psalms 144:8
text:
Vanity; words destitute of righteousness and truth. 
 
  A right hand of falsehood; whose oaths, made by raising the right hand, and pledges made by striking the hand with another, are false.

title: Psalms 144:9
text: A new song; for new mercies received.

title: Psalms 144:12
text:
That our sons may be; in this and the remaining verses of this psalm he draws a beautiful picture of a peaceful and well-ordered state, such as Israel shall be when God has granted to David its king deliverance from all his foes. 
 
  Grown up; grown up strong and vigorous. 
 
The end which rulers should propose to themselves in all their undertakings, is the good of the people whom God has committed to their care.  No victory is worth gaining that has not this for its object and result.

title: Psalms 144:14
text:
Breaking in; of the enemy. 
 
  Going out; into captivity. 
 
  Complaining; literally, cry, that is, of distress. 
 
The true glory of a nation is to be measured, not by its outward conquests, but by it inward peace and prosperity.  The proper business of "kings," and of "all that are in authority," is to take care that their people "may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty."   I Timothy 2:2

title: Psalms 144:15
text: There is but one way for nations to be prosperous and happy; that way is, to acknowledge and obey God.

title: Psalms 145:1
text: It is the nature of holy communion with God to fill the soul with a sweet and comforting assurance that God shall be its portion for ever. Thus the Old Testament believers anticipated the clearer revelation of "life and immortality" which Christ made in the gospel.

title: Psalms 145:4
text: Our lips will soon be silent in death, but the work of praising God on earth will not cease with us.  It will be perpetuated from generation to generation, and will increase more and more, till it fills the whole earth as the waters cover the sea.

title: Psalms 145:10
text: All God's works praise him; but it is the prerogative of rational beings alone to bless him.

title: Psalms 145:16
text: God, who satisfies the desire of every living thing, is abundantly able to provide for all the wants of his children.  He invites them to put unlimited trust in himself, and he never disppoints their confidence.

title: Psalms 145:21
text: The true friend of God wishes to have all the world join him in praising His holy name; and so far as God gives him the opportunity, he will labor to bring all the world to do so.  This is the true missionary spirit, having its foundation in love.

title: Psalms 146:4
text: His thoughts perish; his plans and purposes are cut off by his death.

title: Psalms 146:5
text: The mightiest earthly patrons often fail us in the time of our greatest need; but they who put their trust in God, have a friend who will never disappoint their confidence.  All the resources of heaven and earth are at his disposal, and he will provide for the wants of his servants.

title: Psalms 146:9
text:
The strangers--the fatherless and widow; these three classes of persons are mentioned together because they are peculiarly exposed to injury, and are therefore the special objects of God's care. 
 
The poor, afflicted, and defenceless are the objects of God's special regard.  Herein we ought to imitate our heavenly Father.

title: Psalms 147:1
text: When our hearts are right, there is no employment so pleasant as praising God.  That men so generally neglect this most excellent service, is a proof of their exceeding wickedness.

title: Psalms 147:2
text: Though the Lord may suffer his people to be for a time persecuted and scattered, he will gather them together again and comfort them.

title: Psalms 147:3
text: The afflicted can always find in God a gracious and almighty Comforter.

title: Psalms 147:4
text:
Telleth; counteth. 
 
He who gives names to all the stars will not overlook any of his servants.

title: Psalms 147:9
text: The bounty of God provides for the beasts and the young ravens; how much more for his own children.

title: Psalms 147:10
text:
The strength of the horse; the war-horse. 
 
  The legs of a man; the strong and active legs of the warrior. Jehovah delights not in military forces, whether of cavalry or foot, because he has no need of their help.  Compare  Psalms 33:16-17 , which may serve as a commentary on this verse.

title: Psalms 147:11
text: Outward pomp and power are vian in the sight of God; he looks to the state of the heart.

title: Psalms 147:13
text: The bars of thy gates; by which they are defended against the assaults of enemies.

title: Psalms 147:15
text: His word runneth very swiftly; God's word is a swift messenger sent forth to the elements, and the commands which it bears to them from God, they execute immediately.

title: Psalms 147:17
text:
Ice; hailstones. 
 
  Like morsels; in bits, or small pieces, like morsels of food.

title: Psalms 147:18
text:
And melteth them; the snow, frost, and ice. 
 
  His wind; the warm south wind, which melts the ice, and causes it to flow off in streams.

title: Psalms 147:20
text:
They have not known them; that is, the other nations of the earth. 
 
The greatest blessing which God can confer on any nation is a knowledge of himself.

title: Psalms 148:1
text:
In the heights; the heavenly heights. 
 
To those who love God and live in habitual communion with him, every part of creation is full of his glory, and they see, with holy admiration and gladness, his wisdom, power, and goodness, in all the operations of nature.  But of all his works, none are so precious to them, and so full of grace and truth, as his dealings with his own children--"a people near unto him."

title: Psalms 148:4
text:
Ye heavens of heavens; the highest heavens. 
 
  Ye waters that be above the heavens; the same as the waters "above the firmament,"  Genesis 1:7 .

title: Psalms 148:6
text: Shall not pass; pass away, be abolished.

title: Psalms 148:7
text: Dragons; large sea-animals.

title: Psalms 148:8
text: Fire; lightning.

title: Psalms 148:14
text:
The horn of his people; horn is here a symbol for strength. 
 
  The praise of all his saints; supply from the preceding clause, "he exalteth."  To exalt the praise of his saints, is to give them still higher reasons for praising him. 
 
  A people near unto him; whom he has taken into peculiar relations to himself.

title: Psalms 149:2
text:
In him that made him; God made Israel, not only as all men are his creatures, but also as "a people near unto him." 
 
"The Israel of God" have for their King one to whom all power is given in heaven and in earth.  Under his government they are always safe, and have always abundant reason for rejoicing.

title: Psalms 149:3
text: In the dance--with the timbrel and harp; with sacred songs, accompanied, after the manner of the Hebrews, with musical instruments and dancing.

title: Psalms 149:4
text:
Beautify; adorn.  Salvation is here compared to a beauteous robe.  Isaiah 61:10  
 
The meek, who are conscious of their own weakness and unworthiness, and quietly commit their cause to God, always find that salvation of which the proud and self-sufficient, who rely on themselves, are sure to fail.

title: Psalms 149:5
text: Upon their beds; a place for pious meditation.   Psalms 63:6

title: Psalms 149:6
text: And a two-edged sword in their hand; when God's church had, by his appointment, a national form, conflicts sword in hand with surrounding enemies were a part of the duty of his people.  So when the Jews were rebuilding the walls of Jerusalem under Nehemiah, "the builders, every one had his sword girded by his side, and so builded."   Nehemiah 4:18

title: Psalms 149:9
text:
Written; appointed by God. 
 
  This honor; the honor of accomplishing the will of God upon his enemies. 
 
The greatest honor which a man can receive, is to be employed by God as an instrument of advancing his cause in the world.  "This honor have all his saints," each in his proper station, and according to the measure of the gifts bestowed upon him by God.

title: Psalms 150:1
text:
In his sanctuary; his earthly abode. 
 
  In the firmament of his power; his heavenly abode.  The whole family of God, in heaven and on earth, is here called upon to praise him. 
 
Amid the varied experience of God's servants recorded in the Psalms, their sufferings hold a conspicuous place.  But the book ends with songs of praise.  Such shall be the final issue of all the trials through which his earthly church is passing.  The Lord shall "extend peace to her like a river, and the glory of the Gentiles like a flowing stream;" and all her sons and daughters shall shout "as the voice of many waters, and as the voice of mighty thunderings, saying, Alleluia, for the Lord God omnipotent reigneth."  Such also shall be the history of individual believers.  Their tears and groans and prayers shall end in everlasting gladness.  God shall bring them home, each at the appointed time, to the heavenly Zion, "with songs and everlasting joy upon their heads: they shall obtain joy and gladness, and sorrow and sighing shall flee away."

title: Proverbs 1:2
text:
vv 2-4. 
 
  To know--to perceive--to receive; written that those who read them may know, perceive, and receive. 
 
  To give; written that they may give. 
 
  Wisdom--instruction, etc.; these are all different terms for describing true wisdom and righteousness, which consist in knowing and doing the will of God, and can never be separated. 
 
  To receive--justice, and judgment, and equity; to learn in what they consist, and to conform our life to them. 
 
  Subtilty--discretion; a quick discernment between what is wise and foolish.

title: Proverbs 1:5
text:
A wise man--a man of understanding; one who understands the worth of knowledge. 
 
  Shall attain; by hearing and learning. 
 
They who have wisdom understand the worth of knowledge, and earnestly seek it; but fools despise all instruction.

title: Proverbs 1:6
text: Dark sayings; sayings expressed in an enigmatical or obscure way, and requiring study to understand their meaning.

title: Proverbs 1:7
text:
The beginning of knowledge; lying at its foundation. 
 
  Fools; who have no fear of God. 
 
They who would be truly wise must begin by devoting themselves to God's service, and making his word the rule of their life.

title: Proverbs 1:9
text:
Chains about thy neck; worn as badges of honor.  Chains of gold were common as decorations of princes.   Genesis 41:42 Daniel 5:29  
 
Reverence for parental instruction in the child makes the man prosperous and honored.

title: Proverbs 1:10
text: They who choose the wicked for their companions become like them in character and end.

title: Proverbs 1:17
text:
vv 17-18. 
 
  Surely in vain the net is spread; the fowler does not expect a bird to be caught in a snare which he sees; but these sinners, and all who go with them, are spreading a net for their own souls.  The young should imitate the prudence of the birds in avoiding it.

title: Proverbs 1:19
text:
So are the ways; such is the issue to which they lead. 
 
  Greedy of gain; unlawfully desires gain, and seeks it by unlawful means. 
 
  Taketh away the life; by leading them into a snare.   Proverbs 1:18  
 
Unrighteous gain has destroyed millions; but has never made one man permanently prosperous and happy.

title: Proverbs 1:20
text:
Wisdom; the wisdom of God addressing men.  It includes all the revelations of himself which God has made to men.  And since these are all made through Christ, who spoke before his advent by the prophets, and afterwards by the apostles, we may say that wisdom speaks here as the eternal Word, who is the only revealer of God to men. Joh 1.18 
 
God urges upon men his lessons of heavenly wisdom in so many ways, that none can remain ignorant of them but those who obstinately refuse to hear.

title: Proverbs 1:21
text: Chief place of concourse--the gates--the city; she cries in the most public and frequented places.

title: Proverbs 1:23
text: I will pour out my spirit unto you; she speaks in God's name, and her spirit is God's Spirit.  Compare  Luke 11:49 .

title: Proverbs 1:24
text: Stretched out my hand; the gesture of earnest entreaty.

title: Proverbs 1:28
text: There is a point in rebellion against God and neglect of his warnings, beyond which the sinner's destruction is certain and irremediable.

title: Proverbs 1:31
text:
The fruit of their own way; terror and destruction, the proper recompense of setting at naught the counsels of wisdom. 
 
The sinner is responsible for his own ruin.  The destruction which comes upon him is the proper result of his perverseness in refusing to hear and obey God.

title: Proverbs 2:1
text: Hide; as a precious possession.

title: Proverbs 2:2
text: Incline thine ear unto wisdom; listen to her voice.

title: Proverbs 2:4
text: No man can expect to find the true knowledge of God and eternal life who does not seek them with supreme desire, and hold himself ready to part with every thing for their sake.

title: Proverbs 2:5
text:
Understand the fear of the Lord; by duly seeking, thou shalt know it, and appropriate it to thyself as a heavenly treasure.  This includes the comprehension of its nature, and the experience of the blessedness and safety which it gives. 
 
God gives true wisdom to all who ask it of him in sincerity.

title: Proverbs 2:6
text: Giveth wisdom; to all who thus earnestly seek it.

title: Proverbs 2:11
text: The only effectual safeguard from the ways of sin and ruin is the knowledge and fear of God.

title: Proverbs 2:12
text: Froward things; perverse things, contrary "to righteousness, and judgment, and equity."

title: Proverbs 2:16
text: Strange woman--stranger; adulterous woman.

title: Proverbs 2:17
text:
The guide of her youth; husband of her youth. 
 
  Covenant of her God; the marriage covenant, of which God is the witness, and to which he requires fidelity.

title: Proverbs 2:18
text:
Inclineth; sinketh down with her and all who frequent it. 
 
  Death; utter ruin, here and hereafter.

title: Proverbs 2:19
text:
Neither take they hold of the paths of life; they cannot regain the paths of life, because they have sunk down with her to the dead. 
 
Impurity in all its forms has a deadly influence upon both body and soul.  The house of the strange woman has been in all ages the highway to hell.

title: Proverbs 2:20
text: This verse is immediately connected with  Proverbs 21:10-11 .

title: Proverbs 2:22
text:
Cut off; suddenly and prematurely.   Psalms 55:23  
 
The violent destruction of the wicked in this world is an earnest of the everlasting destruction of their souls in the world to come.

title: Proverbs 3:2
text: A prosperous and happy life is the reward of obeying God's commandments.

title: Proverbs 3:3
text:
Mercy and truth; these include all true goodness. 
 
  Bind them about thy neck; as the noblest ornament. 
 
  Write them upon the table of thy heart; that they may always remain there.

title: Proverbs 3:4
text:
In the sight of God and man; thy good understanding shall be manifest to God and man, and gain for thee their favor. 
 
The possession of true wisdom secures the premanent favor of God and all good men.

title: Proverbs 3:6
text:
Acknowledge him; feel thy dependence upon him and seek his direction. 
 
They who feel their need of God's protection and guidance, and humbly commit themselves to him in the way of duty, shall not be left to perplexity or error.  He will mark out their path for them, and make them truly prosperous and useful.

title: Proverbs 3:8
text:
Navel--bones; put for the whole body. 
 
  Marrow to thy bones; making them strong and vigorous.  Bodily health is here put for prosperity of every kind, temporal and spiritual. 
 
True health of soul and body lies in fearing God and departing from evil.

title: Proverbs 3:9
text:
Honor the Lord with thy substance; by giving to his service the due portion. 
 
  First-fruits; which the Israelites were required to offer to God.  Exodus 23:19 Leviticus 2:12 Leviticus 19:23-24 Deuteronomy 18:4  
 
When we honor God with our property, he will bless us in the possession and use of it.

title: Proverbs 3:12
text: God chastens his children because he loves them, and purposes to make them meet for eternal glory.   Hebrews 12:5-14

title: Proverbs 3:14
text: The merchandise of it; the gaining of it by traffic.  Wisdom is here regarded as a precious treasure, to be gained at whatever cost. Compare  Matthew 13:44-46 .

title: Proverbs 3:15
text: The smallest measure of true wisdom is better than all the kingdoms of the world and the glory of them; for it makes us blessed here, and prepares us for eternal blessedness hereafter.

title: Proverbs 3:16
text: Her right hand--her left hand; she dispenses blessings to her followers from both hands.

title: Proverbs 3:18
text: A tree of life; she gives life to them that receive her instruction.

title: Proverbs 3:19
text: Hath founded--the heavens; the crowning praise of wisdom: by her God hath created the world.

title: Proverbs 3:20
text:
Depths; subterranean abysses. 
 
  Broken up; made to gush forth.  Some understand these words of the division of the great deep, into the waters under the firmament, and the waters above the firmament.   Genesis 1:7

title: Proverbs 3:25
text:
Be not afraid; that is, when thou keepest sound wisdom and discretion.   Proverbs 3:21  
 
  Sudden fear; sudden destruction from God, which overwhelms the wicked with fear. 
 
It is not only the privilege, but the duty of the righteous to be composed and free from fear amidst those judgments which destroy God's enemies.   Psalms 46:1-3 Habakkuk 3:10-19

title: Proverbs 3:27
text: All who need our help have a claim upon us from God for it.  We should give it promptly and cheerfully, and thank him for the opportunity.

title: Proverbs 3:31
text: The oppressor; because of his present success in sinful practices.

title: Proverbs 3:32
text: Secret; intimate friendship.

title: Proverbs 3:33
text: They who provide for their families wealth and power by wicked practices, lay up for them a curse instead of a blessing.  God's favor bestowed upon the children of the righteous is better than houses full of silver and gold.

title: Proverbs 3:34
text: It is the unchangeable purpose of God to abase the proud and exalt the humble; and he is abundantly able to accomplish it in respect to nations, families, and individuals.

title: Proverbs 3:35
text: Shame shall be the promotion of fools; while the wise are promoted to true glory, the only promotion of fools shall be shame; that is, they shall have shame instead of glory.

title: Proverbs 4:3
text:
My father's son; in an emphatic sense, a son tenderly beloved and cherished. 
 
  Only beloved; loved like an only son, that is, very tenderly; for Solomon was not literally the only son of his mother. See 1Ch 3.5.

title: Proverbs 4:4
text:
He taught me also; Solomon commends his instructions to the young as those which he had received from his father in childhood, and obedience to which had made him prosperous and honored. 
 
They who, by precept and example, teach their children to value heavenly wisdom above all earthly possessions, may hope to see them made by God's grace useful and honorable, and the instructors of the following generation.

title: Proverbs 4:7
text:
With all thy getting get understanding; either, Among all thy other acquisitions be sure to get wisdom first; or better thus: Employ all thy worldly gain to get wisdom: part with it all, if need be, for her sake.   Matthew 13:44-46  
 
That men so universally prefer wealth to wisdom, shows the blindness of the natural heart; but they whom God's Spirit has enlightened, understand well that the knowledge of the truth is better than all riches.

title: Proverbs 4:12
text: Shall not be straitened; thou shalt have a wide and plain path in which thou canst go safely.   Psalms 18:36

title: Proverbs 4:15
text: Avoid it--pass away; the accumulation of admonitions shows the extreme danger of the way.

title: Proverbs 4:16
text: Sin has a dreadful power to perpetuate itself.  They who enter upon a course of transgression proceed from bad to worse, till their life becomes one continuous series of sins.

title: Proverbs 4:18
text:
The shining light; of the morning sun. 
 
  Perfect day; noon.  Light is here the emblem of knowledge, holiness, and happiness. 
 
How glorious is the just man's course.  In this life he is increasing in knowledge, holiness, and usefulness; and he has before him an eternity of light and bliss.  "The ungodly are not so."  They walk in darkness and self-delusion, and stumble unawares into perdition.

title: Proverbs 4:19
text: Know not at what they stumble; they cannot see the stumbling-blocks that lie in their way, and they fall over them unawares.

title: Proverbs 4:23
text:
Issues; fountains: when the heart is well kept, and stored with heavenly wisdom, it sends forth life-giving streams. 
 
If men bestowed upon their hearts that care which they give to their estates, they would be rewarded with peace and prosperity, instead of disappointment and consuming anxiety.

title: Proverbs 4:25
text:
Right on--straight before thee; as one looks who is intent upon pursuing a straight path, the path of God's commandments. 
 
Straightforward integrity lies at the foundation of all true excellence and permanent success.  When men rely on crooked artifices, they and their plans will in the end be carried headlong.

title: Proverbs 4:26
text: They who earnestly and prayerfully ponder their path, shall be guided in the right way; but inconsiderateness always ends in shame and misery.

title: Proverbs 5:2
text: Thy lips; when the heart is stored with knowledge it dwells also on the lips, and is communicated to others.

title: Proverbs 5:4
text:
Her end; the final end of yielding to her enticements. 
 
When we are tempted to sinful indulgence, we should consider well its consequences.  It is a sad exchange to give property, health, character, peace of conscience, the favor of God, and everlasting life, for a little momentary pleasure.

title: Proverbs 5:5
text: Go down to death--take hold on hell; compare  Proverbs 2:18 .

title: Proverbs 5:6
text: Movable; changeable; she cunningly alters her demeanor so as to retain her hold on those whom she has enticed.  Or the verse may be rendered thus: Lest she should ponder the path of life, her ways wander, she knows not where.  Compare  Proverbs 4:19 .

title: Proverbs 5:8
text: The only safety of the young lies in avoiding the beginnings of impurity in word, thought, and deed, and all solicitations thereto.  He who needlessly places himself in the way of temptation, is in imminent danger of falling.  And when he once yields, he gives sinful passion the mastery over himself, and his course is rapidly downward, till it ends in the destruction of soul, body, and estate.

title: Proverbs 5:9
text:
Honor--years; the prime and vigor of thy life. 
 
  Others--the cruel; these words probably refer to the husband of the adulteress, who had a right, by the Levitical law, to demand the death of the offender, but might content himself with the exaction of heavy fines and hard servitude.

title: Proverbs 5:10
text:
vv 10-11. 
 
  Filled with thy wealth--are consumed; these words refer to all the ways in which illicit indulgence wastes the estate of the transgressor, destroys his health and character, and exposes him to ignominious penalties.

title: Proverbs 5:12
text: They who will not listen in youth to the admonitions of wisdom, must pay a dreadful penalty for their heedlessness in old age.

title: Proverbs 5:14
text: The congregation and assembly; the public assembly before which the adulterer was arraigned.

title: Proverbs 5:15
text:
Drink waters; be content with the wife of thy youth. 
 
God has ordained marriage for the holiness, comfort, and purity of the human family; and all who in any way dishonor it, by precept or example, are among the worst enemies of mankind.   Ephesians 5:5-6 Hebrews 13:4

title: Proverbs 5:16
text: Fountains--rivers of waters; flowing from the well mentioned in the preceding verse.  These may denote either the pure enjoyment which he has in her society, or their mutual offspring.

title: Proverbs 5:21
text: We can neither conceal from God any crime, nor prevent his exposing and punishing it.  As certainly as he reigns in heaven, every iniquity, unless it be repented of and forgiven through the blood of Christ, will take the sinner in its fatal cords, and hold him fast bound to all eternity.

title: Proverbs 6:1
text:
Stricken thy hand; it was thus that a person pledged himself to be responsible for the debt of another. 
 
He who easily allows himself to become surety for others, is likely to become the prey of weak or designing men, who make false representations of their circumstances.  To make suretyship lawful and proper, we must be fully able to meet the sum pledged without injury to others.

title: Proverbs 6:3
text: Into the hand of thy friend; into his power.

title: Proverbs 6:11
text:
One that travelleth; a traveller that comes unexpectedly, as an enemy or assailant. 
 
Indolent procrastination is the parent of poverty and misery in things temporal and spiritual.  The divine law is, that wealth of every kind comes by toil.

title: Proverbs 6:12
text:
vv 12-15. 
 
These verses describe a cunning deceiver, who accomplishes his mischievous plans by hidden artifices. 
 
  Winketh--speaketh--teacheth; the secret signs which he gives to his accomplices.

title: Proverbs 6:15
text: The man who relies for success upon crooked and deceitful practices, is alike odious to God and man, and his end will be remediless ruin.

title: Proverbs 6:16
text:
Six things--yea, seven; it is a frequent custom of the Hebrew writers, in making enumerations, to begin with one less than the whole number.  Job 5:19 Proverbs 30:18 Proverbs 30:20 Proverbs 30:29 Ecclesiastes 11:2 Amos 1:3 Amos 1:6 Amos 1:9 Amos 1:11 Amos 1:13 Amos 2:1 Amos 2:4 Amos 2:6  
 
God estimates men, not from their outward circumstances, but from their character.  All whose hearts and lives are defiled with wicked practices are abominable in his sight, however high their reputation among men.

title: Proverbs 6:18
text: Imaginations; plots, plans of mischief.

title: Proverbs 6:23
text: Are the way of life; they guide men into the way of life.

title: Proverbs 6:27
text: The penalty of sin is as certain as the laws of nature, and far more terrible in its power.  The youth who enters upon a course of impurity, throws himself into a consuming fire, which will destroy both soul and body.

title: Proverbs 6:30
text: Despise; generally interpreted to mean, to overlook, to connive at. But we may retain the ordinary meaning of the word.  Though men feel the necessity of punishing a thief who has stolen to satisfy his hunger, yet they do not look upon him with such contempt and abhorrence as upon the adulterer.

title: Proverbs 6:32
text: He that doeth it destroyeth his own soul; more literally, The destroyer of his own soul, he will do it; as much as to say, The man who is bent on ruining himself, he will commit this sin.

title: Proverbs 6:34
text: The rage of a man; in an emphatic sense, jealousy excites his fiercest rage.

title: Proverbs 7:1
text: The way of all seducers is to inflame the imagination of the young with glowing representatives of the pleasures of sinful indulgence, while they carefully keep out of view its guilt and misery, and flatter them with the hope of impunity.  All books, discourses, and representations of every kind, that follow the method of this adulteress, are justly to be regarded as her accomplices in the work of corruption and ruin; and their influence in a community is more to be dreaded than "the pestilence that walketh in darkness."  Let all the young who hope to enjoy in this life, comfort, honor, and usefulness, and God's favor in the life to come, keep themselves at the greatest distance from unchaste solicitations of every kind, and labor to maintain purity, in thought, speech, and behavior.

title: Proverbs 7:14
text: Peace-offerings; offered, as she pretends, in fulfilment of her vows.  A portion only of the peace-offering was burned upon the altar. Upon the rest, the offerer and his friends feasted.  She means, that she has a sumptuous feast provided in her house, and has come out to seek him to share it with her.

title: Proverbs 7:26
text: Wounded; mortally wounded, as on the field of battle.

title: Proverbs 8:1
text:
In striking contrast with the strange woman described in the preceding chapter, heavenly Wisdom now addresses men, and invites them to receive at her hand the richest blessings.  It is the essential Wisdom of God, which dwelt with him from eternity, or, the Word, by whom his wisdom is manifested, that speaks.  See note on  Proverbs 1:20 . 
 
God is exceedingly earnest in his endeavors to recall men from sin and folly to heavenly wisdom.  His calls to them are so many, so loud, and so varied, that none can fail to hear but those who wilfully neglect them.

title: Proverbs 8:2
text:
vv 2-3. 
 
  In the top of high places--at the coming in at the doors; in all the most public and frequented places. She continually forces herself upon men's attention.

title: Proverbs 8:8
text: The holy Scriptures, in which the wisdom of God addresses men, contain the revelation of truth unmixed with error; and all who commit themselves to their guidance shall be led in the ways of peace, knowledge, holiness, and eternal life.

title: Proverbs 8:9
text:
Plain to him that understandeth; the words of wisdom are all right and plain of apprehension; but it requires an understanding heart to receive them.  Fools derive no benefit from them.  Compare our Saviour's words, "Wisdom is justified of all her children."  Luke 7:35  
 
The plainest and best instructions are of no avail unless there be an understanding heart to receive them.  The doctrine of Christ was an offence to the scribes and Pharisees; but all who had an humble and obedient spirit received it gladly.

title: Proverbs 8:12
text: Witty inventions; wise counsels.

title: Proverbs 8:15
text:
vv 15-16. 
 
  By me kings reign--princes rule; she commends herself to men as the counsellor and guide of all rulers.

title: Proverbs 8:17
text: God has a tender love for all who earnestly seek the truth; and if they persevere, his grace will make them successful.

title: Proverbs 8:18
text:
vv 18-21. 
 
  Riches and honor are with me--fill their treasures; she further commends herself as the only source of true riches and righteousness.

title: Proverbs 8:21
text: Wisdom is the most excellent of all possessions, having the promise of this life and that which is to come.

title: Proverbs 8:22
text:
The Lord possessed me; the crowning commendation of wisdom: she is the eternal companion of God, his delight, rejoicing always before him, and present at all his works. 
 
In all God's revelations eternal wisdom addresses men, but in the Lord Jesus Christ, who is the Word made flesh, he has given us a full manifestation of that infinite and uncreated wisdom which he possessed "from everlasting, from the beginning, or ever the earth was."  To hear and obey Christ, is to receive heavenly wisdom, and with her, eternal life.

title: Proverbs 8:26
text: The highest part of the dust; the mountain tops; or, The chief part of the dust.

title: Proverbs 8:27
text: Set a compass; formed the circular vault of heaven, or exactly formed all parts of the universe.

title: Proverbs 8:30
text:
vv 30-31. 
 
  Then I was by him--delights were with the sons of men; see note on  Proverbs 1:20 .

title: Proverbs 8:31
text: The love of God for men equals his almighty power to do them good.  He earnestly desires that they should listen to his voice, that he may make them most blessed for ever.

title: Proverbs 8:34
text: My gates--posts of my doors; waiting at her royal palace to receive instruction.  Compare  Proverbs 9:1 .

title: Proverbs 9:1
text:
Her seven pillars; which adorn her palace and give it stability. 
 
They who listen to the wisdom of God, shall receive from her an abundance of all good things; but they who refuse to hear her voice, must perish in the greatness of their folly.

title: Proverbs 9:2
text: Killed her beasts--mingled her wine; that is, she has prepared a sumptuous feast.  Compare  Isaiah 25:6 Isaiah 55:1-2 Matthew 22:4 .

title: Proverbs 9:4
text: The beginning of wisdom is to know our ignorance, and come to God for knowledge.

title: Proverbs 9:7
text:
vv 7-9. 
 
  He that reproveth a scorner--increase in learning; wisdom continues her address to men, reminding them that it is only the wise who will be benefited by her calls, while scorners and wicked men will reject them. This is not inconsistent with  Proverbs 9:4 , in which she addresses "the simple," and "him that wanteth understanding;" for such may be conscious of their ignorance, and this is the beginning of true wisdom. 
 
They who most need instruction are least ready to receive it; because they understand not their own folly, and therefore hate and despise reproof.

title: Proverbs 9:9
text: One of the blessed qualities of true wisdom is, that a little of it prepares men to seek and obtain more.   Matthew 13:12 s

title: Proverbs 9:10
text:
The Holy; God. 
 
The foundation of all true wisdom is the knowledge and fear of God.  A wicked heart separates men from God, and keeps them in darkness and self-delusion.

title: Proverbs 9:12
text:
Wise for thyself--thou alone shalt bear it; in an emphatic sense. Though our wisdom and folly affect others, the principal harvest from them must be reaped by ourselves. 
 
Personal responsibility is always recognized in God's moral government. The counsels of the good cannot benefit us, nor the seductions of the wicked injure us, without our own free consent.  Our wisdom and folly are our own, and we must reap their fruits here and hereafter.

title: Proverbs 9:13
text: A foolish woman; the foolish woman described in the preceding chapters.

title: Proverbs 9:15
text: Right on their ways; who are attending to their lawful employments.

title: Proverbs 9:17
text:
Stolen waters--bread eaten in secret; unlawful pleasures. 
 
Unlawful pleasures promise much good, but their end is bitterness and death.

title: Proverbs 9:18
text: The dead are there; in her house.  Those who have entered it are as good as dead, because "none that go unto her return again, neither take they hold of the paths of life."   Proverbs 2:19

title: Proverbs 10:1
text:
The Proverbs of Solomon; here begins the second division of this book, extending the sixteenth verse of the twenty-second chapter. 
 
  A wise son; in this proverb, as in many of the following, the two clauses must be mutually supplied, each from the other, thus: A wise son maketh glad both father and mother; but a foolish son is the heaviness of both. 
 
Since the happiness or misery of parents depends so much upon the character and conduct of their children, this should be an incitement to them diligently to train them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.

title: Proverbs 10:2
text:
Treasures of wickedness; wealth wrongfully gotten. 
 
  Delivereth from death; from violent and premature death, which is often threatened as the punishment of the wicked,  Proverbs 10:27 .  The words also include the promise of deliverance from eternal death, of which all less deliverances are but pledges and earnests. 
 
The curse of God rests upon all unrighteous gain.  It can confer upon its owners no true happiness in this world, and it exposes them to his everlasting displeasure in the world to come.

title: Proverbs 10:4
text: The general law of God's moral government is, industry and plenty, poverty and want.

title: Proverbs 10:5
text: A principal part of wisdom lies in discerning and improving passing opportunities.

title: Proverbs 10:6
text: Covereth the mouth of the wicked; that is, his mouth is filled with violence, by which he brings upon himself the curses of his fellow-men.

title: Proverbs 10:7
text: A permanent good mane can be gained only by righteousness.

title: Proverbs 10:8
text:
Will receive commandments--shall fall; here, as often in these proverbs, the first clause gives the character of a wise man; the second, the end of a fool.  Fill out the two clauses thus: The wise in heart will receive commandments, therefore he shall stand firm; but a prating fool will not hear advice, therefore he shall fall. 
 
He who is more ready to talk than to take advice is near destruction.

title: Proverbs 10:9
text:
Shall be known; exposed and punished. 
 
All crooked practices will in the end be detected and punished.

title: Proverbs 10:10
text: Winketh with the eye; a sign of malicious cunning.

title: Proverbs 10:12
text: Love is the great principle of harmony; it disposes men to cover the faults of their neighbors, and deal leniently with them.

title: Proverbs 10:13
text: He who will not be corrected by God's word must feel his rod.

title: Proverbs 10:14
text:
Lay up knowledge; which keeps them from speaking unadvisedly. 
 
  Near destruction; constantly exposes them to destruction.

title: Proverbs 10:15
text: Destruction of the poor; that which exposes them to much injury from wicked men.  This is not inconsistent with the promise, that God will protect the pious poor who put their trust in him.

title: Proverbs 10:17
text: The unteachable are in the road to certain ruin.

title: Proverbs 10:19
text: Wisdom is shown not less in what we forbear to utter, than in what we say.

title: Proverbs 10:20
text:
As choice silver; from the rich treasury of his heart he brings forth words that are as choice silver. 
 
  Heart--is little worth; and therefore his words also are destitute of worth.

title: Proverbs 10:22
text: True prosperity flows from God's presence and blessing.  Without this all apparent success will but multiply our troubles.

title: Proverbs 10:23
text: Hath wisdom; which leads him to abhor mischief.

title: Proverbs 10:24
text: Under the righteous government of God, the highest hopes of the righteous and the worst fears of the wicked shall be more than realized.

title: Proverbs 10:25
text: Is an everlasting foundation; his blessedness rests on the immovable foundation of God's promises.   Psalms 15:5

title: Proverbs 10:29
text: The way of the Lord; either God's way of acting, or the way which he prescribes to men.  In the former sense the meaning will be, that God's providence protects the upright; in the latter, that obedience to God secures his protection.

title: Proverbs 10:30
text: Inhabit the earth; in its original meaning, dwell securely in the promised land.   Exodus 20:12   But the words contain a general promise of peace and prosperity to the righteous.  See note to  Psalms 37:11 .

title: Proverbs 10:31
text: Bringeth forth wisdom--shall be cut out; fill out the two clauses thus: bringeth forth wisdom, and therefore is acceptable to God and man; speaketh folly, and therefore shall be cut out.  See note to  Proverbs 10:8 .

title: Proverbs 11:1
text: Dishonest practices in trade are so prevalent, that multitudes have but a feeble apprehension of their great wickedness.  But God regards them all with abhorrence; and unless repented of and forsaken, they will bring upon men his righteous indignation in this world, and will exclude them from heaven.

title: Proverbs 11:2
text: A haughty spirit is a sure precursor of an ignominious fall; but humility is the highway to permanent honor.

title: Proverbs 11:3
text: Integrity is a sure guide; it leads men by a safe path, and brings them out in a safe place.

title: Proverbs 11:4
text: In the day of wrath; of God's wrath.

title: Proverbs 11:5
text: Shall direct his way; shall make his way plain, so that he shall have no occasion of stumbling.

title: Proverbs 11:8
text: Cometh in his stead; cometh into trouble in his place.   Luke 16:25

title: Proverbs 11:9
text: All slanderers are hypocrites; under the pretence of rebuking their neighbor's faults, they are gratifying their own envy and malice.

title: Proverbs 11:11
text: Righteous men are the best defence of a city, and wicked men its most imminent peril.

title: Proverbs 11:12
text:
Despiseth his neighbor; not only feels contempt in his heart, but expresses it in his words and actions. 
 
True self-knowledge makes us forbearing in speaking of the faults of others.  The man who busies himself in publishing his neighbor's failings, thereby proclaims his own folly.

title: Proverbs 11:14
text: When God would destroy a nation, he takes away its wise counsellors, and gives it up to the control of wicked and weak men.

title: Proverbs 11:16
text:
A gracious woman; literally, a woman of grace, that is, a winning and attractive woman.  Her attractiveness includes mental as well as bodily accomplishments.  She is a woman of discretion, for "a fair woman without discertion" does not retain her honor;  Proverbs 11:22 . 
 
  Retaineth; gains and keeps.  There is here a tacit comparison: As strong men gain riches, so a gracious woman gains honor.

title: Proverbs 11:17
text: The principal harvest of mercy and cruelty is reaped by those who exercise them.

title: Proverbs 11:18
text: A deceitful work; a work which deceives and disappoints his hopes.

title: Proverbs 11:21
text: Though hand join in hand; though every combination and effort to escape punishment be resorted to.

title: Proverbs 11:22
text:
In a swine's snout; that is, very much out of place. 
 
Beauty without discretion is a calamity instead of a blessing.

title: Proverbs 11:23
text:
Only good; in its issue.  His hopes of good are all realized. 
 
  Is wrath; ends in wrath.  Instead of the good for which he hoped, he receives wrath from God.

title: Proverbs 11:24
text:
Scattereth; distributes his wealth in deeds of kindness. 
 
True Christian liberality is the road to prosperity.  It secures God's blessing upon our gain, and makes it profitable to ourselves and to others.

title: Proverbs 11:26
text:
Withholdeth corn; hoards it up in time of famine, in order to sell it at a high price. 
 
The worst extortioner is he who takes advantage of a public calamity to fill his own coffers at the expense of the poor.

title: Proverbs 11:27
text:
