Seeketh good; occupies himself in doing good. 
 
  Procureth favor; from God and man.

title: Proverbs 11:29
text:
Troubleth his own house; involves his family in misery by his misconduct. 
 
  The wind; emptiness and disappointment.

title: Proverbs 11:30
text: Fruit of the righteous; the results which he produces.

title: Proverbs 11:31
text:
Recompensed; chastised for his sins.  The Greek version of the Seventy renders this verse thus: "If the righteous scarcely be saved, where shall the ungodly and the sinner appear?" which gives the same general sense, and is followed by,  I Peter 4:18 . 
 
The severity with which God punishes his offending children, is a solemn warning to the wicked of the awful destruction which awaits them.

title: Proverbs 12:1
text: True wisdom disposes men to seek instruction; and the want of wisdom leads them to hate reproof.

title: Proverbs 12:4
text:
A virtuous woman; a woman of worth, one who possesses both moral goodness and mental vigor. 
 
  She that maketh ashamed; by her baseness and worthlessness. 
 
  As rottenness in his bones; very painful and offensive.

title: Proverbs 12:6
text: Deliver them; from the wicked, who lie in wait for them.

title: Proverbs 12:8
text: Wisdom and folly will in the end find each its proper level.

title: Proverbs 12:9
text:
Despised, and hath a servant; occupying a humble station, yet living in a state of independence and comfort. 
 
None are more foolish and miserable than they who sacrifice comfort and independence to vain ostentation.  The affectation of wealth and rank makes men hypocritical and dishonest, and its end is ignominy and contempt.

title: Proverbs 12:10
text:
Regardeth the life; treats it kindly, and supplies it with needful food and rest. 
 
  Are cruel consist of cruelty; that is, in his heart cruelty takes the place of tender mercies. 
 
Kindness to animals is a characteristic of good men, as cruelty is of the wicked.

title: Proverbs 12:11
text:
Vain persons; as Abimelech,  Judges 9:4 , Absalom,  II Samuel 15:1 , and others, who promise their followers plenty without toil. 
 
The divine ordinance is, that he who would have bread must earn it by the sweat of his brow; and it cannot be set aside by any ingenuity of man.

title: Proverbs 12:12
text: The net of evil men; the net which evil men use, for the sake of the prey which it takes.

title: Proverbs 12:13
text: Shall come out of trouble; his upright words shall deliver him.

title: Proverbs 12:14
text: Fruit of his mouth; the result of his wise and prudent discourse.

title: Proverbs 12:15
text: The who most need counsel are often least ready to receive it.

title: Proverbs 12:16
text:
Presently; immediately.  He vents his indignation upon the spot in passionate words and deeds. 
 
  Covereth shame; passes by shameful treatment in silence. 
 
When a wise man receives an injury, he pauses and considers the matter well before he speaks.

title: Proverbs 12:17
text:
He that speaketh truth; the man of truthful character. 
 
  Showeth forth righteousness; makes truthful statements, such as are in accordance with righteousness.  The proverb shows the agreement between men's character and their testimony.

title: Proverbs 12:18
text:
Is health; heals instead of wounds. 
 
No wounds are more painful than those which the calumniator inflicts upon his neighbor's good name.  He is an object of just abhorrence to God and man; but blessed is the tongue that is employed in healing strife.

title: Proverbs 12:19
text: Falsehood and duplicity promise ready success; but in the end they overthrow all who employ them.

title: Proverbs 12:20
text: Imagine evil; devise mischievous plans.  It is implied that their mischievous plans bring them into trouble.  See note to  Proverbs 10:8 .

title: Proverbs 12:23
text:
Concealeth knowledge; does not vauntingly display himself, or publish all he knows. 
 
  Proclaimeth foolishness; they have nothing in their heart to exhibit but folly, and they proclaim it everywhere, as if it were true wisdom. 
 
They who have the least wisdom are often the most forward to express their opinion.

title: Proverbs 12:24
text: It is an ordinance of heaven which none can reverse, that the idle shall be subject to the industrious.

title: Proverbs 12:25
text: The best medicine for soul and body is inward composure and cheerfulness; and this it is the Christian's duty and privilege to maintain; for in the midst of all his troubles and sorrows his heavenly Father has always "a good word" for him.

title: Proverbs 12:27
text: That which he took in hunting; that is, he takes nothing in hunting to roast.

title: Proverbs 13:1
text: Scorner; a child who is "wise in his own eyes," and therefore despises his father's admonitions and counsels.

title: Proverbs 13:2
text:
The fruit of his mouth; his wise words. 
 
  Eat violence; be violently destroyed.

title: Proverbs 13:3
text:
Openeth wide his lips; utters all his thoughts inconsiderately. 
 
Our comfort and prosperity in this world, and our eternal welfare after death, are greatly dependent upon the use we make of the gift of speech.

title: Proverbs 13:4
text: All riches, spiritual and temporal, are the price of industry: they who will not toil for them must remain poor.

title: Proverbs 13:5
text: False and deceitful men generally come to shame in the present life, and their reward hereafter must be "shame and everlasting contempt."

title: Proverbs 13:6
text:
Keepeth him that is upright; is his guardian and guide. 
 
Righteousness is a sure guide.  She leads the soul to God and blessedness.  But sin flatters men only to reward them with disappointment and ruin.

title: Proverbs 13:7
text: Maketh himself rich--maketh himself poor; some understand these words of the affectation of wealth, or poverty; but they rather contrast with the vain show of wealth its opposite virtue, an humble and unostentatious spirit.

title: Proverbs 13:8
text:
Are his riches; he is often compelled to buy his life by giving up his riches to his oppressors. 
 
  Heareth not rebuke; his poverty exempts him from the threats and spoilations to which the rich are subjected.  This proverb is peculiarly applicable to the despotic governments of the East.

title: Proverbs 13:10
text:
Wisdom; to avoid contention. 
 
Pride is the root of all contentions.

title: Proverbs 13:11
text:
Vanity; dishonest practices of every kind. 
 
  Labor; honest industry. 
 
Valuable possessions are gained by labor.  They who seek wealth, place, or influence by cunning and dishonesty, will in the end be disappointed.

title: Proverbs 13:12
text: It is good to set our hearts on God's promises, and not on this world; for he will fulfil the highest desires of those who put their trust in him.

title: Proverbs 13:13
text: The word; of divine admonition.

title: Proverbs 13:14
text:
Law; instructions and counsels. 
 
  To depart; teaching men to depart.

title: Proverbs 13:15
text: Hard; bringing upon them misery and ruin.

title: Proverbs 13:17
text:
A wicked messenger; one unfaithful to him who sends him. 
 
  Health; gives prosperity and joy. 
 
He who has proved himself worthy of being trusted will be trusted again, and thus he will rise to honor and influence; but they who betray the confidence reposed in them must come to speedy ruin.

title: Proverbs 13:18
text: When we see an ignorant, self-conceited youth making light of God's words, and the counsels of his parents, we may know that he is on the road to a miserable and ignominious end.

title: Proverbs 13:19
text:
Desire; the holy desire of the good. 
 
  It is abomination to fools to depart from evil; evil is all their delight.  They have no holy desires whose accomplishment can make them blessed.

title: Proverbs 13:20
text: A great part of wisdom lies in the choice of our companions; for what they are, they will make us also.

title: Proverbs 13:21
text: Pursueth; as an avenger.

title: Proverbs 13:22
text:
To his children's children; which shall descend to them by God's blessing. 
 
  Is laid up for the just; God will take it from them and give it to the just. 
 
The best provision that a man can make for his family is to fear the Lord always, and to train them up in his fear.  An estate gotten by wickedness has the curse of God upon it, and cannot be expected to benefit those who inherit it.

title: Proverbs 13:23
text: Tillage of the poor--want of judgment; the poor man that tills the soil with patient industry shall have plenty of food; but he who despises honest labor, and seeks to live by unrighteous means, shall come to poverty and ruin.

title: Proverbs 13:24
text: Neglect of timely chastisement is cruelty to a child, for the want of early discipline ends in profligacy and misery.

title: Proverbs 14:1
text:
Buildeth her house; figuratively; she advances the welfare of her household by her good management. 
 
The capacity to manage well the affairs of her household the holy Scriptures uniformly represent as one of the chief ornaments of woman, and a principal part of her wisdom.  No outward accomplishments can save a wasteful and improvident woman from the charge of folly; she cannot be wise who does not understand the duties that peculiarly belong to her.

title: Proverbs 14:2
text:
Feareth the Lord-- despiseth him; uprightness and perverseness are here referred each to its true cause; the former to the fear of the Lord, the latter to contempt of his authority. 
 
The fear of God is the only sure foundation of an upright character.

title: Proverbs 14:3
text: A rod of pride; a rod to chastise his own pride.  Others explain it thus: an insolent scourge with which he smites his fellow-men.

title: Proverbs 14:4
text:
Clean; empty of fodder.  An empty crib implies an empty barn. 
 
  Much increase is by the strength of the ox; he requires a full crib for his nourishment.  But he gives back to his owner more than he receives. 
 
In religion, as well as in secular affairs, all outlays are wise that bring "much increase" to those who make them.

title: Proverbs 14:6
text:
Findeth it not; because he neither understands what it is, nor how to gain it. 
 
An humble and teachable spirit is an indispensable qualification for gaining true knowledge.

title: Proverbs 14:7
text: They who would be wise must avoid the company of the foolish.

title: Proverbs 14:8
text: The folly of fools is deceit; instead of occupying themselves with understanding their way, which is true wisdom, they are engrossed with plans of deceit, and this is their folly.

title: Proverbs 14:9
text:
Make a mock at sin; by which they incur God's wrath. 
 
  Favor; God's favor. 
 
There is no surer mark of folly than a disposition to make light of sin.  They who turn wickedness into a jest, will certainly practise it to their everlasting ruin.

title: Proverbs 14:10
text: His own bitterness--his joy; our joys and sorrows are our own, in an emphatic sense--matters of our own experience.

title: Proverbs 14:12
text: Self-conceit has a dreadfully blinding influence; it has led thousands to mistake the way to hell for the road to heaven.

title: Proverbs 14:13
text:
Laughter; the noisy mirth of the light-minded and vicious. 
 
The noisy mirth of the ungodly but poorly conceals a heart troubled with the consciousness of guilt, and the apprehension of wrath to come.

title: Proverbs 14:15
text: In this world of imposture and error, no man can walk safely who does not try the opinions which he hears by God's word, and receive or reject them accordingly.

title: Proverbs 14:16
text:
Feareth; God. 
 
  Rageth, and is confident; he is under the control of passion and self-conceit, and resents reproof.  Hence he rushes on headlong to ruin. 
 
He who will not consider the dangers and temptations that surround him, must soon be destroyed by them.

title: Proverbs 14:19
text:
Bow before the good; this proverb expresses the final issue of righteousness and wickedness, which is often foreshadowed in this life by God's providential dealings with men, as well as by the involuntary homage which conscience compels the wicked to pay to virtue. 
 
Since God is on the side of the righteous, they must in the end triumph over the wicked.

title: Proverbs 14:20
text: The false importance which men so universally attach to wealth is a sad proof of their depravity and folly.

title: Proverbs 14:21
text: Despiseth his neighbor; treats with neglect and contempt his poor neighbor who needs his services.

title: Proverbs 14:24
text:
Their riches; their ornament and honor; because they make a wise use of them. 
 
  Is folly; remains folly under all circumstances. Riches and honor are thrown away upon them.

title: Proverbs 14:25
text: Speaketh lies; by which he destroys souls.

title: Proverbs 14:29
text:
Exalteth folly; makes his folly conspicuous. 
 
The passionate man proclaims his own folly.

title: Proverbs 14:30
text:
A sound heart; a contented and tranquil heart, free from the disquietudes of envy. 
 
A cheerful and contented heart, free from pride and envy, is the best medicine for soul and body.

title: Proverbs 14:31
text: Reproacheth his Maker; God, who made the poor man and ordered his condition.

title: Proverbs 14:32
text: Hath hope in his death; hope respecting the life to come, resting on the continuance of God's favor.  These words show that believers under the Old Testament had a true hope of future blessedness.

title: Proverbs 14:33
text: That which is in the midst of fools; their boasted wisdom, which is only folly.

title: Proverbs 14:34
text: Righteousness is the only foundation of permanent national prosperity. No outward greatness can save a wicked people from ruin.

title: Proverbs 15:1
text: Mild and conciliatory words often win those whom harsh and irritating language would only have driven farther from us.

title: Proverbs 15:4
text:
A breach in the spirit; inflicting upon it grievous wounds. 
 
A ungoverned tongue is the source of misery and ruin to its possessor and to others.

title: Proverbs 15:6
text: The blessing of God makes the possessions of the righteous man, be they great or small, a source of comfort and usefulness to him; but a wicked man's troubles increase with his riches.

title: Proverbs 15:7
text: "Out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh," whether it be wisdom or folly.

title: Proverbs 15:8
text: The sacrifice of the wicked; the sacrifice which he offers to God, put here for all his religious services.

title: Proverbs 15:10
text:
The way; the way of uprightness. 
 
All presumptous transgressors hate reproof, and for this reason they are in imminent danger of persisting in sin till it ends in their destruction.

title: Proverbs 15:11
text:
Hell and destruction; the invisible world.   Job 26:6  
 
We may flatter and deceive our fellow sinners, but with God hypocrisy and dissimulation can have no place.

title: Proverbs 15:12
text: Since scorners are unwilling to receive correction from the wise, they must remain fools, and the companions of fools.

title: Proverbs 15:13
text: Cheerfulness is both the privilege and duty of every Christian; it contributes alike to his own comfort and usefulness, and to the welfare of those around him.

title: Proverbs 15:15
text:
The afflicted; the man who, under the pressure of outward trouble, yields to despondency and gloom. 
 
  Merry; cheerful and contented. 
 
Since affliction is the lot of all men, we should place our happiness rather in a contented and believing spirit, than in the possession of outward good.

title: Proverbs 15:16
text: Great treasure; the reference is to the treasures of the wicked.

title: Proverbs 15:17
text: Stalled ox; fatted in the stall.

title: Proverbs 15:18
text: He who would "live peaceably with all men," must first learn to govern his own spirit.

title: Proverbs 15:19
text:
As a hedge of thorns; he meets with perpetual difficulty and trouble. 
 
  Made plain; it is a highway on which he can walk without impediment. 
 
God has so ordered the course of things in this world, that the industrious alone can enjoy life: the slothful meet with difficulties and troubles on every side.

title: Proverbs 15:20
text: Despiseth his mother; and thus fills her heart with heaviness.

title: Proverbs 15:22
text: The beginning of success is deliberation and wise counsels.

title: Proverbs 15:23
text: In the timely and right use of speech lies an important part of our influence and usefulness.

title: Proverbs 15:24
text: Is above; leads upward to God and blessedness.

title: Proverbs 15:25
text: God's almighty power is as terrible to the proud oppressor and his house, as it is glorious to the poor and defenceless who put their trust in him.

title: Proverbs 15:26
text: Pleasant; acceptable to God and men.

title: Proverbs 15:27
text:
Gifts; bribes given to pervert justice. 
 
Unrighteous gain brings trouble and misery to its owner and his family.

title: Proverbs 15:30
text:
The light of the eyes; either what is bright and pleasant to behold, or a friendly look.   Proverbs 16:15  
 
  A good report; good tidings.

title: Proverbs 15:33
text: Is the instruction of wisdom; it guides men into the possession of wisdom.   Proverbs 1:7

title: Proverbs 16:1
text: The preparations of the heart--the answer of the tongue; both the inward disposing of our thoughts and the outward expression of them. So according to our version.  But the literal rendering of the verse is, "To man [belong] the orderings of the heart: but from Jehovah is the answer of the tongue."  "The orderings of the heart" are the plans which it forms: "the answer of the tongue" is the granting of the heart's desire in respect to these plans when expressed in words: that is, according to some, in words of prayer to God; according to others, in arguments of persuasion addressed to men.

title: Proverbs 16:2
text: Self-flattery is the universal sin of fallen man.  The best preservative against its power is, to remember that God sees us as we are, and that he will decide our eternal destiny not according to our opinion of ourselves, but according to his own infallible judgment.

title: Proverbs 16:3
text: God gives permanent success to all who, in the diligent use of the appointed means, humbly commit their labors to him.

title: Proverbs 16:4
text: Yea, even the wicked for the day of evil; "God cannot be tempted of evil, neither tempteth he any man."   James 1:13   But he appoints the wicked, who are "drawn away of their own lusts and enticed" to sin, to "the day of evil," for his own glory and the welfare of his everlasting kingdom.  Most interpreters prefer to render the first clause of this verse thus: The Lord has made every thing for its corresponding end; which gives substantially the same sense.

title: Proverbs 16:6
text:
Mercy and truth; exercised by penitent sinners. 
 
  Purged; expiated.  The meritorious ground of forgiveness is not here considered, but the character to which God gives pardon and salvation.  Compare  Matthew 25:34-46 Romans 2:10 . 
 
Though no good works can merit forgiveness of sin, God will bestow it only upon those who diligently practise them, for they are the certain fruits of repentance and faith.

title: Proverbs 16:7
text:
To be at peace with him; that is, as far as his best good and that of the church of God require.   I Peter 3:13   God sometimes allows his servants to be persecuted for righteousness' sake. 
 
The good man's enemies are entirely in God's power.  He has only to do his duty, and God will either turn their hatred into love, or overrule it for his good and that of his church.

title: Proverbs 16:9
text: Our plans accomplish not what we intend, but what God sees to be best for us and his cause.

title: Proverbs 16:10
text:
A divine sentence; God has appointed him to administer justice in his behalf. 
 
  Transgresseth not; or, should not transgress.  Here and in  Proverbs 16:13  the king is described according to the true nature of his office.  When he acts in character, his mouth transgresseth not in judgment.

title: Proverbs 16:11
text:
The Lord's--his work; he has ordained them as the means of justice, and requires that they be true. 
 
  The bag; in which travelling merchants anciently carried their weights. 
 
Uprightness in our dealings with each other is a matter not of human convenience, but of divine requirement, and God will punish the want of it by exclusion from heaven.

title: Proverbs 16:12
text: There is but one law for rulers and private persons--righteousness and prosperity, or wickedness and ruin.

title: Proverbs 16:13
text: Upright rulers will surround themselves with men of truth.

title: Proverbs 16:15
text: As a cloud of the latter rain; acceptable and refreshing.  The descriptions in this and the preceding verse are peculiarly applicable to the governments of the East, where the power of the monarch is well-nigh unlimited.

title: Proverbs 16:17
text: Highway of the upright; in which they walk securely.

title: Proverbs 16:19
text: The conqueror who enriches himself by the spoils of nations is great in the eyes of sinners, but the meek and lowly Christian is great in the eyes of God.

title: Proverbs 16:21
text:
Lips; the teacher's lips. 
 
  Learning; the learning of those whom he instructs. 
 
A pleasant and winning manner, not less than soundness of doctrine, is the duty of every teacher, for his success depends mainly upon it.

title: Proverbs 16:22
text: The instruction of fools is folly; if they undertake to teach, they can communicate nothing but folly.

title: Proverbs 16:26
text: Craveth it of him; men's bodily wants urge them on to hard toil.

title: Proverbs 16:27
text: Diggeth up evil; industriously toils at his mischievous plans.

title: Proverbs 16:28
text: No person is more abhorred and avoided than the slanderer and whisperer, whose course is marked by the creation of strife and dissension among brethren.

title: Proverbs 16:30
text: Shutteth his eyes--moving his lips; signs of secret mischief.

title: Proverbs 16:32
text: The mighty conqueror who has not learned to urle his own spirit leads a miserable life, and will come to a miserable end.

title: Proverbs 16:33
text: Cast into the lap--the whole disposing thereof; man casts the lot, but God decides the issue of it.

title: Proverbs 17:1
text:
Sacrifices; sumptuous fare from the flesh of slain beasts. 
 
Domestic comfort depends not on outward abundance, but on inward harmony and love.

title: Proverbs 17:2
text:
Shall have part of the inheritance; his master will give him a share with his own sons. 
 
Wisdom is better than high birth to give influence and honor.

title: Proverbs 17:4
text: Wicked and corrupt men choose the wicked and corrupt for their companions and accomplices.

title: Proverbs 17:6
text: It is the ordinance of God that in well-trained families the parents and children shall be a mutual comfort and honor to each other.

title: Proverbs 17:7
text: Excellent speech; such speech as belongs to men in eminent stations.  He is not fit for a high place, and connot adapt his language to it.

title: Proverbs 17:8
text:
A gift; given to secure influence. 
 
  Him that hath it; its receiver. 
 
  Whithersoever it turneth it prospereth; as a precious stone reflects its lustre in every way, so a gift is successful in influencing men, whithersoever it is directed.

title: Proverbs 17:9
text:
Covereth a transgression--repeateth a matter; he who covers a transgression which he has witnessed in another, seeks the peace and harmony of the community, but he who repeats an ill report separates friends. 
 
Peace and harmony can be maintained only by mutual kindness and forbearance; a tale-bearer may embroil a whole community in strife.

title: Proverbs 17:10
text: Since fools can never learn from experience, their life must be one of perpetual disappointment and trouble, and their end destruction.

title: Proverbs 17:11
text:
Rebellion; contumacy and sedition towards the magistrate. 
 
  A cruel messenger; a messenger sent by the ruling power to execute vengeance upon him.   Proverbs 16:14   The proverb finds its most awful fulfilment in the case of those who rebel against God's righteous government.

title: Proverbs 17:12
text:
Fool in his folly; that is, a fool acting out his folly in a paroxysm of rage. 
 
Nothing is so unreasonable as folly.

title: Proverbs 17:14
text: It is easier to maintain peace in a family or community, that to restore it.

title: Proverbs 17:15
text: Rulers and judges act in God's behalf, and for the perversion of justice he will call them to an account.

title: Proverbs 17:16
text:
A price; an opportunity afforded by God. 
 
Since men remain ignorant of God and his salvation, not from the want of opportunities to learn, but becuase they have no heart for it, the justice of God in their destruction will be made manifest to all at the last great day.

title: Proverbs 17:17
text: Loveth at all times; in adversity, as well as prosperity; the character of a true friend.

title: Proverbs 17:19
text: Exalteth his gate; the gate to his mansion: a lofty gate implies a sumptuous edifice, the product of ambition and vain-glory.

title: Proverbs 17:22
text:
A merry heart; a cheerful heart, full of peace and joy. 
 
"A merry heart" is alike honorable to God, in whose righteous government we have always abundant reason to rejoice, and profitable to ourselves; it strengthens the body, and invigorates the powers of the soul.  By indulging ourselves in despondency and discontent we reproach our Maker, impair our physical health, and wither up the noblest faculties of the soul.

title: Proverbs 17:23
text: A wicked man; privily receives a bribe from the bosom of him whose cause is pending.

title: Proverbs 17:24
text:
Before him that hath understanding; so that he readily discerns it. 
 
  In the ends of the earth; pursuing folly, so that he never sees true wisdom.   Ecclesiastes 2:14

title: Proverbs 17:26
text: For equity; because of their equity.

title: Proverbs 17:27
text: A great part of wisdom lies in forbearing to speak, except when we have something important to say.

title: Proverbs 18:1
text: Having separated himself; from society, that he may give himself to study.  But many render this verse thus: he who separateth himself from his fellow-men, seeketh after his own desire; he opposeth himself to all wisdom.

title: Proverbs 18:2
text: They who have least wisdom are most fond of uttering their opinions.

title: Proverbs 18:3
text:
Cometh; into power and influence. 
 
  Contempt, and with ignominy reproach; contempt and reproach heaped by him upon his fellow-man. 
 
When the wicked come into power they fill society with abuse and contumely.

title: Proverbs 18:4
text:
A man's mouth; that is, a wise man's mouth. 
 
  Well-spring of wisdom; which gushes forth from his heart, and is inexhaustible.

title: Proverbs 18:5
text: To overthrow; in order to overthrow.

title: Proverbs 18:6
text:
Calleth for strokes; provokes men to inflict stripes upon him. 
 
The words of a foolish man are as calamitous to himself as to others. They fill society with contentions, and bring upon him condign punishment.

title: Proverbs 18:8
text: Into the innermost parts of the belly; inflicting mortal wounds.

title: Proverbs 18:9
text: Sloth and prodigality lead to the same end, want and misery.

title: Proverbs 18:11
text: It is natural to fallen man to trust in uncertain riches, rather than in the living God.  This makes the salvation of the rich exceedingly difficult--harder than for a camel to go through the eye of a needle.

title: Proverbs 18:12
text: A man's spirit is a sure indication of the lot that awaits him: if he be humble, honor; if haughty, ruin.   Luke 18:14

title: Proverbs 18:13
text:
Answereth a matter; gives his opinion on a matter. 
 
It is a good rule not to express an opinion till we have had a full opportunity to hear both sides.  He who pursues the opposite course proclaims his folly, and brings upon himself perpetual mortification.

title: Proverbs 18:14
text:
The spirit of a man--a wounded spirit; the meaning is, that a courageous spirit will enable a man to bear up under the pressure of grief and pain; but a broken and desponding spirit, that has lost the power of endurance, is an intolerable evil. 
 
By courage and faith all evils are made tolerable.  A pusillanimous spirit, that faints at the approach of trouble, is as distressing as it is sinful.

title: Proverbs 18:17
text:
First in his own cause; first in telling his own story. 
 
  His neighbor; his antagonist.

title: Proverbs 18:21
text: They that love it shall eat the fruit thereof; they that will exercise the gift of speech must reap the consequences, be they good or evil.

title: Proverbs 18:22
text: God has ordained the marriage relation for the purity, comfort, and usefulness of man.  Notwithstanding all the evils which human depravity has introduced into it, it is, in general, better than to be alone; and he who finds a wise and virtuous wife, receives from God the richest earthly blessing.

title: Proverbs 18:23
text: The tendency of wealth to foster pride and haughtiness of spirit, is great.  To be rich, and at the same time truly humble, is the fruit of divine grace.

title: Proverbs 19:1
text: The true worth of a man should be measured by his character, and not by his outward circumstances.  A poor man of truth and wisdom is more honorable in the sight of God, and more useful to his fellow men, than one of great rank and wealth whose life is made up of perverseness and folly.

title: Proverbs 19:2
text:
Hasteth with his feet; is rash and inconsiderate in his actions--a common result of the soul's being without knowledge. 
 
Hasty and inconsiderate action comes from the want of true knowledge, and leads to sin.

title: Proverbs 19:3
text: Men too frequently lay to the account of God's providence the calamities which their own perverseness brings upon them, and thus foolishly fret against the Lord.

title: Proverbs 19:4
text: The unreasonable deference which is everywhere paid to wealth, is a sad proof of human selfishness and blindness.  The mass of mankind prefer riches without either wisdom or righteousness, to the neglect which attends virtuous poverty.

title: Proverbs 19:10
text:
Delight; dainty living, which implies ease and affluence. 
 
  Much less for a servant to have rule over princes; that is, a servant retaining a low and servile spirit, which often happens through the favoritism of Eastern monarchs. 
 
When wealth and patronage fall into the hands of the foolish, and the base are exalted above the excellent, the true order of society is perverted, and confusion and misery ensue.

title: Proverbs 19:11
text:
Deferreth his anger; makes him slow to anger. 
 
Slowness to anger and a forgiving spirit are true marks of a noble soul.

title: Proverbs 19:13
text: A continual dropping; of water through the roof in a rainy day; which is very common in oriental houses, and very annoying.

title: Proverbs 19:14
text:
The inheritance of fathers; received from fathers. 
 
  From the Lord; the gift of his providence.  She cannot, like houses and riches, be inherited.

title: Proverbs 19:16
text:
Despiseth his ways; despiseth attention to his ways, because he does not consider himself in danger of going astray.   Proverbs 14:16  
 
The man who thinks himself in no danger is near destruction.

title: Proverbs 19:17
text: The best investment of our property is in deeds of loving-kindness.

title: Proverbs 19:18
text:
Hope; of his being reclaimed. 
 
  And let not thy soul spare for his crying; the original might be rendered, Desire not to slay him; that is, act not as if it were your desire to destroy him, which you will do if you withhold needed chastisement. 
 
The rod is God's appointment; and the parent who uses it early and discreetly, manifests the truest kindness to his children.

title: Proverbs 19:19
text: He that is under the control of his angry passions cannot be saved from ruin, either by his own descretion or by the advice and help of his friends.

title: Proverbs 19:21
text: The subordination of all our plans to the wise counsel of God, constitutes the only sure foundation for peace and tranquillity of spirit.  It is only when we make God's will our will, that we can avoid perpetual disquietude and disappointment.

title: Proverbs 19:22
text:
The desire of a man is his kindness; a man's kindness is that which makes him an object of affectionate regard, to whom the afflicted and destitute look with longing desire. 
 
  A poor man is better than a liar; that is, a poor man of kindness is better than a rich liar destitute of all goodness. 
 
None but the truly good can gain the true love of their fellow men.

title: Proverbs 19:24
text: In his bosom; or, in the dish; a figurative way of saying his is too indolent to attend to his own wants.

title: Proverbs 19:25
text: Scorners are smitten for the good of others; men of understanding are reproved for their own benefit.

title: Proverbs 19:26
text: No course of conduct brings greater disgrace upon a young men, than to be guilty of squandering his father's estate, and making his mother homeless.

title: Proverbs 19:27
text: One of the most deadly perils to which the young are exposed, is false doctrine in respect to the principles of religion and morals.  It meets them everywhere, in unprincipled associates, public teachers of error, and corrupt publications.  Without constant vigilance and prayerfulness, they cannot escape its fatal influence.

title: Proverbs 19:28
text:
Scorneth judgment; has no concern to give his testimony according to truth and equity. 
 
  Devoureth iniquity; feeds upon it as upon a sweet morsel.  Job 20:12-13

title: Proverbs 20:1
text: Since wine and strong drink darken the reason, bring the soul under the control of excitement and passion, and thus prepare it for folly and wickedness of every sort, no wise man will give himself up to their power.

title: Proverbs 20:2
text: Fear of a king; his wrath, which is an object of fear to his subjects.

title: Proverbs 20:3
text: Meddling; embroiling himself in contentions.  But we may better render, "Every fool will be angry;" that is, by giving way to a passionate spirit, will involve himself in strife.

title: Proverbs 20:5
text: Man; that is, a wise man; his heart is an inexhaustible reservoir of knowledge, from which the skilful can draw at all times.

title: Proverbs 20:6
text: They who make the largest professions of goodness and love, are in general the least worthy of confidence in any work that requires patient and self-denying toil.

title: Proverbs 20:7
text: The best inheritance which a man can leave to his children is his own holy life.

title: Proverbs 20:8
text: With his eyes; by his vigilance and sagacity in detecting iniquity.

title: Proverbs 20:9
text: The best men are most deeply conscious of their sinfulness.  It is only the blinding power of sin that leads any to claim that they are free from it.

title: Proverbs 20:12
text: The Lord hath made even both of them; "He that planted the ear, shall he not hear? he that formed the eye, shall he not see?"  Psalms 94:9

title: Proverbs 20:14
text:
Naught; that is, bad in quality. 
 
  Boasteth; of his good bargain. 
 
The habit of buyers to depreciate, and of sellers to exaggerate the worth of articles of traffic, is a species of dishonesty as base and degrading as it is common.

title: Proverbs 20:15
text: Gold, and a multitude of rubies--a precious jewel; gold and precious gems are comparatively plenty, but the lips of knowledge are a much rarer and more valuable possession.

title: Proverbs 20:16
text:
Take his garment--a stranger; as much as to say, If one is so foolish as to become a surety for a stranger, he will have to pledge his garment to you for money to meet the obligation thus incurred; and you will have to take his garment, for he will be unable to redeem it himself. 
 
  Take a pledge--strange woman; nothing better can be expected of the same foolish man, than that he should pledge his garment to you for money to be used by him as the hire of a strange woman, and with the same result as before.

title: Proverbs 20:17
text:
Shall be filled with gravel; the bread will, as it were, turn to gravel in his mouth; his fraud will end in sorrow. 
 
It is only in anticipation that dishonest gain is pleasant; its end is bitterness and vexation of spirit.

title: Proverbs 20:19
text:
Flattereth with his lips; literally, openeth wide his lips, that is, as a talebearer, for he will reveal your secrets also. 
 
The man who reveals to us the secrets of others, proves himself unworthy to be intrusted with our own.

title: Proverbs 20:20
text: God returns the injurious conduct of children upon their own heads. Filial ingratitude is the direct road to ruin, temporal and spiritual.  Leviticus 20:9

title: Proverbs 20:21
text:
Gotten hastily; that is, more hastily than it could have been by righteous means.   Proverbs 28:20  
 
As "he that maketh haste to be rich shall not be innocent," so neither shall his prosperity be permanent.

title: Proverbs 20:22
text: We always do well to leave vengeance in the hands of God, to whom it belongs.

title: Proverbs 20:25
text:
Who devoureth that which is holy; appropriates to his own use that which, by the law, should have been consecrated to God's service.  But it may be rendered, who rashly makes vows of consecration. 
 
  To make inquiry; whether they shall be kept. 
 
Rash vows, by which men bind themselves to certain outward actions under the name of religion, are highly perniciuos in their influence. When the young and inexperienced take upon themselves vows of celibacy and exclusion from society, they only spread a snare for their souls.

title: Proverbs 20:26
text: Bringeth the wheel; of the threshing-wagon; that is, he destroys them.

title: Proverbs 20:27
text:
The candle of the Lord; a candle which God has placed within him. 
 
  Searching all the inward parts; taking cognizance of his most secret thoughts.   I Corinthians 2:11

title: Proverbs 20:30
text:
Blueness; the reference is to the scars made by severe blows.  We may paraphrase the verse thus: Severe blows inflicted upon the transgressor cleanse his soul from evil; and stripes, his inward spirit. 
 
That chastisement which cleanses the soul from sin is a rich blessing, however severe it may be.

title: Proverbs 21:1
text: God overrules all the plans of earthly rulers, be they righteous or wicked, for the accomplishment of his own wise and good designs.

title: Proverbs 21:3
text: God will not accept the outward forms of religion as a substitute for its inward spirit, "judgment, mercy, and faith."

title: Proverbs 21:4
text: The ploughing of the wicked; their tillage; put here for all their plans, pursuits, and pleasures.  Or, "the light of the wicked," means that in which they glory.

title: Proverbs 21:5
text:
The diligent; who seek wealth by honest industry. 
 
  Hasty; impatient to amass wealth, and therefore employing unlawful means.

title: Proverbs 21:6
text:
A vanity tossed to and fro; an empty and unstable possession.  Some render, A fleeting breath, which gives the same idea. 
 
  Seek death; take the way to death. 
 
Treasures obtained by fraud and falsehood conduct their owner down to perdition, and there forsake him.

title: Proverbs 21:8
text:
Strange; alienated from God. 
 
  The pure; in contrast with the mass of mankind, whose way is froward and strange.

title: Proverbs 21:10
text: A wicked man cannot be trusted where his own private interests are concerned; for he will not scruple for his own ends to sacrifice his neighbor's property, comfort, reputation, morality, and everlasting welfare.

title: Proverbs 21:12
text: Wisely considereth; derives lessons of instruction from God's dealings with it.

title: Proverbs 21:13
text: We all need mercy at the hand of God: but we shall not obtain it unless we show pity to our fellow men; for with the merciful, God will show himself merciful.

title: Proverbs 21:16
text: Remain in the congregation of the dead; be numbered and dwell with the dead.  Compare  Proverbs 2:22 .

title: Proverbs 21:17
text: Luxurious living is the highway to poverty.

title: Proverbs 21:18
text: Shall be a ransom for the righteous; God will make the destruction of the wicked a means of salvation to the righteous, as is illustrated in the deliverance of Israel from Egypt.   Isaiah 43:3-4

title: Proverbs 21:20
text: When poverty comes from prodigality it is as ignominious as sinful.

title: Proverbs 21:25
text: The desire of the slothful; his longing desire for good that cannot be obtained without labor.

title: Proverbs 21:26
text:
The righteous; who has gained an abundance by honest toil.  Compare  Proverbs 21:20 . 
 
The righteous man values property and labors for it chiefly because of the means which it furnishes of doing good to his fellow men.

title: Proverbs 21:28
text:
Heareth; has an obedient and teachable spirit, which includes in itself the love of truth. 
 
  Speaketh constantly; while "the mouth of them that speak lies shall be stopped," he shall speak constantly with favor and credit.

title: Proverbs 21:29
text:
Hardeneth his face; rejects all counsel, and obstinately follows his own corrupt desires. 
 
  Directeth his way; bestows serious consideration upon it, that it may be conformed to God's law.

title: Proverbs 21:30
text: The Lord has all the resources of heaven and earth at his disposal, and he can with infinite ease accomplish his own purposes in the face of all opposition from wicked men and fallen spirits; nay more, he can make their efforts to defeat his counsels the direct means of fulfilling them.

title: Proverbs 21:31
text: Without God's favor the most formidable warlike preparations will be of no avail.

title: Proverbs 22:1
text: Our comfort and usefulness depend on our character, rather than on our outward possessions.

title: Proverbs 22:2
text:
Meet together; come into contact in various relations of life. 
 
  The Lord is the maker of them all; he is their common Lord, has placed them together in this world, and will call them to an account for their treatment of each other.

title: Proverbs 22:3
text: In the gospel of his Son, God has provided a refuge from the evil that is coming upon all sinners.  The highest wisdom of men is to hide themselves in this refuge; to neglect it, is their folly and ruin.

title: Proverbs 22:5
text: The way of those who oppose themselves to God's government must be filled with "thorns and snares."  It is in the path of duty that we find comfort and safety.

title: Proverbs 22:6
text: In committing to parents the training of their children, God has, in a very important sense, committed to them the formation of their future character, and he will hold them responsible for the influence they exert.

title: Proverbs 22:7
text: To contract debts beyond our ability to pay, is to rob ourselves of that manly independence which belongs to the righteous man's character, and to expose ourselves to innumerable temptations as well as annoyances.  For this reason, as well as from regard to our own reputation and the rights of others, it is a cardinal Christian virtue to "owe no man any thing, but to love one another."

title: Proverbs 22:8
text:
Vanity; disappointment and misery. 
 
  The rod of his anger; the rod wherewith he smote his fellow-men in anger. 
 
They who occupy themselves with devising mischief to others, are preparing for themselves a harvest of shame and trouble.

title: Proverbs 22:11
text: The grace of his lips; his pleasant and well-timed words.

title: Proverbs 22:12
text: Preserve knowledge; watch over and protect knowledge, by protecting those who possess it and use it for the good of their fellow-men.

title: Proverbs 22:13
text: The slothful exaggerate the difficulties that lie in the way of duty.

title: Proverbs 22:14
text:
Mouth of strange women; their "much fair speech,"  Proverbs 7:21 . 
 
  Abhorred of the Lord; because he turns aside from the right way.

title: Proverbs 22:16
text: Giveth to the rich; from selfish motives, to purchase their favor.

title: Proverbs 22:17
text: Here begins another division of the book, extending to the end of the twenty-fourth chapter.  It has a general resemblance to the first nine chapters.

title: Proverbs 22:19
text: Made known; that is, these words.

title: Proverbs 22:20
text: In counsels and knowledge; containing counsels and words of knowledge.

title: Proverbs 22:21
text: To them that send unto thee; to ask counsel of thee.  Or, "To those that send thee;" tht is, mayest make a true report to them of the business intrusted to thee.

title: Proverbs 22:22
text: In the gate; where courts were anciently held, and public business was transacted.

title: Proverbs 22:23
text: The more destitute one is of human protection, the greater is the guilt and the danger of wronging him; the Lord is the patron of the defenceless, and will avenge the injuries done to them.

title: Proverbs 22:29
text: Diligence in business leads to preferment and honor.

title: Proverbs 23:1
text:
With a ruler; who has invited thee to a sumptuous entertainment. 
 
When tempted to the immoderate indulgence of appetite, we should lay a severe restraint upon ourselves; for it impairs the faculties of soul and body, stupefies the conscience, and degrades us in our own estimation and that of our fellow men.

title: Proverbs 23:2
text: Put a knife to thy throat; to prevent excess in eating; a figurative way of saying, Restrain thine appetite at all costs.

title: Proverbs 23:3
text: Deceitful meat; they promise much pleasure, but end in pain and shame.  The reference is to the immoderate indulgence of appetite at the tables of the great, which not only injures the guest, but degrades him in the eyes of all present.

title: Proverbs 23:4
text: Thine own wisdom; the wisdom which makes riches the chief good, and thinks by prudent management to get and keep them.

title: Proverbs 23:5
text: The consideration of the uncertainty of all earthly possessions, leads every wise and considerate man to provide for himself "a treasure in the heavens that faileth not."

title: Proverbs 23:6
text:
That hath an evil eye; the grudging man, or the crafty and malicious man, who invites the unwary to his table only to deceive and ensnare them. 
 
It is a common device of crafty dissemblers to flatter and bestow favors only that they may ensnare and plunder.  Against the hospitality of such men the young should guard as against thieves and burglars.

title: Proverbs 23:8
text:
Vomit up; that is, it will end in bitterness. 
 
  Sweet words; addressed by him to thee.

title: Proverbs 23:9
text: The man who treats with contempt the counsels of the wise, releases them from the obligation of further admonition, and makes his own ruin certain.

title: Proverbs 23:11
text: Their redeemer; God, who defends the cause of the poor and fatherless.

title: Proverbs 23:13
text:
Shall not die; shall be reclaimed from sin, and so saved from death. 
 
Our heavenly Father prefers that we should weep now under his chastising rod, rather than perish at last through want of timely discipline.  Herein every wise parent will imitate God's example in his dealings with his children.

title: Proverbs 23:18
text: An end; that is, in the present connection, a prosperous end; or, a reward, namely, to those that fear God.  Compare  Job 6:11 , note;  Job 42:12 James 5:11 .

title: Proverbs 23:29
text: The imbecility and loathsome disease which the habit of using intoxicating drinks produces, and the dreadful power of this habit to perpetuate itself; the poverty, contention, and wretchedness with which it fills the family circle; the quarrels, murders, debaucheries, and crimes that follow in its train, are well understood at the present day.  Whoever allows himself in this debasing habit, or furnishes to others the intoxicating cup, is without excuse.

title: Proverbs 23:31
text: Moveth itself aright; goes down smoothly.

title: Proverbs 23:34
text: Lieth down; to sleep on the deck of a ship, or at the mast's head; representing the disordered condition of the drunkard in soul and body, which causes him to reel, and makes all around and within him a troubled and heaving sea.

title: Proverbs 23:35
text:
Was not sick; was not pained from the blows, because of my insensibility. 
 
  It; the intoxicating cup.

title: Proverbs 24:1
text:
Envious against evil men--desire to be with them; because of their present success. 
 
Since the prosperity of the ungodly leads only to ruin, no wise man will envy them, or wish to cast in his lot with them.

title: Proverbs 24:4
text: Success comes not by chance, but by prudent counsels and actions.

title: Proverbs 24:6
text: For by wise counsel thou shalt make thy war; that is, with success; an illustration of the declaration in the preceding verse, that wisdom and knowledge give strength.

title: Proverbs 24:7
text: In the gate; where causes are tried and deliberations held on weighty matters.

title: Proverbs 24:9
text: The thought of foolishness; the plans and pursuits of foolish men. fill out the two clauses thus: The thoughts and actions of fools and scorners are sinful, and therefore an abomination to men.

title: Proverbs 24:10
text: God sends upon men adversity for the purpose of exercising their faith and fortitude, and thus increasing these graces; but hed who faints under the discipline loses the benefit of it, and becomes weaker instead of stronger.

title: Proverbs 24:11
text: Drawn unto death--ready to be slain; unjustly seized and dragged to a violent death.  This precept applies primarily to magistrates, and also to private persons according to their ability to help the oppressed and unjustly condemned.

title: Proverbs 24:12
text: It is the duty of all men, as they have opportunity, to succor and relieve the oppressed.  And since the worst bondage is that of sin and ignorance, no man may on any ground excuse himself from doing what lies in his power for the rescue of the millions who are held under its thraldom.

title: Proverbs 24:13
text:
vv 13-14. 
 
  Eat thou honey-- so shall the knowledge of wisdom be unto thy soul; that is, I commend thee for eating honey, because it is good; much more, then, do thou gain the knowledge of wisdom, which is better than honey.

title: Proverbs 24:14
text: No possession yields so precious a revenue as wisdom.  It makes men rich for time and eternity.

title: Proverbs 24:16
text:
The wicked shall fall into mischief; out of which he shall never rise again. 
 
The just man falls for his discipline, and God will raise him up again; but the wicked falls for his destruction.

title: Proverbs 24:17
text: Joy at the calamity of an enemy is a heinous sin, and one which God will visit with condign punishment.

title: Proverbs 24:21
text:
Them that are given to change; seditious men, like Absalom, who seek to change the established order of government. 
 
They who follow discontented innovators, do it to their destruction.

title: Proverbs 24:22
text: The ruin of them both; the ruin which will come upon such men from both God and the king, whose wrath they have incurred.

title: Proverbs 24:23
text:
These things also; the maxims that follow to the end of the chapter. 
 
  Belong to the wise; either, should be observed by the wise, or, are sayings of the wise.  In either case, these words introduce a short appendix to this part of the book.

title: Proverbs 24:25
text:
Him; the "wicked" man mentioned in  Proverbs 24:24 . 
 
  Delight; the pleasant favor of the good.

title: Proverbs 24:27
text:
Thy work without; thy work which lies out of doors; that is, thy work of agriculture. 
 
  Make it fit for thyself; or, prepare for thyself. 
 
  Afterwards build thy house; a house for elegance and luxury seems to be intended, which should be postponed till other more important work is done. In the warm climate of Palestine a very slight structure serves for the necessary wants of a family.  Another interpretation, Get the materials of thy house ready before thou buildest, is not favored by the original words. 
 
The wise man will postpone works of mere elegance and luxury till he has attended to his more necessary business.

title: Proverbs 24:30
text: In things spiritual and temporal, the slothful procrastinator may be known by the disordered and decaying condition of what is committed to his care.

title: Proverbs 24:34
text: One that travelleth; a traveller who comes as an enemy.

title: Proverbs 25:1
text: Copied out; here begins the fourth part of the book, containing a selection of proverbs collected and arranged from the writings of Solomon, probably by Hezekiah's command and for his use.  It repeats a number of proverbs that have already appeared.

title: Proverbs 25:2
text:
To conceal a thing; he manifests his infinite perfections by the unsearchableness of his ways in both nature and providence. 
 
  To search out a matter; they show their qualification for their high office by sagacity in searching out and understanding every thing that concerns the administration of their government.

title: Proverbs 25:3
text: The heart of kings; their secret counsels.

title: Proverbs 25:4
text: A vessel for the finer; a vessel of pure silver to reward the finer's labor.

title: Proverbs 25:5
text: If rulers would have permanent prosperity, they must banish the corrupt from their councils, and surround themselves with righteous men.

title: Proverbs 25:6
text: Modesty is the road to true preferment.  Those who ambitiously thrust themselves above their true position, will be, in the end, cast down to the lowest place.

title: Proverbs 25:7
text: Come up hither; see  Luke 14:7-11 .

title: Proverbs 25:8
text: The wise man will not engage in controversy till he is sure of his ground, and can see his way through it.

title: Proverbs 25:11
text: Apples of gold in pictures of silver; golden apples embroidered in picture-work of silver.  Some render, Apples of gold in baskets of silver network.

title: Proverbs 25:12
text: Reproof wisely administered to the wise is most precious in its results.

title: Proverbs 25:13
text:
Snow; brought from the mountains and used for cooling drinks. 
 
Fidelity in the execution of a trust is a virtue which men are quick to perceive, and ready to reward; the unfaithful man, on the contrary, is with good reason dreaded and shunned, for he is the ruin of all who put confidence in him.

title: Proverbs 25:14
text: Boasteth himself of a false gift; makes a vain show of liberality, but gives nothing.

title: Proverbs 25:15
text: Wise discourse, tempered by mildness and forbearance, is a more effectual weapon than implements of war.

title: Proverbs 25:16
text: Eat so much as is sufficient; make a moderate use of every privilege that falls to your lot--as, for example, a neighbor's hospitality,  Proverbs 25:17 --and do not spoil it by excess.

title: Proverbs 25:17
text: To abuse a neighbor's hospitality is the way to lose it.

title: Proverbs 25:19
text: Fidelity in the execution of a trust is a virtue which men are quick to perceive, and ready to reward; the unfaithful man, on the contrary, is with good reason dreaded and shunned, for he is the ruin of all who put confidence in him.

title: Proverbs 25:20
text:
Vinegar upon nitre; Egyptian nitre, which effervesces with an acid, and loses its strength.  The incongruity of singing songs to a heavy heart is illustrated by two comparisons. 
 
An ill-timed act is unseemly, if not offensive.

title: Proverbs 25:22
text:
Heap coals of fire upon his head; fill him with shame, and thus bring him to repentance. 
 
He who overcomes an enemy by kindness, gains a victory which makes both parties blessed.

title: Proverbs 25:26
text:
Falling down before the wicked; either voluntarily, from fear or interest; or, falling under his power. 
 
  Troubled--corrupt; spoiled by the trampling of cattle. 
 
When the righteous yield to the wicked, the very fountains of virtue are corrupted.

title: Proverbs 25:28
text: As a city without walls is exposed to every assault of the enemy, so a spirit without self-government is the prey of every corrupt passion.

title: Proverbs 26:2
text: As the bird by wandering--so the curse causeless shall not come; God's curse will not come upon men at random, like the flight of birds.

title: Proverbs 26:4
text:
Answer not a fool according to his folly; with such foolish words as he uses. 
 
vv 4-5. In dealing with the ignorant and self-conceited, great wisdom is necessary, lest, on the one side, we make ourselves like them, or, on the other, fail to put to silence their foolish words.

title: Proverbs 26:5
text: Answer a fool according to his folly; in a manner adapted to rebuke it.

title: Proverbs 26:6
text: Cutteth off the feet; his own feet, and thus cripples himself in respect to the business on hand.

title: Proverbs 26:7
text:
Are not equal; so that he has a limping gait.  Others render, "hang down;" that is, as a useless weight. 
 
  So is a parable in the mouth of fools; they have not skill to make a discreet use of it.

title: Proverbs 26:8
text:
Bindeth a stone in a sling; performs an absurd and useless act. Or, "Putteth a precious stone in a heap of stones," among which it will be lost. 
 
All preferment is thrown away upon the foolish.

title: Proverbs 26:9
text:
Into the hand of a drunkard; a reeling drunkard, who lays hold of it to support himself. 
 
  A parable in the mouth of fools; by perverting it, they make it an injury to themselves. 
 
It is the part of folly to pervert to its own injury that which was designed for its profit.

title: Proverbs 26:16
text:
A reason; a good reason for a wise course of action.  The sluggard's course is foolish and ruinous, yet he thinks himself wiser than all his advisers. 
 
They who have no good reason to give for their conduct, are most inclined to despise the counsels of the wise.

title: Proverbs 26:17
text:
By the ears; to his own hurt. 
 
Intermeddlers always bring themselves into trouble.

title: Proverbs 26:19
text: Falsehood and deception do not become either innocent or harmless because practised in sport; the deceiver who excuses himself on this ground, will find that at God's bar these are treated as heinous offences.

title: Proverbs 26:20
text: Since talebearers exist in every community, the best way is to rebuke them, and close our ears to their words.  Where the people have wisdom to do this, strife will cease.

title: Proverbs 26:21
text:
Coals--to burning coals; coals added to a heap of burning coals, which makes the fire hotter. 
 
The contentious man's tongue is "set on fire of hell;" and he sets on fire the whole community in which he dwells.

title: Proverbs 26:23
text:
Burning lips; his lips that make warm professions of love. 
 
  Silver dross; glittering, yet worthless.

title: Proverbs 26:24
text: vv 24-26. The weapons of malice are flattery, hypocrisy, and deceit, but God's providence will strip off its disguises and expose its wickedness before the world.

title: Proverbs 26:27
text:
Rolleth; in order that it may overwhelm others. 
 
  Return upon him; fall back upon him by the slipping of his hands. By some unforeseen turn of events, the mischief which he was preparing for others shall fall upon himself.

title: Proverbs 27:1
text: He who makes confident plans for the future, forgets his dependence on divine providence, and prepares himself for bitter disappointment.

title: Proverbs 27:2
text: The blinding influence of self-love makes us poor judges of our own good qualities.  For this reason self-commendation is always unseemly.

title: Proverbs 27:3
text: A wise man's wrath is under the control of reason; but a fool's rage has no bounds.

title: Proverbs 27:4
text: Mere anger is temporary; but envy, like a poisonous serpent, is ever watching for an opportunity to strike its victim.

title: Proverbs 27:5
text: Secret love; love allowed to lie hid in the bosom through false tenderness and fear of giving offence, and not manifesting itself, as it should, in reproving and correcting the faults of a friend.

title: Proverbs 27:6
text: True love, properly exercised, will not withhold timely reproof through fear of giving offence.   Leviticus 19:17

title: Proverbs 27:7
text: A deep sense of want makes men ready to accept help upon any terms. The highest illustration of this is in the case of lost sinners, to whom Christ's salvation is offered, through repentance, faith, and daily self-denial.

title: Proverbs 27:9
text: The sweetness of a man's friend; his sweet words of friendship.

title: Proverbs 27:10
text: Neither go into thy brother's house; that is, as the preceding and following words show, forsake not a tried family friend who is near at hand, for a brother who is far off.

title: Proverbs 27:11
text: The wisdom of children is the best defence of their parents.

title: Proverbs 27:13
text: Take his garment; see note to  Proverbs 20:16 .

title: Proverbs 27:14
text: A curse to him; to the man who blesses his friend.  Such praise will be suspected as insincere and selfish, and therefore reckoned as bad as a curse.

title: Proverbs 27:15
text: A continual dropping; see  Proverbs 19:13 .

title: Proverbs 27:16
text:
Hideth her; seeks to conceal within doors her unseemly behavior. 
 
  Hideth the wind; that is, tries to hide it, which is a vain undertaking. 
 
  Bewrayeth itself; betrays itself, proclaims its presence by its odor.  His effort to conceal her folly is like attempting to conceal the fragrant ointment upon his right hand.

title: Proverbs 27:17
text:
Sharpeneth the countenance of his friend; a sharpened countenance implies a sharpened mind, that is, a mind made more active and vigorous. 
 
It is only by the contact of mind with mind that it can attain to its highest vigor and strength, as it respects either the intellect or the affections.

title: Proverbs 27:19
text: Since all hearts answer to each other as face to face in water, the foundation of a true knowledge of human nature is the knowledge of ourselves.

title: Proverbs 27:21
text: A man to his praise; praise is the crucible in which a man's character is tried and truly appears.

title: Proverbs 27:22
text:
Bray; pound. 
 
Nothing is so incorrigible as human folly.

title: Proverbs 27:23
text: vv 23-27. The price of an honorable and comfortable competency is diligence and good management.

title: Proverbs 27:24
text:
Are not for ever; are an uncertain possession, requiring vigilance and industry for their preservation. 
 
  Doth the crown endure; even regal dignity is liable to be lost through want of vigilance and wise management.

title: Proverbs 27:25
text: Are gathered; by the prudent husbandman.

title: Proverbs 27:26
text: The price of the field; thou canst give them, or the produce that comes from them, in pay for a field purchased.

title: Proverbs 27:27
text: Shalt have goat's milk enough; that is, by complying with the precept given in  Proverbs 27:23 .

title: Proverbs 28:1
text: Guilt is timorous, and innocence bold.

title: Proverbs 28:2
text:
For; because of. 
 
  Many are the princes thereof; it is continually changing rulers, as we see illustrated in the history of Israel after the revolt of the ten tribes: which is a sore calamity to a nation. 
 
God punishes wicked and corrupt nations by giving them up to frequent and violent changes of government, with all the confusion and misery that follow in their train.

title: Proverbs 28:3
text: A poor man; in eastern countries avaricious men, destitute alike of property and principle, often obtain the government of provinces, which they plunder at pleasure.

title: Proverbs 28:4
text: Wicked men are naturally inclined to take part with those who are, like themselves, against the righteous.  Hence there must be a perpetual conflict between the two classes.

title: Proverbs 28:8
text: For him that will pity the poor; God will take it from him, and give it to him that will pity the poor.

title: Proverbs 28:10
text:
Causeth the righteous to go astray; seeks to lead him astray. 
 
  The upright; whom he sought to mislead.

title: Proverbs 28:11
text: Searcheth him out; finds out his folly.

title: Proverbs 28:12
text:
Great glory; the state is prosperous and honored. 
 
  A man is hidden; a good man is driven into obscurity. 
 
Upright rulers are the glory and strength of a nation; and wicked men its shame and ruin.

title: Proverbs 28:13
text: There is but one way to escape the ruinous consequences of sin, which is by confessing and forsaking it.

title: Proverbs 28:14
text:
Feareth; God. 
 
  Hardeneth his heart; against God's authority.

title: Proverbs 28:16
text:
A great oppressor; it is implied that he shall also come to a violent end. 
 
The highest wisdom of a prince is to seek the welfare of the people committed to his care, for in their prosperity lie his own quiet and security.

title: Proverbs 28:17
text:
Doeth violence to the blood of any person; is laden with the guilt of shedding human blood. 
 
  Shall flee to the pit; shall go down speedily to the dead. 
 
  Stay him; prevent his going to the pit. 
 
That the murderer shall die, is a divine ordinance.  All who seek to set it aside, oppose themselves alike to the wisdom of God and the welfare of the community.

title: Proverbs 28:21
text: The elevation of selfish and unprincipled men to ofice is a great public calamity; they will pervert justice and sacrifice the highest interests of the people for private emolument.

title: Proverbs 28:22
text:
Hasteth to be rich; is greedy of gain, and uses unlawful means to procure it. 
 
The avaricious man, who scruples not to use unjust means for the increase of his estate, is on the highway to final poverty and ruin.

title: Proverbs 28:23
text: Honest dealing with offenders is the way to secure their respect.

title: Proverbs 28:24
text: A destroyer; a dissolute spendthrift.

title: Proverbs 28:26
text:
Wisely; with circumspection and self-distrust. 
 
The absence of self-distrust is a certain sign of folly and approaching destruction.

title: Proverbs 28:27
text:
Hideth his eyes; from their wants. 
 
  Many a curse; from God and man.

title: Proverbs 28:28
text:
Rise; to power. 
 
  Men hide themselves; good men retire into obscurity, that they may avoid the persecution of the wicked.

title: Proverbs 29:1
text: Obstinate residence to reproof is an alarming indication of approaching ruin.

title: Proverbs 29:2
text: Since the welfare of a state depends upon the character of its rulers, it is the duty of all who exercise the elective franchise to prefer the righteous above the wicked, and to elevate to office able men, such as fear God, men of truth, hating covetousness.

title: Proverbs 29:4
text:
Gifts; bribes to pervert judgment. 
 
No government or community can prosper in which the administration of justice is corrupted by bribery.

title: Proverbs 29:6
text:
A snare; to take his own feet. 
 
  Doth sing and rejoice; because his path is free from snares.

title: Proverbs 29:8
text:
Bring a city into a snare; or, set it on fire; fill it with strife and faction. 
 
  Turn away wrath; appease the angry passions of the people, and avert God's anger.

title: Proverbs 29:9
text:
No rest; to the wise man.  He will find it a bootless and uncomfortable contest. 
 
No controversy is more profitless than that which is carried on with one who cannot feel the force of sound arguments.

title: Proverbs 29:10
text: Seek his soul; love him, and protect his life and interests.

title: Proverbs 29:13
text:
Deceitful man; or, "usurer;" who loans to the poor.   Proverbs 22:2  
 
  Lighteneth both their eyes;  Matthew 5:1  Since they both share God's common bounty, they are bound to regard and treat each other as brethren.

title: Proverbs 29:15
text: No child becomes wise and virtuous by pursuing his own inclinations, but only by faithful instruction and discipline.

title: Proverbs 29:18
text:
Vision; revelation of divine truth. 
 
  Perish; or as the Hebrew may be rendered, are made dissolute. 
 
  Keepeth the law; this implies that he lives where there is a "vision." 
 
The faithful dispensation of divine truth is the only hope of a nation. Where this is wanting the people will sink into ignorance and corruption, till their destruction becomes inevitable.

title: Proverbs 29:19
text:
Words; that is, mere words. 
 
  Though he understand; the commands and reproofs of his master. 
 
  He will not answer; in a dutiful spirit; that is, he will not render prompt obedience.  The proverb inculcates the necessity of timely chastisement.

title: Proverbs 29:21
text:
Delicately bringeth up; spoils by indulgence. 
 
  Become his son at the length; the servant will, in the issue, claim to be treated as a son.  But we may understand this proverb of the careful training of a servant of superior worth, so that in the end he takes the place of a son to his master.  Compare  Proverbs 17:2 .

title: Proverbs 29:24
text: Heareth cursing, and bewrayeth it not; is privy to or conceals the false oaths of his companion, and thus shares with him the guilt of perjury.

title: Proverbs 29:25
text:
The fear of man bringeth a snare; leads us in many ways into sin. 
 
He who is swayed by the opinions of his fellow men, rather than by God's word, will be betrayed into innumerable sins and errors, which will prove a snare to his soul.  It is only by faith in God that we can overcome the fear of man, and pursue with steadfastness a course of integrity.

title: Proverbs 29:26
text: Every man's judgment cometh from the Lord; it is to him alone that we can confidently look for justice and deliverance.

title: Proverbs 29:27
text: The whole history of the world from the beginning, is but a fulfilment of the original declaration in Eden: "I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed.

title: Proverbs 30:1
text: The words of Agur; this and the following chapter constitute an appendix to the book of Proverbs.

title: Proverbs 30:3
text:
The holy; God. 
 
Those best qualified to instruct others are most humble and diffident in respect to their own attainments.

title: Proverbs 30:4
text:
Ascended up into heaven, or descended--established all the ends of the earth; these are descriptions of the various operations of God. 
 
  What is his name; to know God's name is to know God himself, for his name expresses the sum of his attributes. 
 
  What is his son's name; a very remarkable expression, in which the Spirit of prophecy seems to point to the future revelation of God's only begotten Son.   John 3:13 Ephesians 4:9-10

title: Proverbs 30:6
text:
Found a liar; in thy additions to his words. 
 
The who add to God's word, under whatever pretext, substitute human wisdom for divine truth, and God will call them to an account for their folly and a wickedness.

title: Proverbs 30:7
text: Before I die; that is, until I die.

title: Proverbs 30:8
text:
Vanity; folly and wickedness. 
 
The most desirable outward condition is that of a moderate competency, free alike from the temptations of wealth and of poverty.

title: Proverbs 30:9
text: Take the name of my God in vain; by false oaths intended to cover the sin of stealing.

title: Proverbs 30:10
text:
He; the servant. 
 
  Guilty; of calumny, and so suffer punishment.

title: Proverbs 30:11
text:
vv 11-14. 
 
  Generation; class of persons.  Through the remainder of this chapter the number four prevails.  Here we have four classes of sinners: the undutiful towards their parents, the self-righteous, the proud, and the avaricious.

title: Proverbs 30:15
text: Two daughters; put here to represent her entire race.  The mention of the horseleech introduces four other insatiable things.

title: Proverbs 30:17
text: Pick it out--eat it; a thing which happens to bodies that have been gibbeted, or left unburied on the battlefield.

title: Proverbs 30:18
text:
Too wonderful for me; that is, whose way I cannot trace, because they leave no mark behind. 
 
There are innumerable deeds of darkness which elude all human vigilance; but God will expose and punish them at the last day.

title: Proverbs 30:20
text:
Eateth; spoken figuratively of her sinful enjoyment. 
 
  Wipeth her mouth; so that none can discern the fact that she has been eating.  The meaning is, that she hides all the marks of her guilt, and passes herself for an innocent person.

title: Proverbs 30:26
text: Conies; a small animal different from our coney, living among the rocks, and distinguished for sagacity.

title: Proverbs 30:28
text: The spider; or house-lizard, which is very frequent in Palestine.

title: Proverbs 30:32
text:
In lifting up thyself; with a haughty and contentious spirit.  This seems to be a caution against the spirit of self-aggrandizement, which is contentious and prone to evil devices. 
 
  Lay thy hand upon thy mouth; be silent and humble thyself. 
 
The spirit of ambition and self-aggrandizement is as foolish as it is wicked. It involves men in angry contention, hypocrisy, falsehood, and dishonest artifices, often to their ruin, both for this world and eternity.

title: Proverbs 30:33
text:
The forcing of wrath; in a struggle for place and power. 
 
  Bringeth forth strife; in which the ambitious man will be involved to his injury.  Here we have a dissuasive from the sin mentioned in the preceding verse.

title: Proverbs 31:2
text:
What, my son? this exclamation of Lemuel's mother implies apprehension in respect to the sins against which she warns him, if not remonstrance against the present practice of them. 
 
  Son of my vows;  I Samuel 1:27-28:1

title: Proverbs 31:3
text:
vv 3-5. 
 
Excessive indulgence is always unseemly and ruinous to both health and intellect; but it is especially unbecoming in magistrates, whom God has appointed to administer justice in his name, and to whom the people naturally look for an example of sobriety and uprightness.

title: Proverbs 31:6
text: The use of wine and other intoxicating drinks as a beverage, may well be given up, as a measure of safety to ourselves and benefit to others, on the principle stated by Paul in  Romans 14:21 .

title: Proverbs 31:10
text:
vv 10-31. 
 
In the closing passage of the book of Proverbs, the pen of inspiration has given, for the instruction of all ages, the character of a "virtuous woman," such as every wise man will choose for his companion in life.  It consists not in the fascination of outward accomplishments, which are too often united with idleness, prodigality, and a selfish, contentious spirit; but rather in industry, good management, authority over her household, and the spirit of love and kindness.  Such a woman will confer honor upon her husband, and make him prosperous and happy, however she may be undervalued by those who are too ignorant to understand in what female worth consists.

title: Proverbs 31:18
text: Perceiveth; well understands from her own experience.

title: Proverbs 31:20
text: Stretcheth out her hand to the poor; her industry has for its object not simply the accumulation of wealth, but the means of doing good.

title: Proverbs 31:23
text: Known in the gates; where courts are held, and public business is transacted.  Her worth confers honor upon him.

title: Proverbs 31:29
text: Many daughters--excellest them all; these are the words of her husband.

title: Proverbs 31:30
text: Favor; outward grace.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:2
text:
Vanity of vanities; utter vanity.  So "holy of holies," as it is in the original, means most holy,  Exodus 30:36 ; and "revolters of revolters," grievous revolters.   Jeremiah 6:28  
 
God has exhibited to us the vanity of all earthly pursuits, that we may make him, and not this world, our portion, and may place our happiness in learning and doing his will.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:3
text:
Profit; solid and permanent good. 
 
  Under the sun; an expression applied in this book to all earthly objects.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:4
text:
vv 4-7. 
 
  One generation passeth--return again; all things run the same unvarying round from age to age; so that the experience of one generation is the experience of all.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:8
text:
All things; all things in this unvarying round.  It is a round of wearisome and unsatisfying toil. 
 
  The eye--the ear; these represent all the human faculties, which are constantly occupied with the pursuit of good, but without being satisfied. 
 
Christ alone can give rest to the soul.  To weary ourselves and waste our day of grace in the vain endeavor to find in the world what he only can bestow, is an unspeakable folly.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:9
text:
There is no new thing; in science and art there may be many new discoveries and inventions; but in the course of human experience, which is the Preacher's theme, there is nothing new. 
 
The errors and follies of the present day are but a repetition of the errors and follies of past ages.  One generation after another gives itself up to the same vain undertaking, that of gaining from this world solid peace and happiness, and meets with the same bitter disappointment.  The way of salvation remains also the same in all ages; a way of holy watchfulness, prayerfulness, and self-denial.  Thus the history of the past, recorded in God's word, becomes a lamp to all succeeding generations.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:11
text: No remembrance of former things; if any thing appears new, it is because the former things are forgotten: forgetfulness of the past is a characteristic of the human family.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:13
text:
By wisdom; by philosophic inquiry, a sense in which the word wisdom is often used in this book. 
 
  Sore travail; wearisome and unsatisfying toil.  The reference is to "all the works that are done under the sun" by men.   Ecclesiastes 1:14

title: Ecclesiastes 1:14
text: Vexation of spirit; or "feeding on the wind." Compare  Hosea 12:1 .

title: Ecclesiastes 1:15
text:
Crooked; in the course of human affairs. 
 
  Numbered; supplied, so as to be counted among the things that are. The vanity of life, growing out of what is crooked and wanting in human affairs, is without remedy.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:17
text: To know wisdom--madness and folly; to understand their nature and effects.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:18
text:
He that increaseth knowledge increaseth sorrow; he learns how many and great are the evils of life, without finding on earth any remedy for them.  Thus ended the Preacher's first experiment to find satisfaction in the pursuit of wisdom. 
 
The mere knowledge of human character and life, however deep and full, cannot make men blessed.  It can only show the desperate malady of sin, without providing any remedy for it.  True happiness comes only from faith and communion with God.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:1
text: Enjoy pleasure; the Preacher here records his next experiment, which was to find good in the pleasures of sense.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:3
text:
Yet acquainting my heart with wisdom;  Ecclesiastes 1:13  that is, as he says in  Ecclesiastes 2:9 , "my wisdom remained with me."  He pursued pleasure with discretion, as an earnest man who was seeking to find what is the true good. 
 
  To lay hold on folly; by folly he means the pleasures of sense.  On these he laid hold, that he might learn what good they had to bestow.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:8
text: The peculiar treasure of kings and of the provinces; that is, treasure contributed by kings and by the provinces.  I Kings 4:21 Exodus 19:5

title: Ecclesiastes 2:11
text: God gave to Solomon all of this world that heart could wish, with wisdom to enjoy it in the highest degree.  Yet, after a full experience, he pronounced the whole to be "vanity and vexation of spirit."
