text: Concerning Egypt; when God overthrew Egypt before Israel.

title: Isaiah 23:6
text: Pass ye over; in flight from the enemy.

title: Isaiah 23:8
text:
The crowning city; the city that dispensed crowns to the rulers of her colonies. 
 
When God intrusts to men princely wealth, he requires them to use it in his fear and to his glory.  If they make it the minister of luxury and ostentation, he will either take it from them, as he did from the merchants of Tyre, or in other ways make it a curse to them instead of a blessing.

title: Isaiah 23:9
text: The tendency of long continued success is to nourish the spirit of pride and self-sufficiency.  Thus the prosperity of cities and nations is often the occasion of lifting them up to their destruction.

title: Isaiah 23:10
text:
As a river; freely, without constraint. 
 
  Strength; literally, "girdle," that is, band of authority, by which Tarshish was kept in subjection to Tyre.

title: Isaiah 23:11
text: He; Jehovah.

title: Isaiah 23:12
text: Arise, pass over to Chittim; in flight from the enemy.  See note,  Isaiah 23:1 .

title: Isaiah 23:13
text:
This people; the Chaldeans, here named as the nation which God employed to destroy Tyre.  This city was taken by the Chaldean monarch Nebuchadnezzar, after a severe siege,  Ezekiel 29:18 . 
 
  Founded it; the Chaldean land. 
 
  For them that dwell in the wilderness; the Assyrians seem to have planted a colony of rude mountaineers in the plain of Babylon, who afterwards made themselves masters of the whole region and founded the Chaldean empire. 
 
  Set up the towers--raised up the palaces thereof; some refer these words to Babylon, others to Tyre.  The latter render the clause thus: "they," the Chaldeans, "have set up their" besieging "towers;" "they have made naked her palaces." 
 
  He brought it; the Chaldeans brought Tyre. 
 
God has often raised a feeble and despised people to power and dominion, and made it the minister of his vengeance upon wicked nations.

title: Isaiah 23:15
text:
According to the days of one king; the days of his natural life,  Psalms 90:10 ; here taken as a measure of the duration of the Babylonian kingdom till its overthrow by Cyrus.  Compare  Jeremiah 25:11-12 . 
 
  Shall Tyre sing as a harlot; because she is restored to her former prosperity.  The commerce of Tyre with the nations is represented in this and the following verses under the figure of harlotry.

title: Isaiah 23:18
text:
Holiness to the Lord; the Lord will make her gains subservient to the welfare of his own people. 
 
  Laid up; without use, as a hoarded treasure. 
 
The wealth of all nations is the Lord's; and he will, in one way or another, make it subservient to the advancement of his kingdom among men.

title: Isaiah 24:1
text:
This chapter is intimately connected with the three following.  Though it relates to God's covenant people,  Isaiah 24:5 , its application should not be restricted to the literal Israel.  In the desolations which God brought upon his chosen people for their sins, it had only its incipient fulfilment.  It covers all the judgments by which he purifies his church from sin, and thus prepares the way for her future enlargement and peace, as foretold in the succeeding chapters. 
 
  The earth; or the land, here the land of Palestine, as the residence of God's covenant people.  Compare  Isaiah 24:5 . 
 
vv 1-12. 
 
God has many times brought upon his people for their sins such desolations as seemed to threaten their utter destruction.  But these have all been overruled for the purification and enlargement of the true Zion.  Thus she has been from age to age steadily advancing, through fiery trials, towards that permanent peace and prosperity which awaits her in the latter day glory.

title: Isaiah 24:5
text:
Changed the ordinance; violated the ordinance of God. 
 
  The everlasting covenant; the covenant made with Abraham and his seed for ever.   Genesis 17:1

title: Isaiah 24:10
text: The city of confusion; or, "of emptiness;" that is, Jerusalem, so called because she is to be made desolate.

title: Isaiah 24:11
text: Crying for wine; on account of the failure of wine.  The failure of wine represents a general famine.

title: Isaiah 24:13
text:
As the shaking of an olive-tree--the gleaning grapes; that is, a small remnant.  Compare  Isaiah 17:5-6 . 
 
vv 13-15. 
 
The terrible judgments which consume hypocrites and sinners in Zion, bring salvation to "the Israel of God."

title: Isaiah 24:14
text: They; this remnant that is left, after God's judgments.

title: Isaiah 24:15
text: The fires; or, "the sunrisings," that is, the east, as opposed to "the isles of the sea," in the west.  The remnant of "God's people are called upon to praise him from the different regions of their abode, because the mighty judgments described in this chapter are preparing the way for their redemption.

title: Isaiah 24:16
text:
We heard songs; the songs of the ransomed remnant. 
 
  My leanness; the words of Jerusalem, contrasting her desolate condition with this "glory to the righteous."  Then follows a new picture of her desolateness, with new threatenings of God's judgments.

title: Isaiah 24:18
text:
The windows from on high; as at the deluge, to pour down God's wrath. 
 
How vain are all the efforts of wicked men to escape God's righteous judgments.  When they flee from one calamity, he can easily plunge them into another and a deeper; and if they persist in impenitence, they must fall at last into the bottomless pit, whence they shall not rise again for ever.

title: Isaiah 24:20
text: Removed; literally, "shaken," made to swing to and fro.

title: Isaiah 24:21
text:
The host of the high ones--kings of the earth; all the host of heaven in a figurative sense; wicked powers, that abuse the authority which God has intrusted to them for the good of his church. 
 
vv 21-22. 
 
When men persist in abusing the power which God has intrusted to them for the good of his church, he will take from them their authority and give it to others.  So he dealt with the Jewish rulers at the Babylonian captivity, and at our Lord's advent; and so he will continue to deal in all ages.

title: Isaiah 24:22
text: Visited; having been for "many days" humbled on account of their sins, they shall be again visited in mercy.  This promise is fulfilled, not to them personally, but to their successors in office.  The honor and authority conferred upon Ezra, Nehemiah, Zerubbabel, and others, after the captivity, were only an earnest of its complete accomplishment in Christ, and those whom he appoints to administer the affairs of his kingdom in his name.  Compare  Isaiah 60:17 .

title: Isaiah 24:23
text: Confounded--ashamed; their splendor shall be lost in the glory of God on mount Zion.

title: Isaiah 25:1
text:
I will exalt thee; the prophet, in the name of the true Israel, praises God for the glorious issue of his judgments recorded in the preceding chapter. 
 
All God's counsels towards his covenant people are "faithfulness and truth."  It is only the narrowness of our vision that prevents our discerning his loving kindness in the discipline to which he subjects his church, as well as in the deliverance and enlargement which he from time to time vouchsafes to her.

title: Isaiah 25:2
text:
A city; Babylon, in the primary application of the words.  This city represents here, as often elsewhere, every great persecuting power. 
 
  Strangers; foreigners and heathen. 
 
The efforts of mighty principalities and powers to destroy God's kingdom, end in their own utter and final overthrow.

title: Isaiah 25:3
text:
Therefore; in view of thy judgments on Babylon. 
 
  City of the terrible nations; a metropolis, like Nineveh, Babylon, or Rome, that rules over terrible nations. 
 
God will inflict upon the persecutors of his people such terrible judgments as shall compel all nations to fear him and acknowledge his almighty power.   Exodus 9:16 Revelation of John 11:13

title: Isaiah 25:4
text:
A shadow from the heat; in the burning desert, where such a shadow is rarely found.   Isaiah 4:6 Isaiah 32:2  
 
  The blast of the terrible ones; an invasion of fierce enemies, compared to a violent storm. 
 
In all times of distress God is a sure refuge to his people.  Under the shadow of his protection, they can pass unharmed through the burning desert of affliction and persecution.

title: Isaiah 25:5
text:
Bring down; make quiet. 
 
  The noise of strangers; their battle-shout. 
 
  The branch; the power of the enemy, compared, as in  Isaiah 10:33 , to a stately bough; but we may better render, "the song."

title: Isaiah 25:6
text:
vv 6-8. 
 
  This mountain; Zion, which here represents the church of Christ. 
 
  Wines on the lees; wines that have been left to stand on their lees have a richer flavor. 
 
  Face of the covering; the veil of ignorance with its attendant sin and wretchedness. 
 
  In victory; literally, "for ever." 
 
  Rebuke of his people; to which his people have been subject.  The swallowing up of death is its abolition in the widest sense.  The prophet's vision extends not only into, but beyond the era of millennial glory.  He has a view of the final issue of Christ's redemption in this world and in eternity. 
 
The power of the gospel to bless men passes all human comprehension. It fills the heart that receives it with light and peace and joy; it makes every nation that obeys it prosperous and happy; it will one day unite all the families of the earth in harmony and blessedness.

title: Isaiah 25:7
text: The covenant made with Abraham was from the beginning designed to bless all nations; and this design Christ will gloriously accomplish.  He will make the light of his gospel shine from mount Zion into every land, till the earth is filled with the knowledge of the Lord as the waters cover the sea.   Isaiah 11:9

title: Isaiah 25:8
text: In the coming millennial age, a more glorious order of society awaits the world than our darkened understandings are able to conceive of; and this will be but an earnest of the perfect redemption of heaven, where God will in the fullest sense of the words swallow up death for ever, and wipe away tears from off all faces.

title: Isaiah 25:10
text:
The hand of the Lord; his omnipotent power. 
 
  Moab; named as a prominent enemy of God's people in the prophet's day, representing every hostile power. 
 
The day is coming when the persecutors of God's church, who were once so terrible to her, shall be known and remembered only by the record of the judgments which have destroyed them.

title: Isaiah 25:11
text:
He shall spread forth his hands in the midst of them; Jehovah, to execute vengeance upon his enemies. 
 
  As he that swimmeth; widely and on all sides. 
 
  Spoils; or "plots."

title: Isaiah 25:12
text: Thy walls; Moab's walls.

title: Isaiah 26:1
text:
In that day; in the day referred to at the close of the preceding chapter. 
 
  A strange city; Zion, in contrast with the fortress of the enemy that has been destroyed. 
 
The same almighty power which overthrows the enemies of Zion, is to her an impregnable bulwark of defence.

title: Isaiah 26:2
text: The gates; of this strong city.

title: Isaiah 26:3
text: True faith in God brings assurance and peace to the soul in all circumstances of prosperity or adversity.

title: Isaiah 26:6
text: The poor and needy who put their trust in God shall eventually triumph over their persecutors, however mighty the power  which they array against them.

title: Isaiah 26:8
text: In the way of thy judgments; God's judgments are here, as in  Isaiah 26:9 , the jedgments by which he destroys his enemies and saves his own people.  To wait for him in the way of these judgments, is to wait in earnest expectation and prayer for their manifestation, since thus the "inhabitants of the world will learn righteousness."

title: Isaiah 26:9
text: Have I desired thee; desired thee to manifest thyself in thy judgments.

title: Isaiah 26:10
text:
vv 10-11. 
 
So incorrigible is the human heart, that God often sees it needful to employ many and sore judgments, with the power of his Spirit, to bring it to consideration and repentance.

title: Isaiah 26:11
text: The fire of thine enemies; the fire with which thou consumest thine enemies.

title: Isaiah 26:12
text:
In us; rather, "for us;" thou hast helped us, and given us success in all our works.  The prophet teaches that salvation is from God's hand. 
 
vv 12-15. 
 
If God's people cleave to him in faith and patience, he will in due time destroy their foes, and make even their memory to perish from among men.

title: Isaiah 26:13
text:
Other lords; the heathen rulers, with the additional idea, that they have also worshipped their false gods. 
 
  By thee only; by calling upon thee alone. 
 
  Make mention; in the way of divine worship.

title: Isaiah 26:14
text: They are dead; the "other lords."   Isaiah 26:13

title: Isaiah 26:15
text:
The nation; Israel. 
 
  Thou hadst removed--the ends of the earth; many prefer to render, "thou hast removed far off all the bounds of the land," that is, enlarged it on every side.

title: Isaiah 26:16
text: It is a most blessed fruit of God's chastening hand, that it makes his children more frequent and earnest in their visits to his mercy seat, and thus brings them into nearer communion with him.

title: Isaiah 26:18
text:
Brought forth wind--not wrought any deliverance; God's people confess the vanity of all their endeavors to save themselves. 
 
  Inhabitants of the world; the gentile nations that have oppressed us. 
 
God sometimes leaves his people for a season to the spirit of self-reliance, that they may learn how vain are all efforts to obtain deliverance without his presence and power.

title: Isaiah 26:19
text:
Thy dead; the dead of God's people.  The life-giving power of Jehovah is now set in strong contrast with the weakness of man. 
 
  Together with my dead body shall thy arise; or, "my dead bodies shall arise," God's people being the speaker. 
 
  Thy dew; the dew, that is, the quickening power that descends upon God's people. 
 
  Is as the dew of herbs; has, like the dew falling on herbs, a life-giving power. 
 
Some understand this verse of a spiritual resurection, compare  Ezekiel 37:1-14 ; others, of the resurrection of the body, and this seems to have been the interpretation of the ancient Jews.  We may reasonably believe that the Spirit of prophecy intended to give here an intimation of this great doctrine, which contains in itself the pledge of all needful previous help and deliverance. 
 
As Christ triumphed over death and hell in his own resurrection, and will at the last day make all his people triumphant over both, he must be able to grant them all needed help and delivernace in their present conflict with the powers of darkness.

title: Isaiah 26:20
text:
vv 20-21. 
 
  Come, my people--until the indignation be overpast--the Lord cometh out of his place; the prophet intimates that a season of affliction must first be passed through, whole God is executing his judgments upon the earth.  From these he exhorts the people of God to hide themselves in their chambers, by a submissive and patient waiting upon him in faith and obedience. 
 
When God's church makes herself a partaker with the wicked in their sins, she must also share the judgments which God sends upon them.  But all who hide themselves in the chamber of obedient and submissive faith, are safe in times of calamity.

title: Isaiah 27:1
text:
Leviathan; in the primary application of the prophecy, Babylon, under the similitude of a sea-dragon.  But Babylon stands here as the representative of all great persecuting powers. 
 
All principalities and powers that oppose themselves to God's kingdom are contending against omnipotence, and their end must be utter destruction.

title: Isaiah 27:2
text: Unto her; unto Zion.

title: Isaiah 27:3
text: Since God is himself the founder of the church, and has promised to her his presence and protection to the end of the world, his honor and faithfulness are pledged to guard her from all injury.

title: Isaiah 27:4
text:
Fury is not in me; my anger toward Zion is over.  Compare  Isaiah 54:8 . 
 
  Who would set; or "who will set:" in these words God challenges his and Zion's foes to the combat.

title: Isaiah 27:5
text:
Or let him take hold of my strength; that is, if the enemy, represented under the similitude of briers and thorns, would escape my vengeance, let him take hold of my strength.  To take hold of God's strength, is to submit ourselves to his almighty power in faith and obedience. 
 
The alternative which God presents alike to individuals and to nations is, that they may make their peace with him, or be destroyed by his judgments.

title: Isaiah 27:7
text:
Hath he smitten him--smote him? hath God smitten Israel as he smote those that smote Israel? 
 
  Is he slain? is Israel slain? 
 
  Them that are slain by him? literally, "his slain," which seems to mean those whom God has slain in Israel's behalf. 
 
vv 7-11. 
 
God's incorrigible enemies shall have judgment without mercy, to their destruction; but his covenant people he chastises in measure, for their purification and future enlargement.

title: Isaiah 27:8
text:
In measure; in moderation. 
 
  When it shooteth forth; or, "when thou sendest it," thy wrath, "forth." 
 
  Debate with it; rebuke it, as it were; check it, lest it should be too severe. 
 
  Stayeth; moderateth.  Many prefer to render this verse thus: "In measure when he sendeth her," Zion, "away, will he contend with her: he taketh her away with his hard wind in the day of his east wind."

title: Isaiah 27:9
text:
By this; by the chastisements described in the preceding verse. 
 
  Maketh all the stones--beaten in sunder; demolishes the idolatrous altar of Jacob.  "Chalk-stones," or "stones of lime," which easily crumble. 
 
  Groves; rather, images of Ashtoreth. 
 
  Images; the original word properly denotes images of Baal.

title: Isaiah 27:10
text:
Yet; in the original, "for." 
 
  The defenced city; Jerusalem.  The prophet continues his account of God's purifying judgments upon his people. 
 
  The branches thereof; of Judah, represented under the similitude of a tree.  There is here a blending of the literal with the figurative.

title: Isaiah 27:11
text: Set them on fire; burn them for fuel.

title: Isaiah 27:12
text:
Beat off; beat off olive-berries; that is, glean, as it were, his people, by gathering them one by one from their dispersion. 
 
  The river; the Euphrates. 
 
vv 12-13. 
 
The final result of God's judgments in this world shall be the establishment of Christ's kingdom over all the earth, and the deliverance of his people from violence and oppression of every kind. But this will be only preparatory to a higher triumph "at the resurrection of the just," when Christ "shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other," to worship the Lord in the new Jerusalem for ever.

title: Isaiah 27:13
text: The great trumpet shall be blown; to call together God's people from their dispersion.  How far this prophecy shall be literally fulfilled to "Israel after the flesh," cannot be known beforehand.  But it covers a promise to the spiritual Israel of complete deliverance and salvation.

title: Isaiah 28:1
text:
To the drunkards of Ephraim; rather, "of the drunkards of Ephraim;" and so in  Isaiah 28:3 . 
 
  Which are on the head; for "are," which is supplied by the translators, we may better put "is," making the clause refer to the "glorious beauty" of "the drunkards of Ephraim," is Samaria, the capital of the kingdom of Israel.  This city was "on the head of the fat valleys" of these drunkards, as it lay on the summit of a hill surrounded by fertile valleys. 
 
vv 1,3,7. 
 
Crimes and abuses of every kind follow in the train of drunkenness. When the rulers of a people are addicted to this sin, they will pervert truth and righteousness, and bring upon themselves and their country the just judgments of God.

title: Isaiah 28:2
text:
A mighty and strong one; a mighty conqueror whom he will send against Samaria. 
 
  With the hand; with a violent hand.   II Kings 18:10-11

title: Isaiah 28:4
text: Hasty fruit; the early figs, which were esteemed a great delicacy.

title: Isaiah 28:5
text: Unto the residue of his people; while Ephraim's "crown of pride" is destroyed, God will be himself "a crown of glory" and "a diadem of beauty," to the remnant of his people in Jerusalem.

title: Isaiah 28:6
text: To the gate; back to the gate of the enemy.

title: Isaiah 28:7
text: But they also have erred; the people of Judah, as well as of Ephraim.

title: Isaiah 28:9
text:
vv 9-10. 
 
  Whom shall he teach--there a little; it is generally agreed that these are the scoffing words of the Jews, complaining that the prophet multiplies his precepts to them as if they were babes.

title: Isaiah 28:11
text: With stammering lips; this is God's answer to the scoffers.  Since they stammer, that is, scoff at the prophet's message, God will teach them by stammering lips, that is, by giving them up to the power of stammering foreigners.  In the Hebrew, to stammer, to scoff, and to speak in a foreign tongue, are all expressed by the same verb.  Compare  Isaiah 33:19 .

title: Isaiah 28:12
text: This is the rest; faith in God and obedience to his law.

title: Isaiah 28:13
text: The word of the Lord was unto them; God has indeed multiplied his precepts to them as to children, but with no other result than their increased wickedness and more aggravated ruin. Compare  Isaiah 6:9-10 Isaiah 18:7 .

title: Isaiah 28:15
text:
Covenant with death--with hell--at agreement; the covenant is, that death and hell shall not injure them.  This they say not in word, but in spirit and action.  They are confident that their lying devices will save them. 
 
In nothing does the desperate wickedness of men more clearly manifest itself than in the delusions which they practise upon themselves in respect to escaping the punishment of their sins.  Every transgressor has some "refuge of lies" in which he hopes to be saved, though he neglects the only way of salvation which God has provided for him.

title: Isaiah 28:16
text:
A sure foundation; the Messiah, who is here contrasted with the vain refuges of these scoffers. 
 
  Make haste; flee in terror, as the wicked must from their refuges of lies.   II Peter 2:6  
 
vv 16-20. 
 
Jesus Christ is the one foundation which God has laid in Zion for sinners.  They who build upon him their hopes for eternity shall never be put to shame; but the hail and tempest of the last day shall sweep away every hiding-place of man's invention.

title: Isaiah 28:17
text: Judgment--to the line--righteousness to the plummet; proceed with exact justice, not sparing the guilty.

title: Isaiah 28:19
text: From the time that it goeth forth; or, "as often as it," the scourge, "passeth over."

title: Isaiah 28:20
text: The bed--the covering; their lying devices, to which they trusted for deliverance.

title: Isaiah 28:21
text:
Mount Perazim; see  II Samuel 5:20 I Chronicles 14:11 . 
 
  The valley of Gibeon; the reference is either to  Joshua 10:12 , or to  I Chronicles 14:16 . 
 
  Strange; unheard of, extraordinary.  What the "strange work" is,  Isaiah 28:22 .

title: Isaiah 28:22
text:
The whole earth; the whole land of Judea.  The original word means both "earth" and "land." 
 
They who scoff at God's judgments will soon find themselves entangled in them, with no power either to escape or endure them.

title: Isaiah 28:24
text:
vv 24-28. 
 
  Doth the ploughman plough--bruise it with his horsemen; the husbandman does not always plough, he also sows; his different seeds he arranges each in the right place; in threshing he pursues different modes according to the nature of the grain: much more, then, must God, who gives to the husbandman all his skill, adapt his dealings with men to their different characters and circumstances, as the case may demand.  The interference from this is, that the righteous will be finally saved, and the incorrigibly wicked in due time destroyed.

title: Isaiah 28:29
text: This also; this wisdom of the husbandman.  How much deeper, then, must be the wisdom of God himself.

title: Isaiah 29:1
text:
This chapter contains prophecies of heavy judgments upon Jerusalem, mingled with promises of final sanctification and deliverance.  These are arranged in two series, the first terminating with  Isaiah 29:8 . Its immediate occasion seems to have been the invasion of Sennacherib; but it looks beyond that event to the general course and final issue of God's dealings with his covenant people.  Hence both our Saviour and the apostle Paul apply its words to their own times. 
 
  Ariel; a symbolical name for Jerusalem.  According to some, "the lion of God," as denoting the invincible might with which God endowed her so long as she continued faithful to him; according to others, "the altar of God," as in  Ezekiel 43:15  with a double allusion to the altar of burnt-offering and the consuming fire of God's wrath.  The latter view is to be preferred. 
 
  Add ye year to year; go on with your round of formal services.  Isaiah 29:13  
 
  Let them kill sacrifices; or, "let the feasts go their round." 
 
vv 1-8. 
 
God controls the movements of all nations for the good of his church. He can with equal case subject her to their power, for her chastisement and purification, or make her victorious over them for her enlargement and the glory of his own name.

title: Isaiah 29:2
text: It shall be unto me as Ariel; an altar on which I will consume the wicked.

title: Isaiah 29:4
text: Brought down--whisper out of the dust; the allusion seems to be to the necromancers, who claimed that their call to the spirits of the dead was answered out of the voice of the necromancers themselves, through the art of ventriloquism.  The prophet means, that Jerusalem shall be greatly humbled, and shall whisper in the tones of weakness and fear.

title: Isaiah 29:5
text:
vv 5-8. 
 
These verses describe the sudden dispersion of the enemy and the disappointment of their hopes. 
 
  Thy strangers; the foreign armies arrayed against thee. 
 
  Like small dust--as chaff; suddenly scattered. 
 
  Visited of the Lord of hosts; the visitation is for Jerusalem's deliverance. 
 
  As a dream of a night vision; the hopes of Zion's enemies shall vanish like the dreams of the hungry and thirsty.

title: Isaiah 29:9
text:
Stay yourselves; stand fixed in amazement at the calamities which shall soon come upon you.  The prophet returns to his denunciations upon the people of Jerusalem. 
 
  Cry ye out, and cry; from terror and anguish.  Or, according to many, "take your pleasure, and be blind." 
 
  But not with wine; it is a spiritual drunkenness. 
 
vv 9-12. 
 
When the teachers and rulers of the church are blind, the people will be sunk in vice and ignorance.   Matthew 15:14

title: Isaiah 29:10
text: Hath he covered; blinded.

title: Isaiah 29:11
text:
vv 11-12. 
 
  The vision of all; all the revelations of God through his prophets. 
 
  Is sealed--I am not learned; that is, none, whether learned or unlearned, can understand and interpret God's messages.

title: Isaiah 29:13
text:
Fear toward me; worship of me. 
 
  Taught by the precept of men; regulated by human authority. Compare  Matthew 15:7-9 Mark 7:6-7 . 
 
God alone has the right to prescribe the way in which he is to worshipped.  All systems of religion that rest on human authority and tradition are empty and formal; they lead to hypocrisy and wickedness, and bring upon men God's displeasure instead of his favor.

title: Isaiah 29:14
text:
A marvellous work--shall be hid; marvellous judgments, such as shall make the wisdom of man of no avail. 
 
Human wisdom is alike impotent to deliver men from God's judgments in this world, and to provide for them a way of justification and eternal life.

title: Isaiah 29:15
text: Seek deep to hide their counsel; seek to hide their counsel as it were in deep recesses, thinking that God does not see them.  These are the men who make lies their refuge, and falsehood their hiding-place.  Isaiah 28:15

title: Isaiah 29:16
text:
Surely your turning--shall the work say; or, "your perverseness! Shall the potter be esteemed as clay,that the work should say," etc. 
 
Since God is the author of human reason, his wisdom cannot be arraigned at its bar, any more than the potter can be called to an account by the clay which he fashions.

title: Isaiah 29:17
text:
Lebanon shall be turned--esteemed as a forest; that is, the high shall be abased and the lowly exalted, as explained in  Isaiah 29:18-24 . 
 
vv 17-24. 
 
The desolating judgments of God work together with his word and Spirit for the enlargement and peace of Zion.  Amid the overthrow of empires without her borders, and the destruction of hypocrites within, the kingdom of Christ is steadily advancing towards universal dominion.

title: Isaiah 29:18
text: The eyes of the blind shall see; compare  Matthew 4:16 John 9:39 .

title: Isaiah 29:20
text: Watch for iniquity; for the opportunity of doing wrong.

title: Isaiah 29:21
text:
Make a man an offender for a word; or, "condemn a man," that is, a righteous man, "in a cause." 
 
  Turn aside the just; deprive him of justice.

title: Isaiah 29:22
text:
vv 22-24. 
 
  Jacob; the "Israel of God." 
 
  They shall sanctify; Jacob and his children; that is, the church and her spiritual offering.

title: Isaiah 30:1
text:
In this and the following chapter, the prophet rebukes the Jews for resorting to Egypt, rather than to the living God, for help against the Assyrians.  The occasion was the invasion of Sennacherib; but here, as in the preceding chapter, he looks far beyond that event to the final issue of God's dealings with his covenant people. 
 
  Cover with a covering; protect themselves against their foes.  Some render, "make a league." 
 
vv 1-7. 
 
"An evil heart of unbelief in departing from the living God." is the great sin of the human race.  This has in all ages led nations and families, as well as individuals, to seek help in trouble from man rather than from God, and always to their disappointment and ruin.

title: Isaiah 30:4
text:
His princes--ambassadors; Judah's princes and ambassodors. 
 
  Zoan; in lower Egypt. 
 
  Hanes; in middle Egypt.

title: Isaiah 30:5
text: They were all ashamed; Judah's ambassadors.

title: Isaiah 30:6
text:
The burden of the beasts of the south; "the beasts of the south" are the beasts which carry the treasures of Judah into the south, that is, into Egypt, for the purpose of securing the alliance and help of the Egyptians.  In the word "burden" there is a double allusion, first to the load of treasures, secondly to the threatened wrath of God upon the undertaking. 
 
  The land of trouble--fiery flying serpent; a description of the southern desert, through which the road to Egypt lies.

title: Isaiah 30:7
text: Their strength is to sit still; their boasted help ends in their doing nothing.

title: Isaiah 30:8
text:
vv 8-14. 
 
Wicked men desire to hear not what is true, but what will flatter them in their sins.  Thus they reject the only way of salvation, and bring upon themselves irremedible ruin.

title: Isaiah 30:11
text: Cause the Holy One of Israel to cease; let us hear no more concerning him.

title: Isaiah 30:13
text:
This iniquity; the iniquity described in the preceding verses, the root of which is an unbelieving spirit. 
 
  Shall be to you as a breach--in a high wall; this sin shall make Judah like a falling wall, which swells out gradually more and more, and at last falls suddenly.  The "breach" here is the broken part of the wall.

title: Isaiah 30:14
text:
He shall break it; God shall break the wall, which represents the Jewish state. 
 
  A sherd; a broken piece of the vessel. 
 
  To take fire--to take water; large enough for these purposes.

title: Isaiah 30:15
text:
Returning and rest; returning to God and resting in his promises. 
 
They who, in times of trouble and danger, honor God with the full confidence of their souls, shall receive from him inward peace and comfort, and also outward deliverance, so far as their highest welfare requires it.

title: Isaiah 30:16
text:
We will flee; will escape from the enemy. 
 
  Shall ye flee; fly before the enemy. 
 
When men refuse to give God their confidence, he makes their devices for obtaining deliverance the means of their destruction.

title: Isaiah 30:17
text: A beacon--ensign; standing solitary and desolate.

title: Isaiah 30:18
text:
Therefore; because in God is salvation,  Isaiah 30:15 , and in man's help is only disappointment and ruin,  Isaiah 30:1-7 . 
 
  Wait, that he may be gracious--be exalted, that he may have mercy; God's long-suffering, and the manifestation of his greatness, both have for their end to bring men, through repentance, to the enjoyment of his forgiving love. 
 
  Judgment; righteousness and faithfulness.

title: Isaiah 30:19
text: The people; the pious remnant.  The prophet, after his usual manner, turns from threatenings to promises.

title: Isaiah 30:20
text: The most prosperous days of God's people have often been those of great temporal suffering.  It is far better to have spiritual life and health with outward affliction, than worldly prosperity with spiritual darkness and deadness.

title: Isaiah 30:21
text:
A word behind thee; the voice of God following them in their wanderings from duty. 
 
They who faithfully attend to the monitions of God's word and providence, will not fall into dangerous error.

title: Isaiah 30:22
text:
Covering--ornament; the overlaying of silver or gold, which is mentioned as the most valuable part of the idol.  They defile them by casting them away with abhorrence as unclean things. 
 
vv 22-23. 
 
Repentance, and fruits worthy of repentance, bring a return of God's favor.

title: Isaiah 30:24
text:
Ear; plough. 
 
  Clean; or, "savory."  The abundance and good quality of the provender are an emblem of the universal plenty that prevails.

title: Isaiah 30:25
text:
Rivers and streams; filling them with verdure and fruitfulness. 
 
  In the day of the great slaughter; here, as elsewhere, this golden age of the church is represented as introduced by the slaughter of God's foes. 
 
  Towers; of the enemy.

title: Isaiah 30:26
text:
As the light of the sun--sevenfold; this is the era of millennial glory, perhaps also with a reference to the perfect blessedness of heaven.  Compare  Isaiah 60:19-22 . 
 
The universal prevalence of the gospel among men will fill the world with such light and gladness as we are unable to conceive of, and all this will be but a foretaste of the eternal blessedness of heaven.

title: Isaiah 30:27
text:
vv 27-32. 
 
The same divine judgments which destroy the wicked, bring gladness and salvation to the righteous.

title: Isaiah 30:28
text:
His breath; his anger, which is compared to an overflowing stream. 
 
  Reach to the midst of the neck; a proverbial expression for imminent danger.   Isaiah 8:8  
 
  The sieve of vanity; the sieve of perdition. 
 
  A bridle--causing them to err; the bridle is the delusions which lead them astray, here represented as a judgment proceeding from God. Compare  II Thessalonians 2:11 .

title: Isaiah 30:29
text:
Ye shall have a song; God's people, when he thus destroys their foes. 
 
  Into the mountain of the Lord; to celebrate there the yearly festivals.

title: Isaiah 30:31
text: The Assyrian; Sennacherib.

title: Isaiah 30:32
text:
The grounded staff; the ordained rod. 
 
  Shall pass; upon the Assyrian. 
 
  With taberets and harps; on the part of God's people. 
 
  Battles of shaking; tumultuous battles. 
 
  He fight with it; God, against Assyria.

title: Isaiah 30:33
text:
Topet; the funeral pile for God's enemies, in allusion to Topet, where the idolatrous Jews offered their children as burnt-sacrifices to Moloch.   II Kings 23:10  
 
  For the king; for Jehovah.  Under this terrible image is represented the final vengeance of God upon his foes, of which their temporal destruction is but the beginning. Compare  Matthew 5:22 Mark 9:43-48 . 
 
The terrible effects of God's wrath in this world are a solemn foreshadowing of its power in that prison of despair "where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched."

title: Isaiah 31:1
text: God deals with his covenant people in such a manner as to manifest at once the vanity of all earthly resources, and his own omnipotent power and immutable faithfulness.  When he has withdrawn their confidence from every arm of flesh, he sends them salvation from his own presence.

title: Isaiah 31:4
text: So shall the Lord of hosts come down; having declared the vanity of all reliance on human aid, God now promises to defend Jerusalem by his own almighty power.

title: Isaiah 31:5
text: As birds flying;hovering over and protecting their young in the nest.   Deuteronomy 32:11

title: Isaiah 31:8
text:
Not of a mighty man--not of a mean man; by the immediate stroke of God.   Isaiah 37:36  
 
  From the sword; before Jehovah's wrath, represented as a destroying sword.

title: Isaiah 31:9
text:
To his strong-hold; to his own city, Nineveh. 
 
  The ensign; Jehovah's ensign, the symbol of his presence.  Compare  Isaiah 5:26 . 
 
  Fire--furnace; see note on  Isaiah 29:1 .

title: Isaiah 32:1
text:
In this and the three following chapters promises and threatenings are mingled together.  Mighty judgments are coming upon sinners in Zion, and upon her enemies without; but amid all these, Christ's kingdom shall advance to its final establishment over all the earth.  Though the immediate occasion of these prophecies may have been the invasion of Sennacherib, they cannot be restricted to that event.  They cover the whole history of the church. 
 
  A king; the Messiah.  The word applies to earthly rulers of the church, such as Hezekiah, only so far as they have Christ's spirit, and exercise their authority under him. 
 
  Princes; under the king. 
 
From the beginning to the end of time, Christ is to his church the source of life and strength and wisdom and holiness.  From him alone are her rulers replenished with grace, and enabled to administer her affairs "in judgment," for the glory of God and her edification.

title: Isaiah 32:2
text: A man; the king spoken of in the preceding verse.

title: Isaiah 32:3
text:
vv 3-8. 
 
  Shall not be dim--shall he stand; the general meaning is, that knowledge shall take the place of ignorance and men shall no longer "call evil good and good evil."   Isaiah 5:20  
 
  The rash--the stammerers; those who are rash and stammer in their judgment of spiritual things. 
 
  The churl; a man destitute alike of truth and mercy, as is plain from the prophet's description. 
 
vv 3-5. The religion of Christ, by purifying the affections of the heart, removes the great source of error, and enables men to judge correctly of moral principles and actions.  In this way the general prevalence of the gospel corrects public sentiment, and maintains it in a healthful condition.  But whenever irreligion prevails, perverse opinions and wicked practices go hand in hand.

title: Isaiah 32:9
text:
vv 9-12. 
 
  Rise up, ye women--the fruitful vine; a threatening against "the daughters of Zion" similiar to that in  Isaiah 3:16-24 . 
 
  The vintage shall fail; because of the invasion of the enemy. Compare  Isaiah 32:13-14 . 
 
  They shall lament for the teats; literally, "for the breasts," that is, the full breasts which have supplied nourishment to their infants. Food shall be wanting for mother and offspring. 
 
Luxury, idleness, and prodigality in females are heinous sins in the sight of God.  They exert a powerful influence to corrupt public morals, and thus bring upon nations and families those heavy judgments in which woman has so large a share of suffering.

title: Isaiah 32:13
text:
Thorns and briers; because it is left desolate and untilled. Compare  Isaiah 7:23 . 
 
vv 13-18. The downward tendency of human nature mainfests itself in the church of Christ, as well as in the world.  But among his own people, God will not allow error and corruption to gain the victory.  In the midst of his judgments he will from time to time pour upon them his Spirit from on high, renovating their faith, and producing a new and abundant harvest of the fruits of righteousness.

title: Isaiah 32:14
text:
Forts and towers; literally, "Ophel and tower," that is, Ophel and its tower.  Ophel is a ridge extending south from the ancient temple area. 
 
  For ever; not absolutely, but through a long period of time, as the next verse shows.

title: Isaiah 32:15
text: Wilderness--a forest; see note on  Isaiah 29:17 .

title: Isaiah 32:19
text:
Coming down on the forest; or "in the fall of the forest."  "The forest" represents the pride and strength of the enemy.  Compare Isa 10.18-19,33-34. 
 
  The city; the city of the enemy--Nineveh, Babylon, and all like persecuting powers to the end of time. 
 
vv 19-20. The destruction of Satan's power, and the establishment of Christ's kingdom, are inseparably connected in God's plan, and shall be effected by the same instrumentalities.

title: Isaiah 32:20
text: Blessed are ye; that is, "my people."   Isaiah 32:18   The quiet and peaceful pursuit of agriculture is here a symbol for prosperity, temporal and spiritual.

title: Isaiah 33:1
text:
To thee; Assyria, as the representative of all persecuting powers. 
 
God uses wicked nations, like Assyria and Babylon, as "the rod of his anger," to chastise his people for their sins.  But when he has accomplished this work, he destroys them as easily as he had before raised them to power.

title: Isaiah 33:2
text:
Unto us--their arm; the prophet's prayer for his people in view of the coming trouble.  In the second clause he passes, as is common with the prophets, from the first to the third person. 
 
The repentance and supplication of God's people is the signal of his interposition in their behalf.

title: Isaiah 33:3
text:
The tumult; caused by God's appearance in behalf of his people. 
 
The only stability of a nation is the prevalence among its citizens and in its counsels of wisdom, knowledge, and the fear of the Lord.

title: Isaiah 33:4
text:
Your spoil shall be gathered; the spoil of the Assyrian host by the Jews. 
 
  Like the gathering of the caterpillar; as locusts gather and devour every thing. 
 
  Shall he run upon them; more literally, "shall one run upon it;" that is, upon the spoil of the Assyrians.

title: Isaiah 33:6
text: Thy times--his treasure; the reference is to the Jewish people. Compare note on  Isaiah 33:2 .

title: Isaiah 33:7
text: Shall cry without; the reference probably is to the event recorded in  II Kings 18:37 .

title: Isaiah 33:8
Isaiah 33:9
text: Lebanon is ashamed--shake off their fruits; a figurative description of the desolation caused by the Assyrian invasion.

title: Isaiah 33:11
text:
Ye; the Assyrians. 
 
  Your breath; your proud and impious spirit.

title: Isaiah 33:12
text:
The people; the nations assembled against God's people. 
 
  As the burnings of lime; consumed as by the intense fire of a brick-kiln.

title: Isaiah 33:13
text: What I have done; what I, Jehovah, have done in the destruction of my enemies.  The immediate reference is to the destruction of Sennacherib's host.  But this represents the vengeance that shall fall on all God's enemies to the end of time.

title: Isaiah 33:14
text:
Are afraid; the terrible judgment of God on their enemies fills them with awe. 
 
  Who among us shall dwell; or, can dwell; the words of the hypocrites and sinners.  If such be the power of God's wrath, who can endure its fierce flame for ever? 
 
The terrible judgments of God upon the wicked in this world, are such an earnest of the awful retributions of eternity as ought to fill all sinners with amazement and terror.

title: Isaiah 33:15
text: vv 15-16. The man who makes God his confidence, and obeys his law, is safe amid the most fearful convulsions and revolutions of nations.

title: Isaiah 33:16
text: He shall dwell on high; the same almighty power that has overthrown the enemies of God's people, and filled sinners in Zion with amazement, shall be to the righteous a munition of rocks.

title: Isaiah 33:17
text:
The king in his beauty; the King of Zion in his divine beauty and majesty. 
 
  They shall behold--far off; the probable meaning is, that the righteous no longer shut up and straitened, shall behold distant regions added to God's kingdom.

title: Isaiah 33:18
text:
Shall meditate terror.  Where is the scribe? shall call to mind the former days of terror, exultingly asking, Where is the scribe? etc. The receiver--weigher, margin--and counter of the towers, are those of the Assyrian army. 
 
vv 18-19. Every present deliverance which God vouchsafes to his people is a pledge of all needful future help; and as such it should be remembered with devout thanksgiving and gladness.

title: Isaiah 33:19
text:
Shalt not see; shalt no longer see. 
 
  A stammering tongue; a foreign language.

title: Isaiah 33:20
text:
Shall ever be removed; this promise has its complete fulfilment to the spiritual Jerusalem, the church of God, of which the earthly Jerusalem was the representative. 
 
vv 20-24. Whatever future trials await God's church, the final issue of them all shall be her establishment in perpetual holiness and tranquility.

title: Isaiah 33:21
text:
Will be unto us a place of broad rivers; which give fertility and strength. 
 
  Galley with oars--gallant ship; that is, galley or ship of the enemy.  It shall be a safe river.

title: Isaiah 33:23
text:
Thy tacklings are loosed; the enemy are addressed under the figure of a dismantled ship. 
 
  A great spoil; the spoil of the Assyrian host. 
 
  The lame; among God's people; so powerless are their once victorious enemies.

title: Isaiah 33:24
text:
Inhabitant; of the spiritual Zion. 
 
  Shall be forgiven their iniquity; this promise was fulfilled to the Jews of Hezekiah's day only in a very imperfect sense.  It manifestly looks to the final issue of all God's interpositions in behalf of his church, of which the overthrow of Sennacherib was an illustrious example.

title: Isaiah 34:1
text:
God is about to execute judgments upon the enemies of his people. Among these Edom is specified by name, because of its peculiar enmity to Judah.   Psalms 137:7 Ezekiel 25:12 Obadiah 1:10-14   Its doom, like that of Moab,  Isaiah 25:10 , and that of Philistia, Edom, Moab, and Ammon,  Isaiah 11:14 , stands as a type of the destruction which awaits all the foes of Zion. 
 
The utter and perpetual desolation of the nations that anciently opposed themselves to God's covenant people, is at once a standing memorial of the truth of prophecy, and a terrible type of the destruction that awaits all the enemies of his church.  If such be the power of God's anger in this world, who can endure that "furnace of fire" which "shall not be quenched night nor day," and whose smoke "shall go up for ever?"

title: Isaiah 34:2
text: He hath utterly destroyed them; the prophet speaks of the future desolation as already past, because God had decreed it.

title: Isaiah 34:4
text: The host of heaven shall be dissolved; see note on  Isaiah 13:10 .

title: Isaiah 34:5
text:
Bathed; with the blood of Edom. 
 
  In heaven; because God who wields it is in heaven.

title: Isaiah 34:6
text: Lambs--goats--rams; like "unicorns" and "bullocks" in the next verse, representing the Idumeans under the figure of animals slaughtered for a sacrifice.

title: Isaiah 34:7
text:
Unicorns; probabaly wild buffaloes; that is, the most fierce and mighty among the people. 
 
  Come down; to the slaughter.

title: Isaiah 34:9
text:
vv 9-10. 
 
  Thereof; of Edom. 
 
  Shall be turned into pitch--shall go up for ever; a figurative description of complete desolation, drawn from the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah.

title: Isaiah 34:11
text:
vv 11-15. 
 
  The cormorant--the vultures; compare notes on  Isaiah 13:21-22 . 
 
  He shall stretch out--the stones of emptiness; he shall measure it with line and plummet for utter desolation. 
 
  To the kingdom; that is, to defend and maintain it.

title: Isaiah 34:16
text:
Seek ye out of the book of the Lord; God challenges his people to compare the prophecy with its fulfilment. 
 
  No one of these; these inhabitants of desolated places.

title: Isaiah 34:17
text: Cast the lot for them--divided it--by line; hath allotted it to them for their habitation.

title: Isaiah 35:1
text:
For them; for the judgments inflicted on the enemies of Zion, which prepare the way for her restoration to fertility and beauty. 
 
  The desert shall rejoice, and blossom; under this imagery is foretold the restoration of spiritual prosperity and fruitfulness to Zion.   Isaiah 35:7 Isaiah 41:17 Isaiah 41:19 Isaiah 43:19-20 Isaiah 55:13   Compare also  Isaiah 44:3-5 , where the prophet gives the spiritual meaning of the figure. 
 
vv 1-7. 
 
Egypt, Assyria, Babylon, and Rome, the ancient persecutors of God's church, were once in great power, and spreading themselves on every side.  But they have passed away for ever.  So shall it be with all her enemies, while she shall be built up on their ruins, and shall extend her borders more and more, till the whole earth is through her, filled with the fruits of righteousness.

title: Isaiah 35:5
text:
vv5-6. 
 
  The eyes of the blind shall be opened--the tongue of the dumb sing; these words have their highest fulfilment in the healing of men's spiritual maladies; they include our Lord's miracles only as parts of his whole work of redemption.

title: Isaiah 35:8
text:
There; in the wilderness, heretofore barren and pathless. 
 
  For those; for the "redeemed,"  Isaiah 35:10 . 
 
vv 8-10. 
 
The highway of salvation, cast up by prophets and apostles under God's direction, is both plain and safe.  No honest inquirer after truth can fail to find it, or go astray after he has entered upon it.  It is guarded on both sides by God's presence and power, and all who walk in it shall finally enter the heavenly Jerusalem "with songs and everlasting joy upon their heads."

title: Isaiah 35:10
text: Shall return, and come to Zion; shall return from their captivity by this highway, and come to their home on mount Zion.  The return of God's people from captivity is here an emblem of all the deliverances which he vouchsafes to them in this world, and of their final introduction to the heavenly Zion.

title: Isaiah 36:1
text:
Sennacherib--came up; the occasion of this invasion was Hezekiah's refusal to serve the king of Assyria.   II Kings 18:7 , compared with  II Kings 16:7-9 . 
 
See also notes on  II Kings 18:1-19:37 .

title: Isaiah 36:2
text:
The king of Assyria sent Rabshakeh; between this invasion and that recorded in the previous verse, Hezekiah had endeavored to conciliate the king of Assyria, as recorded  II Kings 18:14-16 .  Tartan and Rabsaris accompanied Rabshakeh.   II Kings 18:17 . 
 
  Lachish; in the south of Judah. 
 
  The upper pool; see note on  Isaiah 7:3 .

title: Isaiah 36:7
text: Whose high places--Hezekiah hath taken away; he confounds, either ignorantly or designedly, the high places and altars of the false gods with those of Jehovah.  See note to  II Kings 18:22 .

title: Isaiah 36:8
text: Pledges; hostages, as security against another rebellion.

title: Isaiah 36:9
text: How then; that is, if thou canst hardly place riders upon two thousand horses.

title: Isaiah 36:19
text:
Hamath--Arpad; see note on  Isaiah 10:9 . 
 
  Sepharvaim; lying on the eastern bank of the Euphrates, above Babylon.

title: Isaiah 37:4
text: The remnant that is left; the remnant of Judah whose cities Sennacherib was now ravaging.

title: Isaiah 37:7
text:
I will send a blast upon him; a destroying wind; literally, "I will put a spirit within him," that is, probably, a spirit of terror. 
 
  He shall hear a rumor; according to some, the report of the destruction of the host before Jerusalem.  But his host seems to have departed with Rabshakeh.   Isaiah 37:8   It may have been the report of Tirhakah's preparation to attack him, which, joined with the loss of one hundred and eighty-five thousand men of his own army, hastened his return to Nineveh.

title: Isaiah 37:8
text:
Rabshakeh returned; apparently with his army, finding his force insufficient to take Jerusalem. 
 
  Libnah; another city in the south of Judah.

title: Isaiah 37:9
text: When he heard; this report increased his anxiety to bring Hezekiah to a speedy submission.

title: Isaiah 37:12
text:
Gozan, and Haran; regions of Mesopotamia, the former lying on the Chebar.   II Kings 18:11  
 
  Rezeph; west of the Euphrates.

title: Isaiah 37:24
text: I will cut down the tall cedars thereof; the destruction of the forests of Lebanon is put figuratively for the desolation of the nations, with every thing in them that was "high and lifted up." Compare  Isaiah 2:12-16 .

title: Isaiah 37:25
text:
I have digged, and drunk water; where water was wanting for my host, I have provided it. 
 
  Dried up all the rivers of the besieged places; or, "all the rivers of Egypt."  I have, as it were, annihilated them with the feet of my armies: they have not been able to oppose to me any resistance.

title: Isaiah 37:26
text: I have done it--formed it; appointed in my eternal counsels what I have now brought to pass, namely, "that thou shouldest be to lay waste defenced cities."

title: Isaiah 37:29
text: Therefore will I put my hook in thy nose, and my bridle in thy lips; referring to a ring or hook placed in the nose of untamed animals.

title: Isaiah 37:30
text:
A sign unto thee; unto Hezekiah. 
 
  This year; when tillage had been interrupted by the presence of the enemy; so that there could be no seed-time for the second or following year. 
 
  The second year--and in the third year; the sign seems to have consisted in the extraordinary fertility of the earth during these two years, which should make its uncultivated productions sufficient for the wants of the people.

title: Isaiah 37:36
text:
The arose; the Jews, and the Assyrians who were spared. 
 
  They were all dead corpses; the Assyrians that were smitten.

title: Isaiah 38:12
text:
From day even to night; day and night, that is by a sickness that has no intermission.  Compare  Genesis 6:7 . 
 
No age, nor strength, nor station can exempt us from liability to sudden death in the midst of our cherished enterprises.  It is our wisdom to hold ourselves always ready to leave this life with all its labors, at God's bidding.

title: Isaiah 38:13
text: The best relief in times of deep anguish, is to pour out our hearts to God in prayer.

title: Isaiah 38:15
text:
What shall I say? this verse refers to God's second message promising him restoration from his present sickness. 
 
  In the bitterness of my soul; in humility and contrition, from the remembrance of this chastisement.   Isaiah 38:17  
 
The remembrance of past afflictions should fill us with humility in view of the sinfulness which made them necessary, and with gratitude in view of God's undeserved goodness in delivering us from them.

title: Isaiah 38:16
text: By these things--in all these things; by God's forgiving love and healing power.

title: Isaiah 38:17
text: Cast all my sins behind thy back; forgiven them.  Hezekiah regards his sickness as a chastisement for his sins.  Compare  Isaiah 38:15 .

title: Isaiah 38:18
text:
Cannot praise thee; see note on  Psalms 6:5 . 
 
  Hope for thy truth; for the further manifestation of it in this world. 
 
Good men desire the continuance of life mainly for the opportunities which it gives of glorifying God before their fellow men. 
 
See also  II Kings 20:1-11 .

title: Isaiah 38:22
text: Had said; see  II Kings 20:8-11 .

title: Isaiah 39:1
text:
Merodach-baladan; called also Berodach-baladan,  II Kings 20:12 . 
 
  King of Babylon; Babylon was at this time a dependency of Assyria, and governed by viceroys.  But Merodach-baladan, as history informs us, sought to make himself independent.  For this reason, probably, he courted the friendship of Hezekiah. 
 
See  II Kings 20:12-19 .

title: Isaiah 39:2
text: Was glad of them, and showed them; he was unduly elated in view of the attention shown him by the king of Babylon, as well as of his own power and riches.   II Chronicles 32:25

title: Isaiah 39:7
text: Of thy sons--they shall be eunuchs; this was fulfilled, not in his immediate offspring, but in their posterity.  See  Daniel 1:3 , where by "the king's seed" are meant the descendants of the Jewish kings.

title: Isaiah 39:8
text: For there shall be peace; he expresses his gratitude to God for this mitigation of the threatened chastisement.

title: Isaiah 40:1
text:
This and the remaining chapters of Isaiah were probably written by the prophet at a later period.  Their immediate design was to comfort true believers, in view of the heavy calamities with which God had visited his ancient covenant people for their sins, and the still heavier calamities that awaited them in the Babylonish captivity, which he had already foretold.  But since that captivity was only one of a series of chastisements designed for the purification of God's church; and her deliverance from it was to be but an earnest of higher deliverance in the more distant future, especially of the great spiritual deliverance from sin through the incarnation and death of Jesus Christ, we must understand this portion of Isaiah, which makes one connected whole, as covering the entire history of the church to the end of time.  Its great theme is expressed in the introductory verse: "Comfort ye, comfort ye my people, saith your God." 
 
God has always a message of comfort for his people, even in times of deep affliction; the end of all his dealings with them is their establishment in holiness and happiness.

title: Isaiah 40:2
text: Double; double chastisement; that is, according to the ordinary measure of God's dealings with men.

title: Isaiah 40:3
text:
The voice of him that crieth in the wilderness; see  Matthew 3:3   Mark 1:3 Luke 3:4 John 1:23 .  The mission of John the Baptist was a most striking fulfilment of this prophecy in a literal way.  It is also fulfilled, more indirectly, in all those movements of God's providence and Spirit, by which he prepares the way for the revival of his cause in regions of spiritual darkness and desolation. 
 
vv 3-5. 
 
When the set time for Zion's enlargement has come, God provides men and means for the work, and removes all obstacles to its accomplishment.

title: Isaiah 40:4
text: Every valley shall be exalted--the crooked shall be made straight, and the rough places plain; all obstacles to the redemption of God's people shall be taken out of the way.

title: Isaiah 40:6
text:
The voice said, Cry; the voice of Jehovah. 
 
  He said; the messenger to whom Jehovah's command was directed. 
 
  All flesh is grass; this, with the two following verses, contains God's answer to the question, "What shall I cry?" 
 
vv 6-8. 
 
The successive generations of men pass away like the flowers of spring; but God's promise to his church stands fast for ever, and he will make her "an eternal excellency, a joy of many generations."   Isaiah 60:15

title: Isaiah 40:8
text: The word of our God; his word of promise to Zion, which is here contrasted with the frailty of man.

title: Isaiah 40:9
text: Be not afraid; to announce the good tidings, for thou shalt not disappoint the hopes of those that hear them.

title: Isaiah 40:10
text: His work; or, "his recompense for his work;" that is, the recompense which he himself receives in his redeemed people.  Compare  Isaiah 53:11 , "He shall see of the travail of his soul, and be satisfied."

title: Isaiah 40:11
text: Our covenant God and Saviour unites with the majesty of an omnipotent King the gentleness and tender care of a shepherd.   Isaiah 42:3

title: Isaiah 40:12
text:
vv 12-22,25-28. 
 
God's infinite perfections insure the fulfilment of all his promises to his people.  His power is absolute, and can be hindered by no obstacles; his understanding is infinite, and he cannot err or be in perplexity in respect to the means he shall employ; his goodness and truth are eternal, and he will not alter his covenant with those who love him.  In the darkest days of adversity they may rest assured that he is doing all things well in their behalf.

title: Isaiah 40:22
text: Upon the circle of the earth; upon the vault of the heavens extended over the earth.

title: Isaiah 40:23
text:
vv 23-24. 
 
The plans of men are under God's control, and he establishes or overthrows them according to his own pleasure, without interfering with their freedom and responsibility as the accountable subjects of his government.

title: Isaiah 40:26
text: Not one faileth; not one of the heavenly host fails to appear in its appointed place.

title: Isaiah 40:27
text:
Why sayest thou, O Jacob; from God's infinite perfections, the prophet argues that he cannot neglect his people. 
 
  My way; the way in which I go; that is, my situation. 
 
  Hid from the Lord; out of his sight and mind. 
 
  My judgment; my cause, which ought to come before him as "the Judge of all the earth." 
 
  Is passed over from my God; has been neglected by him.

title: Isaiah 40:29
text:
vv 29-31. 
 
Despondency in God's service is sinful and unreasonable, for he is both able and ready to bestow upon his servants any measure of strength and wisdom which their necessities may demand.   II Corinthians 12:9

title: Isaiah 41:1
text:
O islands; the coasts and islands of the Mediterranean, and generally the remote regions of the west. 
 
  Let the people renew their strength; God challenges the heathen nations to vindicate before him, if they can, the claims of their deities. 
 
God invites men to the fullest investigation of his claims of his word. The cause of truth challenges free discussion.  It is error that loves darkness and concealment.

title: Isaiah 41:2
text:
Who raised up--called him to his foot; the reference is to Cyrus, whom God's righteousness, that is, his faithfulness to his covenant people, called to execute its purposes. 
 
"Known unto God are all his works from the beginning of the world."  To him the victories of Cyrus, and the deliverance of His covenant people through his instrumentality, were as certain in the days of Isaiah as of Zerubbabel; and He therefore spoke of them by the prophet as already existing.

title: Isaiah 41:4
text:
Calling the generations from the beginning; calling them into being. 
 
  With the last; enduring while creation endures, that is, for ever.

title: Isaiah 41:5
text:
Saw it; the display of the attributes of God, mentioned in  Isaiah 41:2-3 . 
 
  Feared; for the cause of their idols. 
 
  Drew near, and came; to encourage and help each other in the maintenance of idolatry.

title: Isaiah 41:7
text: Great indeed is the folly of idolaters, who trust for salvation to the gods which smiths and carpenters have made; but it is no greater than that of every worldly man who gives to earthly objects his supreme love and confidence.

title: Isaiah 41:9
text: From the chief men thereof; or, "from the extremities thereof." The reference seems to be to the calling of Abraham.

title: Isaiah 41:15
text:
I will make thee; in the Hebrew, make thee into; that is, cause thee to be. 
 
  A new sharp threshing instrument having teeth; a threshing sledge, armed with points of iron or stone, which was drawn by oxen over the corn to separate the grain from the ear.  The threshing of grain is often, in the Old Testament, a symbol of the destruction of God's enemies. 
 
Of herself the church of Christ is only an earthen vessel, but within her dwells the excellency of divine power.  No array of human forces can stand against her, more than chaff can resist the whirlwind.

title: Isaiah 41:17
text: Seasons of deep distress have often been to God's poeple the dawn of a bright and glorious day; they have thus been withdrawn from every worldly confidence, and led to seek deliverance from God by deep repentance and earnest supplication.

title: Isaiah 41:18
text:
vv 18-19. 
 
  I will open rivers--plant in the wilderness; the wilderness is a symbol of adversity and affliction, as its conversion into well-watered and fruitful fields is of returning prosperity and comfort. 
 
vv 18-20. 
 
God is the fountain of life and power.  It is easy for him to change the wilderness into a fruitful field for his people, and he will do it for the glory of his own name.

title: Isaiah 41:21
text:
Produce your cause; another challenge to the worshippers of idols. 
 
vv 21-29. 
 
The numerous prophecies recorded in the Bible which have been fulfilled, or are now in fulfilment, are God's witness to the truth of Christianity--a witness which no other religion is able to produce.

title: Isaiah 41:22
text:
The former things; ancient prophecies. 
 
  Know the latter end of them; compare the issue with the prophecies, as as to judge whether they have been fulfilled.  The prophet challenges the votaries of idols either to produce their former prophecies that have been fulfilled, or to foretell the future.

title: Isaiah 41:25
text:
I have raised up; in purpose: this is a prediciton of Cyrus. 
 
  From the north--from the rising of the sun; Cyrus came from the north with respect to Babylon, but his kingdom was eastward with respect to Jerusalem, towards which place his invocation of Jehovah's name must be directed. 
 
  Shall he call upon my name; compare  Ezra 1:1-4 .

title: Isaiah 41:26
text:
Who hath declared; the coming of Cyrus. 
 
  Righteous; in his claim to be a true God; or, "it is righteous," that is, true. 
 
  Heareth your words; your words of prophecy; none has ever heard from your lips true prophetic announcements.

title: Isaiah 41:27
text:
The first shall say; or, "I am the first who has said." 
 
  Them; the predicted events.

title: Isaiah 41:28
text: Among them; among the patrons of idolatry.

title: Isaiah 42:1
text:
My servant; the Messiah.   Matthew 12:18-21   The reference to Cyrus in the preceding chapter naturally prepared the way for the mention of one greater than Cyrus. 
 
vv 1-4. 
 
The kingdom of Christ "cometh not with observation," but by the gentle and quiet influences of his word and Spirit operating within the soul. Great outward changes and revolutions accompany its progress in the world, but amid all these it remains "like leaven which a woman took and hid in three measures of meal, till the whole was leavened."  Luke 13:21

title: Isaiah 42:2
text: Lift up; his voice; he shall be quiet and unassuming.

title: Isaiah 42:3
text:
A bruised reed; which the slightest violence might break. 
 
  The smoking flax; the dimly burning wick.  He shall deal gently with the ignorant and feeble-minded.  Compare  Isaiah 40:11 . 
 
  Unto truth; in accordance with truth.

title: Isaiah 42:4
text:
The isles; see note on  Isaiah 41:1 . 
 
  Shall wait; in the spirit of obedience.  The general reception of the gospel by the western nations is a striking fulfilment of this prophecy.

title: Isaiah 42:5
text:
He that created--spirit to them that walk therein; the divine power set forth in this verse is a pledge that the promise contained in the following verse shall be fulfilled. 
 
vv 5-8. 
 
God's glory is pledged to establish Christ's kingdom over all the earth, and to give deliverance and salvation to every sinner who commits his soul to His hands.

title: Isaiah 42:6
text: A covenant of the people; the mediator of God's new covenant with the people.   Jeremiah 31:31-34 , compared with  Hebrews 8:6-13 .

title: Isaiah 42:7
text: To open the blind eyes--out of the prison-house; he is the Redeemer from spiritual blindness and bondage.

title: Isaiah 42:8
text: My glory will I not give to another--to graven images; by allowing the cause of idolatry to triumph.  Thus God pledges his own glory for the success of the Messiah and his kingdom.

title: Isaiah 42:9
text: The former things; the things formerly predicted.

title: Isaiah 42:10
text:
A new song; for the new things declared. 
 
vv 10-16. 
 
The same mighty movements of God's providence and Spirit which bring salvation and rejoicing to his church, carry desolation and destruction into the hosts of her enemies.  While they weep and wail over the fall of Satan's kingdom, she shouts, "Alleluia," as its smoke rises up for ever and ever.   Revelation of John 18:1-19:6

title: Isaiah 42:11
text: Kedar; see note on  Isaiah 21:16 .

title: Isaiah 42:13
text: Jealousy; zeal; that is, his own zeal.  Compare  Isaiah 9:7 Isaiah 37:32  where the word in the original is the same.

title: Isaiah 42:14
text: Holden my peace; not interposed in behalf of my people.

title: Isaiah 42:15
text: Will make waste mountains and hills; will make desolate the enemies of Zion.  This is the opposite of what God promises to his own people. See  Isaiah 41:18-19 , and note.

title: Isaiah 42:16
text: I will bring the blind; compare  Isaiah 42:7 .

title: Isaiah 42:17
text:
vv 17-25. 
 
The hope of God's people is his zeal for the glory of his own name.  He will not give them over to final corruption and ruin, but will, from time to time, purify them by severe judgments, and thus prepare the way for the extension of Christ's kingdom over all the earth.

title: Isaiah 42:19
text:
My servant; Israel, the covenant people of God.  "The servant of the Lord" signifies, in its widest sense, any minister of his will, though he be ignorant of God as Nebuchadnezzar,  Jeremiah 43:10 . Compare  Ezekiel 29:18-20 .  In a more special sense it is applied, particularly in this part of Isaiah, 
 
(1) to God's visible covenant people, "Israel after the flesh," as in this verse,  Isaiah 43:22 , and often elsewhere; 
 
(2) to the body of true believers, "the Israel of God," contained within the outward Israel,  Isaiah 44:1 Isaiah 44:3 , etc.; 
 
(3) to Christ the Head of the church, as in  Isaiah 42:1-7   Isaiah 52:13-15 Isaiah 53:1-12 , and elsewhere. 
 
And as Christ and his true church are one body-- John 15:1-7   John 17:21 John 17:23 Ephesians 1:23 --it is often both difficult and unnecessary to determine whether the words "my servant" apply to Christ alone, or to Christ's body as quickened and sanctified by its union with him. 
 
  My messanger; Israel, whom God appointed to make the Gentiles see and hear his truth, has himself become blind and deaf. 
 
  Perfect; in respect to his privileges and outward relations to God. Compare  Matthew 11:23 .

title: Isaiah 42:20
text: Seeing--thou observest not; compare  Isaiah 6:9-10 .

title: Isaiah 42:21
text:
Is well pleased; it is his good pleasure to do what is expressed in the last clause of the verse. 
 
  For his righteousness' sake; his covenant people having forfeited all claim to his favor by their sins, he will do this for the glory of his own name and character. 
 
  Will magnify the law; will put honor upon it by all his dealings with his people, and, in a most emphatic sense, by the mission and propitiatory death of his Son.

title: Isaiah 42:22
text:
vv 22-25. 
 
These verses describe the character and punishment of the outward Israel.  Compare  Isaiah 6:11-12 .

title: Isaiah 43:1
text: O Jacob--Israel; Jacob and Israel "according to the election of grace."  The judgments upon the outward Israel, described at the close of the preceding chapter, had for their end the sanctification and enlargement of the true Israel.  Hence the transition from the former to the latter is both natural and beautiful. Such transitions are very frequent in the prophets.

title: Isaiah 43:2
text: God will not allow any calamity, however great, to overwhelm his true children; but will graciously sustain and comfort them under it, grant them in due time deliverance from it, and make it subservient to their highest welfare.

title: Isaiah 43:3
text:
Ethiopia and Seba; regions adjacent to Egypt on the south.  God sacrificed Egypt, at the exodus, to the welfare of his people, and he has often repeated this sacrifice in the case of the nations that have arrayed themselves against his church. 
 
vv 3-4. 
 
God governs the world for the good of his church.  For her, empires rise and fall, and battles are lost and won.  Every power that arrays itself against her must perish for her sake.   Isaiah 43:14-17

title: Isaiah 43:7
text:
Created him--made him; in a spiritual sense. 
 
It is for his own glory that God begins and carries forward the work of redemption in men's souls, and he will make every ransomed spirit in heaven an eternal monument of his praise.

title: Isaiah 43:8
text:
Bring forth; that they may maintain their cause before God. Compare  Isaiah 41:1 . 
 
  The blind people that have eyes; the patrons of idolatry, as in  Isaiah 43:9 .

title: Isaiah 43:9
text:
This; which I have predicted and brought to pass; that is, who can show like predictions? 
 
  Former things; former prophecies. 
 
  Witnesses; to their prophecies. 
 
  Let them hear; my witnesses to my prophecies.

title: Isaiah 43:11
text:
vv 11-13. 
 
All who give to God their supreme love and confidence receive from him abundant proofs, in their own blessed experience, that he has power to help in every extremity: all who depart from him shall be made to feel that besides him there is no saviour.

title: Isaiah 43:14
text:
Sent to Babylon; by the Persians and Medes. 
 
  Brought down; humbled. 
 
  Cry; the reference is to the shouts or songs of the mariners as they pursue their business.

title: Isaiah 43:16
text:
vv 16-17. 
 
  Maketh a way in the sea--bringeth forth the chariot and horse; as in the overthrow of Pharaoh. 
 
  They shall lie down together; all the opponents of Israel shall perish as did Pharaoh's host. 
 
  Tow; a flaxen wick.   Isaiah 42:3

title: Isaiah 43:18
text:
Remember ye not the former things; because of the surpassing glory of the new.  Compare  Jeremiah 16:14-15 II Corinthians 3:10 . 
 
The revelation of redemption is "as the shining light, that shineth more and more unto the perfect day."  The light under which we live excels in brightness that which was enjoyed by ancient patriarchs and prophets, yet we see but the dawn of the glory which is reserved for the latter days of Zion, and even that glory shall be swallowed up in the everlasting brightness of the new Jerusalem.

title: Isaiah 43:20
text: Dragons; in the sense of wild animals, as jackals.

title: Isaiah 43:22
text:
vv 22-25. 
 
  Hast not called upon me--for mine own sake; this great redemption is wholly undeserved.  God does it for the glory of his own name. 
 
Neither Zion, nor any one of her children, has any thing to meniton before God but unfaithfulness, lukewarmness, and iniquities without number.  He has mercy upon his people, not for their sake, but for his own name's sake; so that to him belongs all the praise, and to them shame and confusion of face.

title: Isaiah 43:26
text:
vv 26-28. 
 
The severest rebukes that come upon God's people are less than their iniquities deserve.  They should therefore be borne with humility and submission, and deliverance from them sought by confession and repentance.

title: Isaiah 43:27
text: Thy first father; Adam.  The meaning is, that Israel's teachers have imitated Adam's apostasy, and led the people also into apostasy.

title: Isaiah 44:1
text:
vv 1-5. 
 
The promised outpouring of God's life-giving Spirit is the hope of Zion.  In times of deep declension within her borders, and abounding wickedness without, God's faithful servants should not despond, but seek from him this unspeakable gift by repentance, obedience, and earnest intercession, assured that when he bestows it all will again become green and flourishing.

title: Isaiah 44:2
text: Jeshurun; a term of endearment applied ot Israel.  Deuteronomy 32:15 Deuteronomy 33:5

title: Isaiah 44:7
text:
Call; command into being. 
 
  Declare it; announce it beforehand. 
 
  Set it in order for me; that is, as the original implies, state it to me in regular order.  Jehovah both ordains and foretells the course of coming events for his people; he challenges the false gods to do the same. 
 
  The ancient people; either the ancestors of the human race or those of the Israelitish people.

title: Isaiah 44:8
text:
Fear ye not; the idol-gods, which have no power either to do or to foretell. 
 
  From that time; that is, "since I appointed the ancient people."  Isaiah 44:7  
 
  Told--declared; the course of coming events.

title: Isaiah 44:9
text:
Delectable things; idols in which they delight. 
 
vv 9-20. 
 
The idolater fashions silver or wood into the form of a god and then worships it, as if human workmanship could give life to that which is in its own nature dead and powerless.  The same folly is manifested by all who think to make worldly objects a permanent and satisfying portion by any labor which they can bestow upon them.

title: Isaiah 44:14
text: Strengtheneth for himself; has nourished by culture.

title: Isaiah 44:18
text: He hath shut their eyes; God hath shut them.  Isaiah 6:10 John 12:40

title: Isaiah 44:20
text:
Deliver his soul; from its delusion. 
 
  Nor say; he has not understanding enough to ask himself the question that follows. 
 
  In my right hand; the right hand is mentioned as the instrument of action: to have a lie in the right hand, is to be occupied with a lie; that is, with the service of idols, which are themselves false, and which deceive those who put their trust in them.

title: Isaiah 44:21
text: These; these proofs of the vanity of idols.

title: Isaiah 44:22
text: It is by the offer of gratuitous pardon that God calls sinners to himself.  He commands them to come, that they may receive through Christ the justifying righteousness which he has provided for them; not to establish their own righteousness before coming to him.

title: Isaiah 44:23
text: Christ's redemption is the sum of all blessings.  It fills every heart that receives it with gladness and thanksgiving.  When all nations shall embrace it, the whole erth will resound with God's praises.

title: Isaiah 44:24
text: Formed thee from the womb; Israel is here spoken of as God's child from the womb, that is, from the infancy of the nation.

title: Isaiah 44:25
text:
Tokens; signs, pretended miracles. 
 
  Maketh diviners mad; shows them to be fools. 
 
The progress of God's kingdom in the world is a perpetual manifestation of his own infinite power and wisdom, and of the folly and weakness of all human systems of religion.

title: Isaiah 44:26
text: His servant; the prophet with his fellow-messengers.

title: Isaiah 44:28
text: Cyrus; who conquered Babylon, and released the Jews from their exile more than a century and a half after this prediction. Ezr 1.1-4

title: Isaiah 45:1
text:
Anointed; as set apart to the work of redeeming God's people. 
 
  The gates shall not be shut; remarkably fulfulled in the conquest of Babylon, the gates of the city having been left open during a night of feasting.

title: Isaiah 45:4
text:
Hast not known me; when Cyrus took Babylon he was ignorant of Jehovah and of the designs which he purposed to accomplish through him, and was only indulging his own ambitious desires.  The knowledge which he afterwards had of God,  Ezra 1:2 , was doubtless received from the Jews residing in Babylon. 
 
God has often employed heathen princes, who were ignorant of him and his counsels, to accomplish wonderful deliverances for his people.

title: Isaiah 45:7
