text: Since God is the author of all things, he governs and sets limits to all.  The good and bad actions of men and angels are so under his control that he accomplishes through them his own wise counsels, while they are left altogether free and responsible to him for their conduct.

title: Isaiah 45:8
text:
Drop down; distil. 
 
  Open; open her bosom to send forth a harvest of righteousness and salvation. 
 
  Let them bring forth; that is, the heavens and the skies.  God's righteousness and salvation are here compared to refreshing showers and a harvest of precious fruits.

title: Isaiah 45:9
text:
vv 9-10. 
 
  Woe unto him; God rebukes his people for arraigning his dealings with them at the bar of their own reason.  The primary reference may be to their long-continued sufferings during the Babylonish captivity; but the words have a general application to God's treatment of all men in all ages. 
 
All our capacity to reason concerning God's works and ways is his gift. How unspeakable the folly and wickedness of contending against his dealings with us; as if the creature could sit in judgment on the infinite Creator.

title: Isaiah 45:11
text: Command ye me; in the way of petitioning, not of prescribing.

title: Isaiah 45:14
text:
Labor; wealth gained by labor. 
 
  Men of stature; the Ethiopians and Sabeans were celebrated for their tallness. 
 
  Shall come after thee--make supplication unto thee; compare  Psalms 72:9-11 Psalms 14:2 Psalms 49:20  and especially  Psalms 60:1-12 .  These passages are to be understood in a spiritual sense.  The meaning is, that God will give his church, through Christ, universal dominion and honor.

title: Isaiah 45:15
text: Hidest thyself; hidest thy counsels in darkness.  The prophet has in mind the sore afflictions through which Zion must come to the fulfilment of the promises which he has just recorded.

title: Isaiah 45:18
text: Not in vain; as God's purpose in creating the earth shall be fulfilled, so shall all his counsels respecting his chosen people.

title: Isaiah 45:19
text:
In secret, in a dark place of the earth; not uttering dark responses from caves, like the ancient oracles. 
 
  In vain; as did those who consulted the heathen oracles. 
 
The many and explicit predictions of God's word constitute a proof of its divine origin, such as no pretended revelation can offer.

title: Isaiah 45:20
text: Escaped of the nations; the remnant of them who have escaped God's judgments.

title: Isaiah 45:21
text:
Tell ye; recount your arguments. 
 
  Them; the patrons of idols. 
 
  Declared this; deliverance of my people through Cyrus, which I have foretold. 
 
  From that time; see note on  Isaiah 44:8 .

title: Isaiah 45:23
text: God possesses absolute authority over all men: and he will exercise it throughout eternity, for their salvation if righteous; but if wicked, for their destruction.

title: Isaiah 45:24
text: It is vain to look for justifying righteousness, or strength to overcome sin, to any thing that we can do, or that our fellow sinners can do for us.  We must receive both from God as his free gift through Jesus Christ.

title: Isaiah 46:1
text:
Bel-Nebo; Babylonian gods. 
 
  Boweth down--stoopeth; under the conqueror.  The gods of Babylon have gone into captivity with their worshippers. 
 
  Their idols; the images of Bel and Nebo. 
 
  Carriages; that is, things carried, loads; the old English sense of the word. 
 
  Heavy-laden; literally, "lifted up," placed upon the beasts.  The images of your gods, which you have been accustomed to bear in solemn procession, are now packed upon beasts to be carried away.

title: Isaiah 46:2
text:
They; the gods. 
 
  The burden; the load consisting of their own images.  Bel and Nebo cannot save their own images from this disgrace. 
 
The gods of the heathen need the constant care and protection of their makers.  They cannot help themselves, much less their worshippers.  So the objects to which worldly men give their supreme love and confidence--riches, honors, titles, pleasures--cannot save their possessors, but must themselves be watched over day and night, lest they "make themselves wings," and "fly away as an eagle toward heaven."  Proverbs 23:5 Luke 12:19-20 I Timothy 6:17

title: Isaiah 46:3
text:
vv 3-4. 
 
  Borne--carried; the gods of the heathen must be borne by their worshippers, but Jehovah bears and carries his people. 
 
  From the womb--to hoar hairs; from the infancy of Israel to his old age; that is through his whole existence.  See note to  Isaiah 44:24 . 
 
The salvation of nations, as well as of individual men, comes from God alone.  When they depart from him and put their trust in vanity and lies, they must perish.

title: Isaiah 46:8
text:
This; the contrast between Jehovah and the idol-gods. 
 
  Show yourselves men; act like men, not like children, as do the worshippers of idols.

title: Isaiah 46:9
text: The former things of old; ancient prophecies that have been fulfilled.

title: Isaiah 46:11
text: A ravenous bird; Cyrus, represented as a bird of prey.

title: Isaiah 46:13
text: Righteousness; as manifested in the deliverance of my people, and the destruction of their enemies.

title: Isaiah 47:1
text:
O virgin daughter of Babylon; Babylon herself personified as a female. 
 
  No throne; that is, to thee. 
 
vv 1-5. 
 
No present degree of power, wealth, or splendor, can protect wicked and persecuting nations from the wrath of God.  He has pledged himself to humble every oppressor of his people, and for the fulfilment of his word all the resources of heaven and earth are at his disposal.

title: Isaiah 47:2
text:
Take the millstones; grinding, in the East, is a menial office. The mistress of nations must now take the place of a servant. 
 
  Uncover thy locks; remove thy veil; another sign of degradation. 
 
  Make bare the leg--pass over the rivers; she is represented as fording streams in the manner of a woman of the lowest condition.

title: Isaiah 47:3
text: Will not meet thee as a man; not as a frail man, but as the omnipotent God.  But some prefer to render, "I will meet no man;" that is, no one who can offer me any resistance.

title: Isaiah 47:6
text: It is no excuse to wicked men, that God employs them as the instruments of executing his purposes.  They will be judged according to the spirit and intention of their deeds, not according to the use which God's overruling wisdom makes of them.

title: Isaiah 47:7
text:
The latter end of it; of thy pride, luxury, and cruelty; that is, the disgrace to which they would bring thee. 
 
vv 7-9. 
 
A proud, self-sufficient, and contemptuous spirit is the harbinger of ruin to nations not less than to individuals.  When a nation thinks itself most secure from danger, it is often nearest to destruction.

title: Isaiah 47:10
text:
vv 10-15. 
 
When a nation has cast off the fear of God, and trampled under foot his holy law, no device of human wisdom can save it from speedy and utter ruin.

title: Isaiah 47:11
text:
From whence it riseth; or, "its morning."  It shall be a night of calamity, without any morning of prosperity. 
 
  Shalt not know; suddenly, and without notice beforehand.  Compare  Job 9:5 .

title: Isaiah 47:13
text: Monthly prognosticators; those who pretend to foretell events from the changes of the moon.

title: Isaiah 47:14
text: Not be a coal--nor fire; the consumption shall be so complete that nothing shall be left.

title: Isaiah 47:15
text: Thy merchants; the merchants whose trade had enriched Babylon. Compare  Isaiah 13:14 .

title: Isaiah 48:1
text:
Out of the waters of Judah; from the family of Judah.  Compare  Psalms 68:26 . 
 
  Swear by the name of the Lord; thus acknowledging him as your God.

title: Isaiah 48:3
text: Former things; formerly predicted and now fulfilled.

title: Isaiah 48:6
text:
Heard; the prediction. 
 
  See all this; see the whole accomplished. 
 
  Declare it; be my witnesses to its fulfilment.

title: Isaiah 48:7
text: Before the day when thou heardest them not; rather, "before to-day thou heardest them not."  Thy idol gave thee no prophetic intimation of them.

title: Isaiah 48:8
text:
From that time; from of old. 
 
  Thine ear was not opened; it was not revealed to thee. 
 
  For I knew that thou wouldest deal very treacherously; for the meaning, compare  Isaiah 48:3-5 .

title: Isaiah 48:10
text: Not with silver; or "for silver," the refining produced no good result.  Compare  Jeremiah 6:28-30 .

title: Isaiah 48:11
text: God continues to carry forward his work of redemption in the hearts of his people, not from any goodness or faithfulness that he sees in them, but for the glory of his own name.  Lest his and their enemies should triumph in their destruction, he bears with their waywardness and folly, disciplines them with much longsuffering, and makes them at last eternal monuments of his almighty power and abounding grace.

title: Isaiah 48:14
text:
Assemble yourselves; another challenge to the patrons of idolatry. Compare  Isaiah 41:1 . 
 
  These things; concerning the redemption of God's people. 
 
  Him; Cyrus, as the next verse shows. 
 
  He will do his pleasure; God, through Cyrus.

title: Isaiah 48:16
text:
In secret; my predictions have been open and unambiguous. 
 
  From the time that it was; from the time that these events began. 
 
  There am I; as the doer. 
 
  And now--hath sent me; the Messiah, who may be considered as speaking in God's name through the remainder of the chapter, and who speaks in the beginning of the following chapter.  To the Messiah, as God, the whole of the present verse may be referred.

title: Isaiah 48:17
text:
vv 17-19. 
 
Nothing is more plain than that the happiness and prosperity of God's people lie in whole-hearted obedience and devotion to him; yet nothing is so difficult for them to learn.  Sin and suffering make up a large part of their history.

title: Isaiah 48:20
text: Hath redeemed; in this and the following verse the deliverance of Israel is spoken of as already accomplished in God's purpose.

title: Isaiah 48:21
text: They thirsted not--gushed out; God provides for his people, as of old, when he delivered them from Egypt.  Allusions of this kind to the miraculous provision which God made for the wants of his people in the wilderness of Arabia, when on their way to the promised land, abound in this part of Isaiah, and are to be understood not literally but figuratively.  See  Isaiah 42:17-19 Isaiah 43:19-20 Isaiah 49:10 Isaiah 55:13 .  Their spiritual application is given directly in  Isaiah 44:3-5 .

title: Isaiah 48:22
text: In all the glorious promises which God makes to those who love him, the wicked have no share.  Not peace but destruction is their portion.

title: Isaiah 49:1
text:
The subject of this chapter is Christ and his body the church.  In the former part, Christ the Head is especially exhibited; in the latter, Christ's body. 
 
  Made mention of my name;  Matthew 1:21 Luke 1:31 Luke 2:1  The name contains in itself a description of his character.

title: Isaiah 49:2
text:
Like a sharp sword; this describes the power and energy of Christ's word and doctrine.  Compare  Isaiah 11:4 Hebrews 4:12 Revelation of John 1:16 Revelation of John 19:15 Revelation of John 19:21 . 
 
  Hid me; from the power of the enemy. 
 
  Polished shaft; compare  Psalms 45:5 . 
 
When Christ himself preached, his word was like a sharp sword, piercing men's consciences and revealing their inmost thoughts; and the same power he gives through the Holy Spirit to his gospel, whenever his servants preach it in its simplicity and purity, "commending" themselves "to every man's conscience in the sight of God."  But they who think to make it attractive to sinners by clothing it "with enticing words of man's wisdom," destroy its living energy, and make it dead and powerless for the salvation of the soul.

title: Isaiah 49:4
text:
In vain--for naught; compare  Isaiah 53:1 John 12:38 Romans 10:16 . 
 
The reward of Christ's labors and sufferings, though long delayed, is made sure to him by the promise of his Father; and in like manner, he insures to all his faithful servants the reward of their toil in his cause.

title: Isaiah 49:5
text:
Though Israel be not gathered; that is, "Israel after the flesh," be not gathered for a season.   Romans 11:25  
 
  Glorious; as "a light to the Gentiles,"  Isaiah 49:6 .  Many prefer, "the Israel of God." 
 
Ministerial acceptance depends not on outward success, but in fidelity.

title: Isaiah 49:7
text:
Him whom man despiseth; the Messiah,  Isaiah 53:3 ; but we need not wholly exclude his members.   John 15:20 I Peter 2:21  
 
  Shall see; his exaltation. 
 
  Arise; to do him reverence. 
 
Christ's road to exaltation lay through the deepest humiliation.  Isaiah 50:6   Herein his servants should be content to follow in his footsteps.   Romans 8:17 II Timothy 2:12

title: Isaiah 49:8
text:
In an acceptable time; in a time of favor, the appointed time for his exaltation. 
 
  A covenant of the people; see note on  Isaiah 42:6 . 
 
  To establish the earth; or, "to raise up the earth," that is, to build up its ruins. 
 
  To cause to inherit the desolate heritages; to restore thy people to the possession of their lost and desolate heritages.  This is to be understood spiritually of the renovation of the church, and the extension of her borders through Christ.

title: Isaiah 49:9
text:
Say to the prisoners; see  Isaiah 42:7  
 
  They shall feed; Christ's flock shall feed.

title: Isaiah 49:10
text: They who have Christ for their shepherd cannot want any needful provision for soul or for body.   Psalms 23:1

title: Isaiah 49:11
text: Exalted; cast up, so as to afford them a safe way.

title: Isaiah 49:12
text: Sinim; these are probably the Chinese, or some nation on their western border.

title: Isaiah 49:14
text:
vv 14-17. 
 
In times of long-continued suffering, God's people are often tempted to despondency, through "an evil heart of unbelief."  But his love for them can never suffer any abatement.  In all their sorrows he bears them continually on his heart, and will in due time great them a glorious deliverance.

title: Isaiah 49:16
text: Upon the palms of my hands; as an object to be always remembered.

title: Isaiah 49:17
text: Make haste; to return from their captivity.

title: Isaiah 49:21
text:
Who hath begotten me these; there seems to be a reference in these words to the great accession of gentile converts. 
 
The experience of God's church in all ages has been, that every period of sharp conflict and persecution has brought to her a great enlargement of her spiritual offspring.

title: Isaiah 49:22
text:
vv 22-26. 
 
The more glorious the triumph which God has promised to Zion, the more terrible must be the overthrow of all who seek to destroy her.  Revelation of John 18:8

title: Isaiah 49:23
text: Bow down to thee--lick up the dust; see note on  Isaiah 45:14 .

title: Isaiah 49:24
text: Shall the prey be taken; mighty conquerors have taken God's people captive: can she hope for deliverance from them?  The question suggests a difficulty in the way of Zion's redemption, which the next verse answers.

title: Isaiah 50:1
text:
Where is the bill of your mother's divorcement; produce the bill, and it will show that she, not Jehovah, has been unfaithful.  The "mother" of the Jews is the nation itself, that is, the visible church. 
 
  Which of my creditors--sold you; the people are indeed sold into bondage, but it is by their own sinful acts.  The allusion is to the custom of a debtor's selling his children to his creditor to satisfy his demands. 
 
God is true to his engagements with his people, and mighty to deliver them.  Their sufferings come through their own unfaithfulness.

title: Isaiah 50:2
text:
vv 2-3. 
 
  When I came; to call you to repentance and obedience. 
 
  Is my hand shortened--sackcloth their covering; these words show that the divorce and captivity of God's people came from their own unfaithfulness and perverseness, not from want of power in God.

title: Isaiah 50:4
text:
vv 4-9. 
 
  Hath given me the tongue of the learned; the Messiah speaks here. "The tongue of the learned" is the tongue of those who, being themselves learned in the ways of God, are able to teach others.  This tongue the Messiah has received from Jehovah.  This accords with our Lord's constant teaching, that he had received his doctrine from the Father.   John 7:15-16  
 
Christ came from the Father, and taught the doctrine the Father committed to him.  His word is infallible truth, every way adapted to the wants of perishing sinners, and will save all who receive it in a believing, loving, and obedient spirit.

title: Isaiah 50:7
text:
vv 7-9. 
 
God's power and faithfulness are pledged to make his Son Jesus Christ victorious over every foe; and in this victory, all who are united to him by living faith shall share.  Because he triumphs, they shall triumph.   John 14:19 Romans 8:34

title: Isaiah 50:10
text:
His servant; the Messiah.  The address is to afflicted believers. 
 
vv 10-11. 
 
Quiet confidence in God is the only way to obtain deliverance from darkness.  They who in times of distress forsake the mercy seat, and rely on their own devices, must "lie down in sorrow."

title: Isaiah 50:11
text: Kindle a fire--sparks; these words describe the vain devices of unbelievers to save themselves, instead of seeking salvation from God.

title: Isaiah 51:1
text:
Hearken to me; the Messiah seems to be still the speaker.  Compare  Isaiah 51:4-5 .  The address is to God's people, who are thrice described by their character and relations to God, in  Isaiah 51:1 Isaiah 51:4 Isaiah 51:7  and thrice encouraged by the promise of God's everlasting faithfulness and love. 
 
  The rock--ye are hewn--the hole--ye are digged; that is, your origin, as explained in the next verse. 
 
vv 1-8. 
 
Heaven and earth are no so stable as the prosperity of the righteous: their helper and protector is the unchangeable God, who is faithful to fulfil all his promises to those who put their trust in him.

title: Isaiah 51:2
text: I called him alone; literally, "I called him one;" that is, when he was but one.  The power of God was shown by making of one man a great nation.

title: Isaiah 51:5
text: My righteousness; God's righteousness is manifested in the redemption of his people; hence, it is naturally joined with "my salvation."  So also  Isaiah 51:8 .

title: Isaiah 51:6
text: Lift up your eyes to the heavens; nothing is so stable as the heavens; yet these shall perish, while God's faithfulness to his people shall remain for ever.  Compare  Matthew 5:18 Matthew 24:35 Luke 16:17 .

title: Isaiah 51:9
text:
O arm of the Lord; the prophet calls upon God's arm to work as in ancient days. 
 
  Cut; hewn in pieces by thy plagues. 
 
  Rahab; Egypt.   Psalms 87:4 Psalms 89:10  
 
  The dragon; Egypt herself, under the symbol of the crocodile that inhabits the Nile. 
 
God is well pleased when his children urge his past interpositions for Zion as a reason why he should now deliver her: by every such interpostion he has pledged his infinite attributes to be with her, and help her, and give her the victory to the end of time.

title: Isaiah 51:11
text: Therefore the redeemed of the Lord shall return; thou shalt repeat thy wondrous works of old in bringing thy redeemed to thyself.

title: Isaiah 51:12
text:
vv 12-16. 
 
No array of human opposition, however formidable, ought to dismay God's people; they have on their side the Maker of heaven and earth, before whom the mightiest oppressors are but as chaff before the whirlwind.

title: Isaiah 51:13
text: Where is the fury of the oppressor? what has now become of it? This is said in anticipation of his destruction.

title: Isaiah 51:14
text: The captive exile hasteneth; the oppressor having been destroyed, the captive exiles whom he had imprisoned hasten to escape from their dungeon.

title: Isaiah 51:16
text: Plant the heavens--lay the foundations of the earth; the same as, "create new heavens and a new earth."   Isaiah 65:17

title: Isaiah 51:17
text: The cup of his fury; God's judgments are often compared to an intoxicating cup, which causes those who drink to reel.  Psalms 75:8 Jeremiah 25:15-16 Jeremiah 51:7 Lamentations 4:21 Ezekiel 23:31-34

title: Isaiah 51:18
text:
vv 18-20. 
 
When God would humble his people for their sins, he takes away from their leaders wisdom and strength, and leaves them no way of deliverance but that of a return to himself by repentance and renewed obedience.

title: Isaiah 51:19
text:
These two things; famine and the sword, producing desolation and destruction. 
 
  Who shall be sorry for thee--comfort thee? these words imply that Zion's griefs are beyond the reach of human sympathy and comfort. Therefore God himself will interpose to deliver and comfort her,  Isaiah 51:21-23 .

title: Isaiah 51:21
text:
vv 21-23. 
 
The sufferings which God inflicts upon his covenant people are designed for their purification, and he will in due time remove them.  But their merciless persecutors "shall have judgment without mercy."

title: Isaiah 52:1
text:
Zion-Jerusalem; here the representative of the true church. 
 
  There shall no more come--the unclean; the words do not so much promise to the earthly Zion an absolute exemption from the presence of the wicked, as deliverance from their dominion.   Matthew 13:24-30 Matthew 13:36-43  
 
It has ever been the effort of the "wicked one" to introduce into Zion "the uncircumcised and the unclean," and to give them the dominion over her.  But though they may greatly afflict and trouble her, God will in the end give her the victory over them.

title: Isaiah 52:3
text:
Sold yourselves for naught; your captors have paid me nothing for you.  Compare  Psalms 44:12 . 
 
  Without money; I will pay your enemies nothing for your redemption. Compare  Isaiah 45:13 .

title: Isaiah 52:5
text:
What have I here; what is this case that comes before me?  The question implies that it is a case which demands his interposition for his people. 
 
vv 5-10. 
 
The destruction of Christ's church would be a victory of Satan over the Redeemer, such as would fill the mouths of the wicked with exultation and blasphemy.  But God will never allow any oppression from without, or corruption from within, to prevail against her.  Though her enemies may triumph for a season, he will send to her, as he did to the captive Jews in Babylon, the joyful tidings of deliverance, filling the hearts of her children with gladness and thanksgiving.

title: Isaiah 52:7
text: How beautiful upon the mountains; the prophet sees in vision messengers running to announce to Zion the deliverance which God has accomplished for his people.

title: Isaiah 52:8
text:
Thy watchmen; the watchmen of Zion catch the joyful tidings, and shout for joy. 
 
  Eye for eye; "face to face," as the same words are rendered in  Numbers 14:14 .  the watchmen of Zion shall see God's glory face to face; that is, in open vision, as one sees a present friend.

title: Isaiah 52:11
text: Thence; from Babylon.  Compare  Isaiah 48:20 .  But we must understand deliverance from Babylon as an earnest and pledge of higher deliverances in the distant future.

title: Isaiah 52:13
text: My servant; the Messiah.  The remaining three verses of this chapter belong to the following, and should not have been separated from it.

title: Isaiah 52:14
text: Marred; by suffering, it wore the marks of deep sorrow.

title: Isaiah 52:15
text:
So shall he sprinkle; as a priest, with the blood of his own propitiatory sacrifice.  As his humiliation has been most deep, so shall its results be most glorious. 
 
The precepts of Christ and the living efficacy of his doctrine far transcend the wisdom of earth's most renowned sages; and they are destined to work such a glorious change in the condition of man, as never entered the heart of any heathen philosopher or prince.

title: Isaiah 53:1
text:
Our report; what we have published concerning the Messiah.  The prophet, in the name of God's messengers, laments men's rejection of the gospel. 
 
  The arm of the Lord; as manifested in the person and work of Christ. 
 
  Revealed; by the inward teaching of God's Spirit, so as to be understood.   Matthew 11:27 Matthew 16:17  
 
vv 1-2. 
 
The inward illumination of the Holy Spirit, revealing to the soul its lost condition and the all-sufficiency of Christ, can alone enable men to see his infinite excellence and glory.  To the eye of natural reason, he must ever appear without comeliness.   Matthew 16:17 I Corinthians 2:14

title: Isaiah 53:2
text:
Before him; before God.  The words imply God's deep interest in him. 
 
  A tender plant; literally, "a suckling," that is, a young shoot springing up from an old stock.  See  Job 14:7 , where the same word is rendered "tender branch." 
 
  A root; that is, the root of a decayed tree springing up into a new tree.  Compare  Isaiah 11:1 . 
 
  Out of dry ground; whence no "plant of renown" can be expected to spring.  The meaning is, that the Messiah shall be of humble origin,  John 9:29 ; of a despised region,  John 1:46 John 7:41 John 7:52 ; and that the beginnings of his kingdom shall appear small and contemptible in the eyes of men.   Matthew 13:31-32  
 
  Form--beauty; the reference is to Christ's spiritual excellence, for which the carnally-minded Jews had no discernment.

title: Isaiah 53:3
text: No one ever came on such an errand of love as the Saviour, and no one ever received such treatment at the hands of sinners.   John 1:11

title: Isaiah 53:4
text:
vv 4-6. 
 
The only sinless being who ever endured suffering, ignominy, and death, is the Lord Jesus Christ; and he suffered for our sins, "the just for the unjust, that he might bring us to God."   I Peter 3:18

title: Isaiah 53:5
text: The chastisement of our peace; the chastisement which procures for us peace with God.   Romans 5:1 Ephesians 2:13-18

title: Isaiah 53:6
text: The iniquity of us all;  Romans 4:25 II Corinthians 5:21 Galatians 3:13 I Peter 2:24 I John 2:1

title: Isaiah 53:7
text:
As a lamb to the slaughter;  Acts 8:32-28:31 
 
The Redeemer, who knew no sin, bore the ignominy of the cross with perfect meekness and submissive spirit under injurious treatment become us, who are all defiled with iniquity, and deserve nothing but evil at God's hands.   I Peter 2:21

title: Isaiah 53:8
text:
From prison and from judgment; or, "by distress and judgment," that is, by an oppressive and unrighteous judgment. 
 
  Who shall declare his generation? the number of his spiritual offspring.   Psalms 22:30   Compare  Isaiah 52:10 .  Some understand these words of Christ's divine origin.

title: Isaiah 53:9
text: He made--his death; or, "he," that is, my people, "appointed his grave with the wicked, but he was with the rich in his death."  Our Saviour was curcified as a malefactor, and would, in the natural course of events, have had his grave with the wicked; but God gave him a burial in the tomb of a rich man.   Matthew 27:57-60

title: Isaiah 53:10
text:
He shall see his seed; his spiritual children.  Psalms 22:30 Psalms 45:16 Psalms 69:36 Psalms 102:28 Psalms 110:3  
 
  He shall prolong his days; though slain as a sin-offering, he shall live for ever. 
 
Though the number of Christ's servants has hitherto been small, the day is coming when the earth shall be filled with the knowledge of his salvation.  His redeemed shall constitute a "great multitude which no man can number, of all nations, and kindred, and people, and tongues."  Isaiah 11:9 Jeremiah 31:34 Revelation of John 7:9

title: Isaiah 53:11
text:
Shall see--of his soul; shall see the fruits of his toil and sufferings. 
 
  By his knowledge; by the knowledge of himself, as the one who has borne the iniquities of men. 
 
The knowledge of Christ has a justifying and saving efficacy, because it is the knowledge of an atoning sacrifice for sin.  When the doctrine that Christ "bare the sin of many" is left out of the gospel, it becomes "another gospel," and has no longer any power to sanctify and save the soul.

title: Isaiah 53:12
text:
Divide him a portion--the strong; the "portion" and the "spoil" which God will give to the Messiah, as the reward of his sufferings, is dominion over all nations,  Psalms 2:8 Psalms 22:27 Psalms 72:11 Psalms 110:6 ; and over all the heavenly principalities and powers,  Ephesians 1:21 Philippians 2:10   Colossians 2:10 ; in a word, all power in heaven and on earth.  Matthew 28:18  
 
  Because he hath poured out his soul unto death; compare  Isaiah 52:14-15 Philippians 2:8-9 .

title: Isaiah 54:1
text:
This chapter may be regarded as an expansion of the words, "He shall see of the travail of his soul, and shall be satisfied," in the preceding chapter. 
 
  The desolate--the married wife; "the married wife" seems to be the ancient Jewish church in her union with God; "the desolate," the gentile church, which began with the rejection of the Jews,  Acts 13:46-47 Romans 11:11-12 Romans 11:30 ; but with which the Jews are to be again united.   Romans 11:25-26  
 
God's love for his church is infinite.  His care over her from the beginning has been unceasing.  He has suffered no afflictions to come upon her, but such as were necessary for her purification, and he has made them all subservient to her enlargement and final triumph.  He has appointed her to universal dominion over the hearts of men, and her progress is continually onward towards that blessed day when in righteousness she shall be established.

title: Isaiah 54:11
text:
Thy stones; the stones of Zion's walls and battlements. 
 
  Sapphires; compare  Revelation of John 21:18-21 .  The preciousness of the materials shows the excellence and glory of the city.

title: Isaiah 54:15
text:
They shall surely gather together; the enemies of Zion to seek her hurt. 
 
  Not by me; not only without, but against my authority.

title: Isaiah 54:16
text: I have created the smith--the waster; he who created the maker of deadly weapons, and the waster who employs them, can protect his people against all injury from them.

title: Isaiah 55:1
text:
In the preceding chapter the triumph of Zion over all her foes is exhibited; in the present, all the inhabitants of the world are invited to come and partake of the blessings which God gives to her true members. 
 
  Buy--without money and without price; the blessings of salvation are to be bought, because they must be earnestly sought after, and every thing forsaken for them,  Matthew 13:44-46 Luke 14:33  they are to be bought "without money and without price," because they must be received as God's free gift through Christ. 
 
God makes a most free and gracious offer of salvation to all men, so that none need despair of his mercy who are willing to receive it as a free gift through Jesus Christ.

title: Isaiah 55:2
text: All who make worldly good their portion, or who seek to save themselves by their own righteousness, are spending "money for that which is not bread," and their spirits must remain empty and unsatisfied.  It is only God's salvation that can fill the human soul.

title: Isaiah 55:3
text:
The sure mercies of David; the sure mercies promised to David. These are the contents of the everlasting covenant.  Why they are called "sure" is explained in  Psalms 89:34-35 .  The promise to David was, "Thy house and thy throne shall be established for ever."  II Samuel 7:16 , compared with  Psalms 89:19-37 .  This promise is fulfilled in Christ,  Luke 1:32-33 ; so that he is the sum of "the sure mercies of David." 
 
God has pledged his own glorious perfections that all who seek salvation through Christ shall find it.  Sooner shall heaven and earth pass away, than any soul be put to shame that makes Jesus its confidence.

title: Isaiah 55:4
text:
Him; the Messiah. 
 
  A witness to the people, a leader and commander;  John 18:1

title: Isaiah 55:5
text: A nation that thou knowest not, and nations that knew not thee; the Gentiles.

title: Isaiah 55:6
text: God now tenderly calls sinners to himself, and if they seek him they shall find him.  But if they refuse, the day is coming when he will no longer call, and can no longer be found.

title: Isaiah 55:7
text: God has no pleasure in the death of sinners.  He waits with much longsuffering for their repentance, that he may pardon them, and receive them into his bosom of infinite love.

title: Isaiah 55:10
text: To God's ministers, who are deeply conscious of their weakness and many infirmities, it is an unspeakable consolation that he has promised that his words shall not return unto him void; so that, in delivering their message to sinners, they can confidently leave with him the results, assured that it shall accomplish that which he pleases.

title: Isaiah 55:12
text:
Ye shall go out; from your bondage.  The promised redemption is to be taken in the widest sense, and not restricted to deliverance from the Babylonish captivity, which was only one of the bright series of God's interpositions in behalf of his church. 
 
vv 12-13. 
 
The deliverances which God vouchsafes to his children in this vale of tears, are earnests and pledges of that last perfect redemption when the mountains and the hills shall break forth before them into singing, as their ransomed spirits ascend to the new Jerusalem, there to be for ever with the Lord.

title: Isaiah 56:1
text:
vv 1-7. 
 
As no outward privileges can secure to any man the spiritual blessings of God's covenant with Abraham, so no outward disabilities can debar any man from the enjoyment of them.  Everywhere, and in all ages of the world, it has been true, that "he that feareth God and worketh righteousness is accepted of him."

title: Isaiah 56:3
text:
The son of the stranger; the Gentile, whom the Mosaic law did not admit to the full privileges of an Israelite. 
 
  The eunuch--dry tree;  Deuteronomy 23:1  These words indicate the approaching abolition of all outward and national distinctions among God's people.

title: Isaiah 56:4
text: Take hold of my covenant; embrace its privileges, which belonged to all true believers.   Romans 4:11

title: Isaiah 56:7
text: My holy mountain--my house of prayer; Zion, with the temple, the seat of God's public worship under the old covenant, and the representative of the true church in all ages.

title: Isaiah 56:8
text:
Others to him; others to Israel than Israelites, that is, Gentiles. 
 
  Besides those; that is, besides those of his own people.  The words are a prophecy of the union of Jews and Gentiles in one church.  John 10:16  
 
The union of Jews and Gentiles under Christ in one spiritual fold will be the fulfilment of the original covenant with Abraham, "In thee shall all families of the earth be blessed."   Genesis 12:3

title: Isaiah 56:9
text:
Come to devour; to devour Israel, neglected by those whom God has appointed to be his watchmen,  Isaiah 56:10 .  Compare  Ezekiel 34:5 ;  John 10:12-13 .  Through the remainder of this chapter and the three following, the prophet rebukes the sins of God's visible church. 
 
vv 9-11. 
 
When the pastors of God's church are ignorant of their duty, indolent, self-indulgent, and devoted to their own private ends, the neglected flock becomes an easy prey to the destroyer.  Thus in all ages the unfaithfulness of the watchmen has been the chief cause of the desolations of Zion.

title: Isaiah 56:10
text: Bark; that is, defend the flock.

title: Isaiah 57:1
text:
Perisheth; dies. 
 
  Taken away from the evil to come; compare  II Kings 22:20 . 
 
When iniquity abounds in a nation, and the righteous become few, it is a sign that evil days are at hand.

title: Isaiah 57:2
text: Shall rest in their beds; that is, in their tombs.   Job 3:17  The rest of the body in the grave, is an emblem of the higher rest of the soul in heaven.   Revelation of John 14:13

title: Isaiah 57:3
text: Sons of the sorceress--seed of the adulterer; race of sorcerers and adulterers; as wicked man are called the children of the devil.  John 8:44

title: Isaiah 57:4
text:
Draw out the tongue; thrust it out in derision. 
 
God's faithful servants must be content to bear the scorn and derision of the ungodly, for so did they treat the prophets and apostles of old, and Christ himself, the Lord of prophets and apostles.

title: Isaiah 57:5
text:
Slaying the children; sacrificing them to idols.  This sin, as well as sorcery and idolatry, was practised by Manasseh, to whose reign many refer the present description.  See  II Kings 21:3-7 II Chronicles 33:3-9 . 
 
vv 5-12. 
 
The root of idolatry, with all its abominations, is "an evil heart of unbelief in departing from the living God."  It is because men have neither love for God's service, nor faith in his presence and power, that they multiply their efforts to find salvation by their own devices--only to sink deeper in misery and ruin.

title: Isaiah 57:6
text:
Smooth stones; these seem to have been stones set up in the valleys as objects of idolatrous worship. 
 
  Stream; that is, torrent-bed, like that of the valley of Hinnom, which was the seat of idolatrous rites.   II Chronicles 28:3 II Chronicles 33:6 Jeremiah 32:35  
 
  Thy portion--thy lot; thou hast chosen them and not God for thy portion.

title: Isaiah 57:7
text:
Lofty and high mountain; high places were selected by the ancients for sacrifices, whether to the true God,  I Samuel 9:12 I Kings 3:2 I Kings 3:4 I Kings 18:30   II Chronicles 33:17  or, as here to idols,  Numbers 22:41 I Kings 11:7 II Kings 17:32  
 
  Set thy bed; idolatry is described as spiritual adultery; a common figure with the prophets.

title: Isaiah 57:8
text:
Doors--posts; of thy house. 
 
  Thy remembrance; the image of thy idol. 
 
  Gone up; upon thy bed.   Isaiah 57:7

title: Isaiah 57:9
text:
To the king; probably the king of Egypt.   Isaiah 30:1-31:9   The mention of "messengers" shows that a heathen prince is meant, whose alliance Judah sought in an idolatrous spirit. 
 
  With ointment; as a present.   Hosea 12:1

title: Isaiah 57:10
text:
In the greatness of thy way; in the multitude of thy journeys to obtain foreign aid. 
 
  Found the life of thy hand; found thy hand still strong for further effort. 
 
  Grieved; rather, "weakened," exhausted with toil.

title: Isaiah 57:11
text:
Of whom; of what foreign foe.  The fear of the Jews, which led them to seek help from the worship of false gods and the alliance of heathen kings, was unreasonable; since their covenant God was almighty, and faithful to his engagements. 
 
  Lied; been false to me. 
 
  Held my peace; borne thy waywardness in silence. 
 
  Thou fearest me not; the result of my forbearance is only thy continued sinfulness.   Ecclesiastes 8:11 Romans 2:4-5

title: Isaiah 57:12
text: Thy righteousness; its true character, showing that it is no righteousness.

title: Isaiah 57:13
text: Companies; literally "gatherings," thy idol-gods and foreign alliances.

title: Isaiah 57:14
text: And shall say; he shall see the highway for Israel's redemption in preparation, and shall exhort all God's servants to cooperate in the work of completing it.  See note on  Isaiah 55:12 .

title: Isaiah 57:15
text: Though heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain God, his chosen temple is the soul of the humble and contrite; and his blessed presence fills it with light and peace and strength.

title: Isaiah 57:16
text:
For the spirit should fail before me; were I to deal with my people after their sins, they could not endure my wrath.  Job 9:3 Psalms 78:38-39  
 
The best of men could not endure God's wrath for a moment, were he to deal with them in strict justice.  Our only hope is in his mercy through Christ.

title: Isaiah 57:17
text: The shame and guilt of men's wickedness belongs to them; but the glory of their repentance and obedience to God alone.

title: Isaiah 57:18
text:
I have seen his ways; his ways of perverseness. 
 
  Heal him; convert him, and thus restore him to my favor.  The doctrine here taught is, that God will have mercy upon his people for his own name's sake, and not for their sake.   Ezekiel 36:21 Ezekiel 36:31-32

title: Isaiah 57:19
text:
The fruit of the lips; thanksgiving and praise for salvation. 
 
  Far off--near; to all the penitent of Israel, at home and abroad. 
 
vv 19-21. 
 
God knows how to distinguish between the righteous and the wicked in his visible church.  To the former he will give peace and comfort in this life, and in the life to come glory everlasting; but the latter shall have disquietude here, and inherit "shame and everlasting contempt."

title: Isaiah 57:20
text: The wicked; the wicked in Israel, such as have been described in this chapter.  But the words apply to all wicked men.

title: Isaiah 58:1
text: God's ambassadors must not spare the sins of his people, whatever be the rank and standing of the transgressors, but must rebuke them with all plainness and fidelty.

title: Isaiah 58:2
text: Great exactness and scrupulousness in respect to the outward observances of religion is often connected with great wickedness of heart and life.

title: Isaiah 58:3
text:
Afflicted our soul; by such mortifications as are mentioned  Isaiah 58:5 . 
 
  Find pleasure; indulge your lusts. 
 
  Your labors; the oppressive services which you impose upon your dependents.  This is the way of all Pharisees, who "disfigure their faces, that they may appear unto men to fast," and at the same time "devour widows' houses," and practise "extortion and excess."  Matthew 6:16 Matthew 23:14 Matthew 23:25  
 
When men complain that their services are not noticed and rewarded by God, they show clearly that their supposed services are an abomination in his sight, the fruit of formality and self-righteousness.

title: Isaiah 58:4
text:
For strife and debate; their fasting was a cloak for strife and debate.  Compare  Matthew 23:14 . 
 
  On high; in heaven.  Such fasting as this will not gain for you acceptance with God. 
 
vv 4-7. 
 
The true spirit of fasting lies in inward sorrow for sin, and hearty renunciation of it in every form.  Outward mortifications are of no value, except as they express the inward humiliation of the soul before God.  When men cleave to their wicked practices, and seek to cover them under the cloak of outward rites and penances, they provoke the wrath of Him who cannot be deceived and will not be mocked.  Isaiah 1:11 Isaiah 1:17 I Samuel 15:22 Psalms 50:8-15 Joel 2:12 Joel 2:13 Amos 5:21-24   Micah 6:6-8 Matthew 6:16-18

title: Isaiah 58:7
text: From thine own flesh; thy brethren.   Genesis 29:14 Genesis 37:27 Nehemiah 5:5  But this must be understood of all who need our help.  Compare our Lord's answer to the question, "Who is my neighbor?"   Luke 10:29-37

title: Isaiah 58:8
text:
Thy righteousness shall go before thee; before Israel, to remove all obstacles from his path.  The reference is to the journey from Egypt to the land of Canaan. 
 
  The glory of the Lord; an allusion to the pillar of cloud and fire, which went behind the Israelites in their passage through the Red sea, and protected them from Pharaoh and his host.   Exodus 14:19-20  
 
vv 8-12. 
 
When God's people truly repent of their sins, and bring forth fruits meet for repentance, he does not delay to hear their prayers, and bless them with his presence and salvation.

title: Isaiah 58:9
text: The putting forth of the finger; a sign of scorn, like making a wide mouth, and drawing out the tongue.   Isaiah 57:4

title: Isaiah 58:10
text: Draw out thy soul; let thy compassion go forth in deeds of love.

title: Isaiah 58:13
text:
From the sabbath; from trespassing upon its sanctity. 
 
  The holy of the Lord, honorable; that is, call the holy day of the Lord an honorable day. 
 
vv 13-14. 
 
God has appointed the Sabbath as a day of holy rest, not only from worldly labor, but also from worldly thoughts and conversation.  They only call it "a delight" and "honorable" who, with glad and willing hearts, devote it sacred hours to communion with God and spiritual labors for the good of their fellow men; and all such receive an abundant reward in the light of God's countenance and the rich communications of his grace.

title: Isaiah 58:14
text: Ride upon the high places of the earth; have victory and dominion over thine enemies.   Deuteronomy 32:13 Deuteronomy 33:29 .  Compare  Ezekiel 36:2 .

title: Isaiah 59:1
text:
vv 1-5. 
 
When God withdraws from his people the light of his countenance and leaves them in darkness and affliction, it is not from his unwillingness to hear their prayers, or want of power to save them, but because of their iniquities unrepented of and unforsaken.

title: Isaiah 59:5
text:
Hatch cockatrice's eggs, and weave the spider's web; form mischievous plans. 
 
  Eateth of their eggs; has any thing to do with their wicked devices. 
 
  That which is crushed breadeth out into a viper; the operation of their plans is like breaking open a cockatrice's egg, by which a venomous serpent is let loose.

title: Isaiah 59:6
text:
Shall not become garments; their iniquitous schemes shall not profit them. 
 
vv 6-14. 
 
All the devices of transgressors to deliver themselves from trouble without forsaking their sins and returning to God in faith and obedience, are vain.  That there shall be no peace to the wicked is his appointment, and men cannot alter it.

title: Isaiah 59:9
text: Judgment--justice; God's judgment, as manifested in the salvation of his people and the destruction of his foes.   Isaiah 59:11

title: Isaiah 59:14
text: Judgment--justice; between man and man.

title: Isaiah 59:15
text:
vv 15-21. 
 
When wickedness comes in like a flood upon God's church, and there is no human arm to stay it, he will interpose for the glory of his own name and the fulfilment of his promises to Zion.  By his mighty judgments, working together with his word and Spirit, he will purify her from transgressors, and enlarge her borders until all nations are converted to her.

title: Isaiah 59:16
text:
He saw that there was no man; that is, as immediately explained, no man to intercede in behalf of truth and equity. 
 
  Brought salvation unto him; more exactly, "saved for himself;" that is, saved his people for his own glory. 
 
  His righteousness; which bound him to maintain the cause of truth.

title: Isaiah 59:17
text:
Vengeance; to be executed upon the wicked. 
 
  Zeal; for his own cause and the glory of his own name.

title: Isaiah 59:18
text: The islands; the remote heathen nations that are banded together against him and his Anointed.  These words describe the mighty judgments by which the kingdom of Satan is to be destroyed, and the kingdom of Christ established over all the earth, as is plain from the verses that follow.  Compare  Revelation of John 19:11-21 .

title: Isaiah 59:21
text:
With them; them that turn from transgression in Jacob, that is, the true people of God. 
 
  My Spirit--and my words; God pledges to his church for all coming ages his word of truth, and his Spirit to give it efficacy.  This glorious promise contains the secret of her unconquerable power, and thus the prophet returns again to the latter-day glory of Zion.

title: Isaiah 60:1
text:
Arise, shine; the address is to Zion, that is, God's church, of which the literal Zion was the representative. 
 
God's covenant with Zion is, that his word and Spirit shall dwell with her for ever.  These are mightier than the powers of darkness; so that in all her conflicts with them it is certain that she will, in the end, prevail.  Thus her progress must be onward, until God shall at last bruise Satan under her feet, and give her a complete victory over him. Then will arise upon this world the long-promised day of millennial glory, whose brightness and blessedness shall far exceed what we in our darkness and ignorance are able to conceive.

title: Isaiah 60:5
text:
Shall fear; be filled with awe at this token of God's presence and power. 
 
  Be enlarged; swell with joy.

title: Isaiah 60:6
text:
Midian; east and south of the Moabites, who occupied the eastern border of the Dead sea southward from the Arnon. 
 
  Ephah; a tribe of the Midianites. 
 
  Sheba; in the south of Arabia.

title: Isaiah 60:7
text: Kedar--Nebaioth; northern tribes of Arabia.  The different people here mentioned represent all nations.

title: Isaiah 60:12
text: Serve thee; this is to be understood of a willing spiritual subjection to Christ the Head of the church; not of an outward and forcible subjection, according to the false expectation of the ancient Jews.

title: Isaiah 60:13
text: To beautify the place of my sanctuary; the enlargement and glory of God's spiritual temple are here described under an image drawn from Solomon's temple, the wood of which came from Lebanon.   I Kings 5:1-15

title: Isaiah 60:17
text: For brass I will bring gold--for stones iron; every thing shall be made more excellent.  Compare  Isaiah 9:10 .

title: Isaiah 61:1
text:
The Messiah, through whom alone the triumphs of Zion described in the preceding chapter are achieved, is now again distinctly brought to view.  We must not, however, restrict these words to our Lord's personal ministry.  His Spirit dwelt in the prophets before, and in the apostles after his advent; and it dwells now in all his faithful ministers; so that through them instrumentally, not less than by his personal labors when he was on earth, he preaches good tidings to the meek, binds up the broken hearted, and sets free the captives of Satan. 
 
  Anointed me;  Acts 4:27 Acts 10:1 
 
vv 1-3. 
 
The Lord Jesus came "to save that which was lost," and a true apprehension of our lost condition will make him a precious Saviour to our souls.  To the self-righteous and worldly-minded, who "have their portion in this life," he has no beauty that they should desire him; but to the sorrowful and broken-hearted, who mourn because of their bondage to sin, and feel that they have no power to deliver themselves, he is "the chiefest among ten thousand," and "altogether lovely."  Luke 4:18-19 Isaiah 11:4 Isaiah 57:15 Isaiah 66:2 Psalms 51:17 Matthew 5:3-5 Matthew 9:13 Matthew 18:11   Luke 18:13-14 John 16:20

title: Isaiah 61:2
text:
The acceptable year; the year of God's favor to Zion; the same as the "year of my redeemed,"  Isaiah 63:4 , and the "set time to favor Zion,"  Psalms 102:13 . 
 
  The day of vengeance; upon Zion's enemies.

title: Isaiah 61:3
text: The oil of joy; the allusion is to the use of oil on festive occasions.   II Samuel 14:2 Psalms 23:5 Matthew 6:17

title: Isaiah 61:4
text: The old wastes; of Zion.  Compare  Isaiah 49:8 Isaiah 58:12 .

title: Isaiah 61:5
text: Strangers shall stand--vine-dressers; see note on  Isaiah 14:2 .

title: Isaiah 61:6
text: Priests of the Lord; as offering to him spiritual sacrifices.  The reference is to  Exodus 19:6 , where the Israelites are called "a kingdom of priests."  In this and the preceding verse, the distinction between ancient Israel and the surrounding "strangers" and "sons of the alien," is transferred to the true spiritual Israel and those without her inclosure.

title: Isaiah 61:7
text:
Double; a double reward.  The recompense shall exceed the shame. 
 
  They shall rejoice; the sons of Zion.  The address changes, as often elsewhere, from the second to the third person. 
 
  In their land; in their own land after their restoration from captivity.  But the deliverance of Israel from captivity represents here the redemption of God's people in the widest sense. 
 
The chastisement which God inflicts upon his people is often long-continued.  But the harvest of righteousness and peace and joy that springs from it will be so abundant, that the suffering will be forgotten in comparison with the "far more exceeding and eternal weight of glory" that follows.

title: Isaiah 61:8
text:
Love judgment--burnt-offering; God's love of righteousness, and hatred of hypocrisy and wickedness, move him to interpose in behalf of his people. 
 
  I will direct their work in truth; rather, "I will give their reward in truth."

title: Isaiah 61:9
text: God will not only save his people, but will compel all nations to see and acknowledge that their salvation is from himself.

title: Isaiah 61:10
text:
I will greatly rejoice; the speaker seems to be the same as in the first verse of the following chapter, that is, the prophet speaking in the name of Zion's watchman.  Compare  Isaiah 62:6 . 
 
All "our righteousness" are loathsome and abominable, but the garment of Christ's righteousness and salvation, wherewith he clothes his people, is excellent and glorious in the view of all beholders; it fills the hearts of its possessors with "the peace of God, which passeth understanding," with "joy unspeakable, and full of glory."

title: Isaiah 62:1
text:
Will I not hold my peace--will not rest; from intercession with God for Zion.  Compare  Isaiah 62:6-7 . 
 
God will be inquired of by his people for the fulfilment of his glorious promises.  It is in answer to their fervent prayers, that he appears for their salvation; and in this work of intercession, Zion's watchmen are called to take the lead.   Isaiah 62:6-7

title: Isaiah 62:2
text: A new name; like that mentioned in  Isaiah 62:4 , denoting her new and glorious character and condition.  Compare  Revelation of John 2:17 .

title: Isaiah 62:3
text:
Crown-diadem; these figures denote her excellence and dignity. 
 
  In the hand of the Lord; under his safe-keeping.

title: Isaiah 62:5
text:
Thy sons marry thee; viewed in one aspect, the church is the mother of believers, for in her they are spiritually born; in another, she is their bride, for they have chosen her, and are devoted to her welfare. This blending of figures in metaphor is natural and beautiful. 
 
The true children of Zion prefer her above their chief joy, and are willing to give both their substance and their life to the advancement of her welfare.

title: Isaiah 62:6
text:
Watchmen; the ministers of the church, which is here represented by Jerusalem. 
 
  Make mention of the Lord; rather, "put the Lord in remembrance," that is, of his promises to Jerusalem.   Isaiah 43:26 Jeremiah 14:21

title: Isaiah 62:8
text:
vv 8-12. 
 
Though all the powers of darkness are combined against Zion to desolate and destroy her, they cannot hinder her triumph.  This is made sure to her by the oath of Jehovah; what he has promised he will perform in the eyes of all nations, so that they shall be compelled to acknowledge that she is "the redeemed of the Lord."

title: Isaiah 62:10
text: Go through the gates; of Babylon, in escaping from captivity. Compare  Isaiah 48:20 Isaiah 52:11-12 .  But we must not restrict the prophet's words to the literal deliverance from Babylon.  This is rather to be considered as an earnest and pledge of greater deliverances in the coming days of the Messiah's kingdom.

title: Isaiah 63:1
text:
Cometh from Edom; cometh as a conqueror from Edom, where he has inflicted vengeance upon the foes of Zion.  The Edomites were among the bitterest enemies of the Jews, and they here represent all the enemies of God's people. 
 
  Bozrah; one of the principal cities of Edom, lying south-east of the Dead sea. 
 
vv 1-6. 
 
God corrects his own people in measure, for their sanctification and future enlargement; but their enemies are crushed and destroyed by his judgments, like grapes beneath the feet of them that tread the wine press.

title: Isaiah 63:3
text:
Trodden the wine-press; destroyed my enemies, who are compared to grapes trodden in the wine-press.  The work which Jehovah here performs is elsewhere ascribed to Christ.   Revelation of John 19:15   Compare  John 5:19-23 . 
 
  Their blood; literally, their juice, in allusion to the juice of trampled grapes, which here represents the blood of God's enemies.

title: Isaiah 63:4
text: The year of my redeemed; the year of their deliverance; the same as "the acceptable year of the Lord."   Isaiah 61:2

title: Isaiah 63:5
text: I looked; compare  Isaiah 59:16 .

title: Isaiah 63:6
text: Their strength; rather, "their blood," as the same word is rendered  Isaiah 63:3 , where see note.

title: Isaiah 63:7
text:
I will mention the loving-kindnesses of the Lord; throughout the remainder of this and the following chapter the prophet, in the name of the pious remnant among the Jews, acknowledges God's great goodness to his covenant people, confesses their sins, and supplicates the return of his favor. 
 
vv 7-19. 
 
The prayerful review of God's dealings with his covenant people is eminently profitable to believers.  While it humbles them in view of man's weakness, waywardness, and inconstancy, it encourages them in view of God's power and faithfulness, and the glorious manifestations he has made of his purpose to destroy the kingdom of Satan, and establish the kingdom of his Son Jesus Christ over all the earth.

title: Isaiah 63:9
text: The Angel of his presence; the Angel, in whose person Jehovah was present.   Exodus 14:19 Exodus 23:20-23 Exodus 32:34   From a comparison of these passages with  Genesis 18:1-33 Exodus 33:14 Numbers 22:22-35 Joshua 5:13-15   Judges 6:11-23 Judges 13:1-24 , we learn that the Angel of God's presence was Jehovah himself.  And since "no man hath seen God at any time," it must have been he who "was in the beginning with God," and "was God," manifesting himself in vision as he was afterwards "manifest in the flesh."

title: Isaiah 63:11
text:
Then; in their affliction. 
 
  He remembered; Israel remembered. 
 
  Shepherd of his flock; Moses.

title: Isaiah 63:13
text: In the wilderness; that is, in the open desert, which offers no obstruction to the course of the horse.

title: Isaiah 63:14
text: Down into the valley; that is, to rest there in a quiet and safe retreat.

title: Isaiah 63:15
text:
Look down; the prophet speaks in the name of the church. 
 
  Sounding; yearning motion.  See note on  Isaiah 16:11 .

title: Isaiah 63:16
text: Abraham be ignorant--acknowledge us not; though we be not, "according to the flesh," the children of Abraham and Israel.  We need not understand these words of Gentiles in contrast with Jews.  They are rather the prayer of the whole church, Jewish and Gentile; and they contain an intimation that, in the days of the Messiah, "the children of Abraham" shall no longer be reckoned according to outward descent. Compare  Romans 4:11-12 .

title: Isaiah 63:17
text: Made us to err--hardened our heart; compare  Isaiah 6:9-10 Isaiah 29:10 .

title: Isaiah 63:18
text: The people--have possessed it; the promised land.

title: Isaiah 63:19
text: Over them; over their enemies.

title: Isaiah 64:1
text:
Might flow down; compare  Judges 5:5 Psalms 97:5 Micah 1:4 Nahum 1:5 . 
 
vv 1-4. 
 
Every deliverance which God has vouchsafed to his people is not only a manifestation of his power to save, but a pledge that he will exert that power to make the cause of truth and righteousness triumphant.

title: Isaiah 64:4
text: Seen, O God beside thee; or, "seen a God beside thee who doeth so for him that waiteth for him;" that is, doeth wonders.  The apostle Paul applies these words to the wisdom of God as manifested in the plan of redemption, "which none of the princes of this world knew."  I Corinthians 2:6-10

title: Isaiah 64:5
text:
Thou meetest; with thy favor. 
 
  Rejoiceth and worketh righteousness; worketh righteousness with holy gladness. 
 
  In those; probably, in thy ways. 
 
  Continuance; permanency; that is, firm prosperity. 
 
  Shall be saved; by continuing in them.

title: Isaiah 64:6
text: To see and acknowledge our own utter vileness, emptiness, and weakness, is an indispensable preparation for receiving the righteousness "which is through the faith of Christ, the righteousness which is of God by faith."

title: Isaiah 64:7
text:
Calleth upon thy name--to take hold of thee; earnestly intercedes with thee in behalf of thy people. 
 
The want of a fervent spirit of intercessory prayer is one of the saddest proofs of God's absence from his people, and its return is a sure token that he is again among them and preparing to bless them.

title: Isaiah 64:8
text: We have a right to plead our entire dependence upon God as a reason why he should interpose for our salvation; but this must always be done in the spirit of repentance and active obedience.

title: Isaiah 64:9
text:
vv 9-12. 
 
The depressed and desolate condition of Zion is a valid argument with God why he should interpose for her salvation.  He has promised to make her "an eternal excellency, a joy of many generations."   Isaiah 60:15

title: Isaiah 65:1
text:
vv 1-2. 
 
  Them that asked not for me; the Gentiles. 
 
  A rebellious people; Israel.  See the apostle Paul's explanation of these two verses,  Romans 10:20-21 .  The prophet then proceeds to rebuke the Jews for their sins, and to show them that the kingdom of God shall be taken from them and given to others. 
 
Christ will always have a seed to serve him.  When the great body of the Jewish people rejected him, he took from them the kingdom of God and gave it to the Gentiles.  so will he continue to deal with every branch of his visible church that proves unfaithful to its high calling.

title: Isaiah 65:3
text:
Sacrificeth; to idols. 
 
  In gardens; which were a common resort for idolators. 
 
  Upon altars of brick; literally, "upon bricks."  Some suppose an allusion to the command given,  Exodus 20:24-25 , that God's altars should be made of earth or unhewn stone.  But it is more probable that the bricks themselves contained images or symbols of their gods.

title: Isaiah 65:4
text:
Among the graves--in the monuments; they used sepulchral caves for their idolatrous rites.  The word rendered "monuments" rather signifies recesses, caverns in the rocky cliffs. 
 
  Eat swine's flesh; which was forbidden by the law of Moses,  Leviticus 11:7 , and was undoubtedly connected with idolatrous observances.

title: Isaiah 65:5
text:
A smoke in my nose, a fire; they excite my wrath.  Compare  Psalms 18:8 . 
 
Great wickedness and great self-righteousness are often found united in the same persons and communities.

title: Isaiah 65:7
text: When the children sanction and perpetuate the sins of their fathers, God will recompense both together into their bosom.  Genesis 15:16 Matthew 23:32 Matthew 23:34-36

title: Isaiah 65:8
text:
New wine; that is, juice from which new wine can be made. 
 
  The cluster; probably a good cluster among a mass of corrupt clusters which the vintages are destroying. 
 
  A blessing is in it; God has blessed it, and thus made it valuable. here, as often elsewhere, the prophet foretells the preservation of a pious remnant amid the general destruction of the people.  Isaiah 4:3 Isaiah 6:13 Isaiah 10:20-23 Isaiah 11:11 Isaiah 17:6-8 Isaiah 24:13 Isaiah 30:17  
 
vv 8-16. 
 
The same wind which blows away the chaff, cleanses the wheat and makes it ready for the garner; so the same judgments of God which destroy the wicked from among his people, purify the righteous and prepare them for a more abundant increase.

title: Isaiah 65:11
text:
Ye; the mass of the Jewish people. 
 
  That troop--that number; "Gad" and "Meni," names of false gods.

title: Isaiah 65:14
text: My servants; the true worshippers of Jehovah,  Isaiah 65:9-10 .

title: Isaiah 65:15
text:
Shall slay thee; the outward Israel. 
 
  His servants; the true Israel; the same as the seed which God will bring forth out of Jacob.   Isaiah 65:9  
 
  By another name; the church of God shall no longer be named from Israel, but from Christ, without respect to outward descent.

title: Isaiah 65:17
text:
New heavens and a new earth; the new and glorious order of things under the Messiah.  There is no necessity for limiting this promise to the beginning of the Christian dispensation, or even to this world.  It includes the whole history of Christ's kingdom, to its final consummation in heaven.  Compare  Revelation of John 21:1 . 
 
vv 17-25. 
 
Many prophets and righteous men desired to see the Redeemer's wonderful works, and to hear his words of heavenly wisdom, but died without beholding him; so they who come after us shall enjoy such manifestations of his glory as our eyes have not been permitted to witness; for the progress of his kingdom must be onward, from glory to glory, until it shall end in the everlasting light and blessedness of heaven.

title: Isaiah 65:20
text:
An infant of days; whose life is only a few days. 
 
  An old man that hath not filled his days; one who, though he has reached an advanced age, yet dies prematurely. 
 
  The child shall die a hundred years old; one who dies at that age shall be considered as dying in childhood. 
 
  The sinner being a hundred years old shall be accursed; shall be accursed by being prematurely cut off at the age of a hundred years. Compare  Isaiah 65:22 .  But we need not interpret the words of this verse literally.  They may be understood as a promise of great spiritual vigor under the figure of extreme longevity.

title: Isaiah 65:22
text: As the days of a tree; such as an oak, which is supposed to live a thousand years and longer.

title: Isaiah 65:25
text:
The wolf--the bullock; see note on  Isaiah 11:6-9 . 
 
  Dust shall be the serpent's meat; the original curse shall be executed upon the serpent and his seed.   Genesis 3:14   The kingdom of Satan shall be crushed and prostrate.

title: Isaiah 66:1
text:
Where is the house that ye build unto me? what house can ye build, that shall be worthy of my majesty?  Compare  I Kings 8:27 . 
 
vv 1-4. 
 
God is not "worshipped with men's hands, as though he needed any thing."  No magnificence of outward rites can please him, when the heart and hands are polluted with iniquity.

title: Isaiah 66:2
text:
All those things; heaven and earth: they have been of old my temple, and I need no dwelling-place made with hands.  Compare  Acts 7:48-50 Acts 17:24-25 . 
 
  To this man will I look; with approbation; the same as, "with him will I dwell,"  Isaiah 57:15   Jehovah shows what is the temple which he loves.

title: Isaiah 66:3
text:
Killeth an ox; in sacrifice. 
 
  As if he slew a man; in sacrifice.  The meaning is, that all the services prescribed by the Mosaic law are utterly abominable to God when offered by wicked men and in a wicked spirit.  Compare  Isaiah 1:13-15 .

title: Isaiah 66:4
text: Will choose their delusions; will give them up to fatal delusions.  II Thessalonians 2:11

title: Isaiah 66:5
text:
Ye that tremble at his word; "the Israel of God." 
 
  Your brethren; "Israel after the flesh."  The words of this and the preceding verses, though of general application, were remarkably fulfilled in the character and history of that generation of the Jews who crucified our Lord.  While their hearts and lives were full of wickedness, they attached an inordinate value to the temple and its services, and hated and cast out the Saviour and his followers. 
 
vv 5-24. 
 
In all ages God's humble worshippers have been hated and cast out by the proud and self-righteous.  But he has never failed to appear in due time for their deliverance and the confusion of their persecutors. Amidst the mighty judgments of God upon the enemies of his people, Christ shall continually go forth conquering and to conquer, until all nations have submitted themselves to his authority.  Then the whole earth shall break forth into singing, and shout, "Alleluia, for the Lord God omnipotent reigneth," while the smoke of Satan's kingdom shall go up for ever and ever.  Amen.

title: Isaiah 66:6
text: A voice of noise--recompense to his enemies; fulfilled in the destruction of Jerusalem with its temple by the Chaldeans; but more signally fulfilled in its destruction by the Romans.

title: Isaiah 66:7
text: She travailed; Zion travailed; this and the two following verses seem to refer to the large accession of Gentiles to the church in immediate connection with the rejection of the Jews.

title: Isaiah 66:9
text: Bring to the birth--shut the womb? shall God begin the work of multiplying Zion's offspring, and not complete it?

title: Isaiah 66:11
text: Suck--milk out; Jerusalem, the church, is "the mother" of true believers; and from her, under God, they are nourished unto everlasting life.   Galatians 4:26

title: Isaiah 66:12
text: The glory of the Gentiles like a flowing stream; I will bring the Gentiles with their glory to her like a flowing stream.  Isaiah 60:5-7 Revelation of John 21:24

title: Isaiah 66:17
text:
Sanctify themselves--purify themselves; for idolatrous rites in the gardens. 
 
  Behind one; literally, "after one;" that is, after one as their leader, following his directions.  The word "tree" is not in the original.

title: Isaiah 66:19
text:
Set a sign; perform wonders.  Some refer the sign directly to the appearance of Christ.  Compare  Luke 2:34 . 
 
  Those that escape of them; the pious remnant of Israel; remarkably fulfilled in the days of the apostles, who carried the gospel to the Gentiles, and thus declared God's glory among them. 
 
  Pul-Lud; probably African people. 
 
  Tubal; a people of Asia Minor. 
 
  Javan; Greece.  These contries stand as representatives of all distant nations.

title: Isaiah 66:20
text:
Your brethren; probably, your brethren of the Gentiles.  The address is to "the remnant according to the election of grace."  Under the Mosaic law, all God's people were required to go up to Jerusalem to offer sacrifices and keep the yearly feasts.  The extension of the true religion from Jerusalem over all the earth, is here, as elsewhere, foretold under the figure of God's bringing all nations to Jerusalem to worship him there,  Isaiah 66:23 ; and compare  Isaiah 2:2-4 Micah 4:1-3 Zechariah 14:16-19 . 
 
  For an offering; see  Romans 15:16 .

title: Isaiah 66:21
text: For priests and for Levites; to offer spiritual sacrifices.  I Peter 2:5

title: Isaiah 66:24
text:
They shall go forth; God's worshippers of "all flesh" shall go forth from Jerusalem.  They shall see with their own eyes that their enemies have perished. 
 
  Their worm shall not die--fire be quenched; the carcasses of God's enemies shall be consumed by a worm that dieth not, and a fire that is not quenched.  This terrible imagery represents the everlasting destruction of the wicked.   Mark 9:43-48

title: Jeremiah 1:1
text: Anathoth; a town three or four miles north of Jerusalem.

title: Jeremiah 1:5
text: When the church has need of any service, God raises up and qualifies men for it.

title: Jeremiah 1:6
text: Humility is essential as a preparation for God's service; but we should be careful that it do not degenerate into timidity, and thus hinder us from discharging the work that he assigns to us.

title: Jeremiah 1:7
text:
vv 7-10. 
 
God's ministers should not shrink from any duty that he lays upon them, however arduous and dangerous; but faithfully perform it, assured of his constant presence and help.

title: Jeremiah 1:10
text: To root out--to plant; to declare my purpose to do so.

title: Jeremiah 1:11
text:
vv 11-12. 
 
  An almond-tree--hasten;in the original Hebrew, the words "almond- tree" and "hasten" are the same.  There is also an allusion to the fact that the almond-tree is the earliest tree to blossom and bear fruit in the spring.

title: Jeremiah 1:13
text:
A seething-pot; literally, "a pot blown," that is, having under it a blown fire, which causes it to boil violently.  This is a figure of God's wrath to be executed on the Jews by the Babylonians. 
 
  Toward the north; or, "from the face of the north," is preperable. This represents the seething-pot itself as coming from the north.

title: Jeremiah 1:14
text: Out of the north; though the Babylonians and their allies were to the east of Judea, yet they always entered the land from the north.

title: Jeremiah 1:17
text: To be afraid of God's enemies is the way to bring ourselves into subjection to them.

title: Jeremiah 1:18
text: vv 18-19. Though the wicked may persecute and distress, they can never destroy those whom God protects and helps.

title: Jeremiah 2:2
text: Thy youth--thine espousals; the youth of the nation, when God espoused it to himself by entering into covenant with it.

title: Jeremiah 2:3
text:
First-fruits; the first nation consecrated to God's service, and the first generation of that nation after the establishment of the covenant at Sinai. 
 
  Increase; harvest or ingathering of believers.

title: Jeremiah 2:5
text: The conduct of backsliders greatly dishonors God; it is a virtual declaration before the world that they have tried his service, and found it hard and unreasonable.

title: Jeremiah 2:6
text:
vv 6-7. 
 
The beginning of departure from God is ingratitude and forgetfulness of he mercies; where the remembrance of these is warm and fresh in the soul, it keeps us near to God, and makes communion with him exceedingly sweet and precious.

title: Jeremiah 2:8
text: Pastors; shepherds of the people; that is, rulers, whose duty it was both to obey God's law, and require obedience in others.

title: Jeremiah 2:10
text:
Chittim; to the west; see note on  Isaiah 23:1 . 
 
  Kedar; on the east, in Arabia.

title: Jeremiah 2:11
text: The constancy of the heathen in serving their idols is a standing rebuke of the inconstancy of many worshippers if the living and true God.

title: Jeremiah 2:13
text: God is the eternal and uncreated fountain of good; upon all who cleave to him he bestows life and strength and blessedness; but every device of those who forsake him, and put their confidence in earthly objects, is only a broken cistern that can hold no water, and its end must be disappointment and misery.

title: Jeremiah 2:14
text: Is Israel a servant?--why is he spoiled? since Israel is God's first-born son,  Exodus 4:22 , why is he spoiled as if he were a slave?

title: Jeremiah 2:15
text: Young lions; the northern enemies.   Jeremiah 1:14

title: Jeremiah 2:16
text: Noph--Tahapanes; cities of Egypt.  The Egyptians join with the northern invaders in destroying Judah.

title: Jeremiah 2:18
text:
Sihor; the Nile.   Isaiah 23:3  
 
  The river; the Euphrates.  Drinking the water of these rivers seems to denote the vain efforts of the Jews to obtain help first from one, then from the other of these nations.   II Kings 16:7 II Kings 18:21 Isaiah 30:1-3   Isaiah 31:1-3

title: Jeremiah 2:20
text: Playing the harlot; by serving false gods, which the prophets everywhere regard as spiritual fornication.

title: Jeremiah 2:21
text: The tendency of the human race to degeneracy is a sad and humiliating proof of its fallen condition; so strong is this downward current in families and nations, that nothing but God's grace can preserve them from utter corruption and ruin.

title: Jeremiah 2:22
text:
Wash thee; endeavor to hide thy guilt. 
 
  Nitre; not our nitre, but a mineral substance used anciently as now for soap. 
 
The vain endeavors of sinners to justify themselves, fail to satisfy either their own consciences or the judgment of their fellow sinners; how much more the judgment of God, who knoweth all things.

title: Jeremiah 2:23
text:
The valley; the valley of Hinnom, where the idolatrous Jews sacrificed their children to Moloch.   Jeremiah 7:31  
 
  Traversing her ways; running hither and thither in her wantonness.

title: Jeremiah 2:24
text: At her pleasure; in the excitement of her desire.

title: Jeremiah 2:25
text:
Withhold thy foot--thy throat from thirst; do not wear out thy sandals and make thyself thirsty in the pursuit of false gods. 
 
  There is no hope; my case is desperate, and I must seek the help of idols.

title: Jeremiah 2:27
text:
vv 27-28. 
 
They who forget God in prosperity, and call upon him only in adversity, have no true love for him, and connot expect deliverance.

title: Jeremiah 2:30
text: When a nation persecutes and destroys the messengers by whom God calls it to repentance, the measure of its iniquity is full, and it is near destruction.

title: Jeremiah 2:31
text:
We are lords; or, "we are free" to go where we please. 
 
  Unto thee; unto Jehovah.

title: Jeremiah 2:33
text:
Trimmest--thy way; usest subtle artifices. 
 
  Taught the wicked ones; the wicked women.  Jerusalem has become a leader in idolatry.

title: Jeremiah 2:34
text:
Blood of--the poorest innocents; she has added murder to idolatry. "The poor innocents" are not merely the children sacrificed to Moloch, but the righteous poor whom she has slain. 
 
  Upon all these; probably, in open view, upon all thy skirts, to which God points as it were with the finger.

title: Jeremiah 2:35
text: The self-delusion of sinners has no limits; it leads bold and shameless transgressors to deny their guilt, and persuade themselves that God is not angry with them and will not punish them.

title: Jeremiah 2:36
text: Gaddest thou about--to change thy way; wanderest every way in search of idolatrous alliances.

title: Jeremiah 2:37
text:
Thy hands upon thy head; a posture expressive of grief.  II Samuel 13:19  
 
When God is against a people for their sins, their earthly confidences turn to their destruction.

title: Jeremiah 3:1
text:
Played the harlot; by idolatry, which is spiritual fornication.  So it is represented throughout the book. 
 
  Yet return; God in his great mercy is ever ready to recieve the true penitent.

title: Jeremiah 3:2
text:
Sat for them; waited for thy lovers. 
 
  As the Arabian; as he lies in wait to rob travellers.

title: Jeremiah 3:5
text: Will he reserve his anger for ever? will not God pardon thine iniquity as soon as thou comest to him in true penitence?

title: Jeremiah 3:8
text: Put her away--given her a bill; by giving her over to captivity.  II Kings 17:6-23

title: Jeremiah 3:11
text:
Backsliding Israel--treacherous Judah; Judah is more guilty than Israel, because she has failed to take warning from God's judgments upon her sister nation.   Ezekiel 16:51-52  
 
When men refuse to take warning from the punishment of those whose sinful example they are imitating, they aggravate their guilt, and bring upon themselves severer judgments.

title: Jeremiah 3:12
text:
Toward the north; where Israel was held in captivity. 
 
vv 12.15. 
 
God waits to be acknowledged in the calamities which he sends upon his people; and when they return to him by hearty confession and repentance, he will graciously accept them, and restore them to more than their former prosperity.

title: Jeremiah 3:14
text: One of a city--two of a family; that is, a remnant of you shall be saved.  This purpose of God respecting both Judah and Israel is often repeated in the Old Testament.   Isaiah 10:22

title: Jeremiah 3:16
text:
The ark--of the Lord; the former glory of the ark shall be forgotten in comparison with the greater glory of the future.  Compare  Jeremiah 16:14-15 Isaiah 65:17 .  At the same time the prophet intimates the removal of this outward symbol of God's presence, which took place at the captivity. 
 
The glory of the gospel dispensation is such that, in comparison, there is no glory in the old dispensation which preceded it, and prepared the way for it.   II Corinthians 3:10

title: Jeremiah 3:17
text:
All the nations shall be gathered; a prophecy which can have its complete fulfilment only in "the last days" of the Christian dispensation.  See  Isaiah 2:2-4 Micah 4:1-4 Zechariah 14:16-19 . 
 
Though in the establishment of his church God began with one nation, it was from the beginning his plan to extend it from that nation over all the earth.  The calling of the Gentiles is the fulfilment of the original promise, "In thee shall all families of the earth be blessed."  Genesis 12:3

title: Jeremiah 3:18
text: With the house of Israel; in harmony with it.  Isaiah 11:13 Ezekiel 37:15-28

title: Jeremiah 3:19
