text: When we cleave to God, as children to a father, with a free and willing spirit, he fulfils to us his promises; and when he sends forth the Spirit of his Son into our hearts, we cry, "Abba, Father;" to us belongs the childlike obedience, and to him the glory of it.

title: Jeremiah 3:21
text:
vv 21-25. 
 
  A voice was heard; in these words the prophet anticipates the repentance and supplication of Israel.

title: Jeremiah 4:2
text: Shalt swear, The Lord liveth; swearing by Jehovah's name, when it is performed in sincerity, is an open profession of allegiance to him in opposition to all false gods.  Compare  Isaiah 48:1 .

title: Jeremiah 4:3
text:
Break up your fallow ground; the hearts of the Jews are compared to untilled ground, covered with thorns, and unfit to receive good seed.  Matthew 13:3-8 Matthew 13:18-23   To break it up, is to put away their obduracy and their abominations.  Compare  Ezekiel 18:31 , "Make you a new heart and a new spirit." 
 
True reformation must begin with an inward preparation of the heart to receive and obey God's word; that obedience which is only outward and forced is short-lived, and generally ends in making a man's last worse than the first.   Matthew 12:43-45 Matthew 13:4-7 Matthew 13:19-22

title: Jeremiah 4:4
text:
Circumcise yourselves to the Lord; circumcision was the outward sign of consecration to God.  The Jews are here exhorted to do that inwardly which the outward rite signified.   Deuteronomy 10:16  
 
No outward rite has, in and of itself, any saving efficacy.  The inward grace of which it is the sign can alone bring men into a state of salvation.

title: Jeremiah 4:5
text:
Declare ye; the approaching invasion of the Chaldeans. 
 
  Into the defenced cities; for protection against the invaders.

title: Jeremiah 4:6
text: Toward Zion; calling the people to flee to it as their strong-hold.

title: Jeremiah 4:7
text:
The lion; the Babylonian conqueror. 
 
Wicked kings and nations are under the control of God's providence, and he makes them at his pleasure the ministers of his purposes towards his people, whether of wrath or mercy.

title: Jeremiah 4:9
text: When God forsakes a nation for its sins, its wisdom and strength fail, and it becomes an easy prey to its enemies.

title: Jeremiah 4:10
text:
Thou hast deceived this people; allowed them to be deceived by false prophets.  This was a judgment sent upon them by God for loving falsehood rather than truth.  Compare  II Thessalonians 2:11-12 . 
 
The most dreadful judgment upon a people is, that God should give them up to the delusions of false teachers, who flatter them in sin, and promise them peace in the way of transgression.

title: Jeremiah 4:11
text:
Of the high places; coming over the barren hills.  The reference is to the hot and withering wind from the eastern deserts. 
 
vv 11-31. 
 
The terrible desolations which God brought upon Judah and Jerusalem for their rebellion against him, are a perpetual warning to nations who enjoy the light of Christianity, of the calamities which will overtake them as they depart from him.

title: Jeremiah 4:12
text: Unto me; unto Jehovah, that is, for the execution of his vengeance.

title: Jeremiah 4:13
text: He shall come; the Chaldean monarch.

title: Jeremiah 4:15
text:
From Dan; a city in the northern extremity of the land. 
 
  Mount Ephraim; the mountainous region of Ephraim also lay toward the north, through which the invader would approach Jerusalem.

title: Jeremiah 4:16
text: Watchers; that is, besiegers, as the following verse explains.

title: Jeremiah 4:17
text: Keepers of a field; persons set to guard it against robbers and beasts.

title: Jeremiah 4:19
text: My bowels; the bowels are the seat of compassion.  See note on  Isaiah 16:11 .  In this and the two following verses Zion is the speaker, or the prophet personating Zion.

title: Jeremiah 4:22
text: For my people is foolish, they have not known me; in this verse God speaks.

title: Jeremiah 4:23
text: I beheld; the prophet has a vision of the utter desolation of the land.  The description is borrowed from that of the primitive chaos.  Genesis 1:2

title: Jeremiah 4:24
text: Moved lightly; quivered under God's wrath.  Compare  Isaiah 13:13 .

title: Jeremiah 4:29
text:
The whole city; rather, as the same words are rendered just below, "every city," that is, of Judea. 
 
  They shall go into thickets; the Jews shall go for shelter.

title: Jeremiah 4:30
text:
Rentest thy face; rather, "thine eyes," by applying a black paint to the eyelids.  This is done by passing an instrument smeared with the paint along the lids.  Judah is here compared to a harlot, who, in her eagerness to apply the paint, tears or furrows the lids. 
 
  Thy lovers; the idolatrous allies to whom the Jews looked for help against the Chaldeans.

title: Jeremiah 5:1
text: God often bears long with wicked nations and cities, and withholds his judgments from them, for the sake of the few righteous men which they contain.   Genesis 18:23-32

title: Jeremiah 5:2
text:
Though they say, The Lord liveth; see note to  Jeremiah 4:2 . 
 
vv 2-11. 
 
When corruption and profligacy have pervaded all classes of the community, and God's repeated chastisements have failed to bring them to repentance, then it is certain that their destruction is at hand.

title: Jeremiah 5:10
text: Go ye up; this is addressed to the enemies of Judah.

title: Jeremiah 5:12
text:
They have belied the Lord; while they readily believed the false prophets, they refused to believe the true, and thus charged God himself with falsehood. 
 
  It is not a he; it is not God that speaks by the prophet's lips. 
 
vv 12-17. 
 
The self-flatteries of sinners cannot for a moment stay God's approaching vengenace; at the appointed time it will fall upon them with resistless power, and sweep away them and their delusions together.

title: Jeremiah 5:13
text:
The prophets shall become wind; the language of the unbelieving Jews, who deride the warnings of God's prophets, is continued. 
 
  Thus shall it be done unto them; the evils which the prophets predict shall fall upon themselves, not upon us.

title: Jeremiah 5:16
text: An open sepulchre; ready to swallow up and destroy.  Compare  Psalms 5:9 .

title: Jeremiah 5:18
text: Since God's judgments have for their end the purification and not the destruction of the true Israel, he will take care that his church shall not only survive them, but receive from them new strength and enlargement.

title: Jeremiah 5:23
text:
vv 23-31. 
 
When iniquity abounds among God's professed people, and both teachers and taught are united in maintaining falsehood, they should expect that he will vindicate the cause of truth by terrible manifestations of his wrath.   Isaiah 59:16-18

title: Jeremiah 5:24
text:
The former; which falls in autumn, and prepares the ground or ploughing and sowing. 
 
  The latter; which falls in the spring, and matures the crops. 
 
  Reserveth unto us--the harvest; gives us the harvest in its appointed weeks.

title: Jeremiah 5:25
text: These things--good; the good gifts mentioned in the preceding verse.

title: Jeremiah 5:27
text:
Full of birds; birds caught by stratagem. 
 
  Deceit; wealth gained by deceit.

title: Jeremiah 5:28
text: Overpass the deeds of the wicked; go beyond ordinary sinners in crime.

title: Jeremiah 5:31
text:
What will ye do; what will ye sinners of Judah and Jerusalem do to avert destruction? 
 
  In the end thereof; when God shall bring upon you the consequences of your sins.

title: Jeremiah 6:1
text: Benjamin; Jerusalem lay on the southern border of the tribe of Benjamin.  The Benjamites in great numbers would naturally take refuge in her from the invaders.  But they are here warned to escape, as she will fall into the hands of the enemy.

title: Jeremiah 6:3
text:
Shepherds with their flocks; kings with their armies. 
 
  Shall feed; shall destroy her, as flocks consume pasturage.

title: Jeremiah 6:4
text:
vv 4-5. 
 
  Prepare ye war--destroy her palaces; the impatient language of the enemy.  They regret that they cannot reach her before evening, and resolve to continue the march through the night.

title: Jeremiah 6:7
text: Grief and wounds; the grief and wounds caused by her oppression and violence.

title: Jeremiah 6:9
text:
Turn back thy hand; persist in gleaning.  Jehovah here addresses the enemy. 
 
God is slow to inflict punishment upon his people; it is only after expostulation and warning have proved vain, that he gives them over, as he did Jerusalem of old, to desolating judgments.

title: Jeremiah 6:10
text: Shall I speak; the prophet says this.

title: Jeremiah 6:11
text: Full--weary with holding in; I have forborne to speak, because the people would not listen; but I can refrain no longer.  "The fury of the Lord" is the coming wrath of the Lord, which he was commanded to proclaim.

title: Jeremiah 6:14
text:
They have healed; the false prophets and priests.   Jeremiah 5:31  
 
  Slightly; they have covered over the festering wound of her iniquity, instead of probing it. 
 
vv 14-15. 
 
The aim of all false doctrine is to flatter men with the hope of impunity in sin; and its result is to make them impudent and hardhearted, and thus plunge them into irremediable ruin.

title: Jeremiah 6:16
text:
Stand ye in the ways; to examine and decide which is the right way. 
 
  The old paths; those prescribed of old by God.

title: Jeremiah 6:17
text:
Watchmen; prophets. 
 
  Sound of the trumpet; warning you of approaching danger.  Compare  Ezekiel 33:1-9 .

title: Jeremiah 6:18
text: What is among them; what wickedness demanding my judgments.

title: Jeremiah 6:20
text:
Sheba; a region of southern Arabia. 
 
  Burnt-offerings not acceptable, nor your sacrifices sweet; because they are the offerings of the wicked.   Isaiah 1:11-14  
 
When men's hearts are full of rebellion, and their lives of iniquity, no multiplication of outward rites can be acceptable to God, or avert his displeasure.   Isaiah 58:1-4 Luke 18:9-14

title: Jeremiah 6:21
text:
I will lay stumbling-blocks; see note on  Jeremiah 4:10 . 
 
When men do not love the truth, God leaves them to embrace falsehood, which becomes a stumbling-block, to their destruction.

title: Jeremiah 6:27
text:
I have set thee; God addresses the prophet. 
 
  A tower and a fortress;  Jeremiah 1:1 
  Know and try their way; by the truth which thou proclaimest from me. 
 
The way in which men treat God's faithful serants and their messages, is a true touchstone of their own character.

title: Jeremiah 6:28
text:
vv 28-30. 
 
They who cannot be purifies by God's discipline, must be destroyed by his judgments.

title: Jeremiah 6:29
text: The bellows--the lead; these were destroyed in the vain effort to separate the silver from the dross; that is, to purify the people from sin.  Lead was anciently used in the process of refining.

title: Jeremiah 6:30
text: Reprobate silver; that cannot be refined, and is therefore worthless.

title: Jeremiah 7:1
text:
vv 1-15. 
 
As the Israelites in Samuel's time thought that the presence of God's ark would give them victory over the Philistines, though they repented not of their transgressions against him; so the Jews in Jeremiah's day who burned incense to idols, and their descendants who crucified the Saviour and persecuted his apostles, believed that God's temple, with its divinely appointed services, would make them secure from danger. All who now put their trust for salvation in outward ordinances and privileges, without inward repentance and obedience, are guilty of the same folly, and must come to the same ruin.   Romans 2:28-29

title: Jeremiah 7:4
text: The temple of the Lord are these; these buildings; the temple properly so called, with its several courts.  They said, These are "the temple of the Lord," and therefore he will defend them and all who worship in them from injury.  Thus the Jews put their trust in outward privileges, and not in holiness of heart and life.

title: Jeremiah 7:10
text: We are delivered to do all these abominations; more exactly, "We are delivered; in order to do all these abominations."  The words, "We are delivered," are those of the people expressing their confidence that their relation to God and his temple makes them safe from all fear of evil.  The words that follow, "in order to do all these abominations," are those of the prophet, showing the fruit of this false confidence.

title: Jeremiah 7:11
text: A den of robbers; a den to protect robbers, since they trusted to it for protection in their robberies.  Compare  Matthew 21:13 Mark 11:17

title: Jeremiah 7:12
text: Shiloh; north of Jerusalem, in the tribe of Ephraim.  From Joshua to Samuel it was honored as the abode of the tabernacle and ark.  Joshua 18:1 I Samuel 1:3

title: Jeremiah 7:15
text: Ephraim; that is, the kingdom of Israel, of which Ephraim was the chief tribe.

title: Jeremiah 7:16
text: There is a limit in sin, beyond which God will no longer hear intercessory prayer or delay his judgments.

title: Jeremiah 7:18
text:
The queen of heaven; the moon, worshipped as a female deity. 
 
When the members of a family or community sin together, they must also suffer together.

title: Jeremiah 7:19
text: Me--themselves; does the damage fall on me, or on themselves?

title: Jeremiah 7:21
text:
Put your burnt-offerings unto your sacrifices; by the Mosaic law the burnt-offerings were to be wholly consumed on the altar; but of the peace-offerings a portion only was burned, and upon the remainder the offerer feasted with his friends.  They are here told to eat their burnt-offerings, if they will, with their peace-offerings, for Jehovah will not accept them. 
 
vv 21-23. 
 
God values outward services only as they are expressions of inward love and obedience, and he will not allow the former to be substituted for the latter.

title: Jeremiah 7:22
text: I spake not--concerning burnt-offerings; I made not these, but love and obedience your main duty.  Compare  I Samuel 15:22 Psalms 50:8-15 .

title: Jeremiah 7:24
text:
vv 24-34. 
 
When men refuse to receive the correction of God's word, he will make them feel the power of his anger.  The awful desolation of ancient Jerusalem is a solemn warning to all cities and nations of what awaits them if they imitate her crimes.

title: Jeremiah 7:29
text: Cut off thy hair; as a sign of deep grief.  Isaiah 15:2 Isaiah 22:12 Micah 1:16

title: Jeremiah 8:1
text:
They shall bring out the bones of the kings--out of their graves; the enemy shall do this, probably in their search for hid treasures. Such an exposure of the bones was a great indignity. 
 
vv 1-18. 
 
God's power to curse is as unlimited as his power to bless.  With infinite ease he can bring upon the strongest of his enemies calamity after calamity, until death shall be chosen rather than life.

title: Jeremiah 8:4
text: Shall they fall--not return? a lamentation over the incorrigible perverseness of the people.  Shall the fall of my covenant people be final?  Shall Judah turn away from her God, and never return?

title: Jeremiah 8:7
text: The time of their coming; their annual return in the spring.

title: Jeremiah 8:13
text:
No grapes--the leaf shall fade; the gleaning of the vine and fig-tree, and the withering of their leaves, represent the complete desolation of the land by the armies of the Chaldeans. 
 
  And the things--shall pass away from them; rather, "and I will appoint those who shall overrun them."

title: Jeremiah 8:14
text: Why do we sit still? assemble yourselves; the words of the people, exhorting each other to flee into the defenced cities.

title: Jeremiah 8:16
text:
His horses; the horses of the invader. 
 
  From Dan;  Jeremiah 4:1

title: Jeremiah 8:18
text: When I would comfort myself; the words of the prophet.

title: Jeremiah 8:19
text: Why have they provoked me; Jehovah answers, that it is not his absence from Zion, but her sins that have given the enemy power over her.

title: Jeremiah 8:20
text:
The harvest is past--we are not saved; the words of the people lamenting that all their expectations of help and deliverance have passed away. 
 
To those who fail of God's great salvation, it will be a most bitter reflection that they have misimproved abundant opportunities which will never return.

title: Jeremiah 8:22
text:
No balm--no physician; has Judah no almighty helper?  The balm of Gilead was employed in healing wounds. 
 
  Why then--recovered? the implied answer is, Not for want of balm or a physician, but because she persists in her rebellion. 
 
Christ the great Physician is near to the unconverted, as well as to his church, with the balm of salvation in his hand.  If any remain unhealed, and die in their sins, it will be because they refuse his help, freely and graciously proffered.

title: Jeremiah 9:1
text:
vv 1-2. 
 
While God's faithful servants abhor the ways of wicked men, and loathe their companionship, they feel deep compassion for them in view of the ruin which they are bringing upon themselves.

title: Jeremiah 9:2
text: A lodging-place of wayfaring men; anciently, as now, such lodging-places were erected for the accommodation of caravans.

title: Jeremiah 9:3
text:
vv 3-9. 
 
In this perverse and fallen world it is hard to find any who are worthy of perfect confidence; but when the mass of a people have become thoroughly false and treacherous, their destruction is at hand.

title: Jeremiah 9:6
text: Thy habitation is in the midst of deceit; Jehovah here addresses the prophet.

title: Jeremiah 9:8
text: An arrow shot out; rather, "a murderous arrow."

title: Jeremiah 9:10
text:
For the mountains; that is, on account of their impending desolation. 
 
  The fowl--the beast are fled; a figure to express utter desolation. Compare  Jeremiah 4:25 .

title: Jeremiah 9:12
text:
vv 12-16. 
 
The highest wisdom of statesmen and rulers is to understand that the prosperity of a nation lies in fearing and obeying God, and its destruction in forgetting him and trampling under foot his laws.

title: Jeremiah 9:14
text: Baalim; images of Baal.

title: Jeremiah 9:23
text: Glory in his wisdom--his might--his riches; all these resources would fail to deliver the Jews from the calamities which God was about to bring upon them.

title: Jeremiah 9:24
text: That he understandeth and knoweth me; because a true knowledge of God, which includes love and obedience, is the only salvation of individuals or of nations.

title: Jeremiah 9:25
text:
Punish--circumcised with the uncircumcised; make no distinction between the circumcised Jews and the uncircumcised Gentiles; because, as the next verse explains, the Jews are "uncircumcised in the heart." 
 
vv 25-26. 
 
When God's covenant people imitate the sins of the ungodly, they must expect to suffer punishment with them.

title: Jeremiah 9:26
text: Are in the utmost corners; or, "have the corners of their hair shorn;" a description of the Arabian tribes.

title: Jeremiah 10:2
text:
The signs of heaven; the positions of the stars and planets, eclipses, etc., by which the heathen supposed that the destinies of men were controlled.  From the vanity of these the prophet naturally passes in the following verses, to consider the vanity of idolatry. 
 
In God's word we have a perfect rule of faith and practice, and have no occasion to look to signs and omens, as the heathen do, to learn either our duty or our destiny.

title: Jeremiah 10:3
text:
vv 3-5. 
 
  One cutteth a tree--to do good;  Isaiah 40:19-20 Isaiah 44:9-19 Isaiah 45:1 
 
vv 3-16. 
 
The living God alone, who made heaven and earth, can help and save his worshippers.  All gods of human workmanship must perish with their makers.

title: Jeremiah 10:9
text: Uphaz; perhaps the same as Ophir.

title: Jeremiah 10:14
text: Every man; that is, every idolater.

title: Jeremiah 10:17
text:
Gather up thy wares; as one about to enter upon a journey.  The people of Jerusalem are warned to prepare for going into captivity. 
 
  Of the fortress; or of the besieged city.

title: Jeremiah 10:19
text:
Woe is me; Jerusalem now speaks. 
 
vv 19-22. 
 
God will not overlook the transgressions of his own people, but will visit them with afflictions and chastisement until they learn that in obeying him alone they can find blessedness and salvation.

title: Jeremiah 10:21
text: The pastors; the rulers of Judah and Jerusalem.   Jeremiah 2:8

title: Jeremiah 10:22
text:
Bruit; rumor, report of the invading army. 
 
  Dragons; the original word means wild animals of the jackal family that inhabit ruins.

title: Jeremiah 10:23
text:
Is not in himself; in his own power.  The prophet acknowledges God's supreme control over himself and his people. 
 
vv 23-24. 
 
Every true child of God deeply feels his inability, without God's help, to direct his steps, or to bear the just punishment of his sins.  It is his constant prayer that God would keep him in the ways of holiness, and chasten him with gentleness, so that the discipline shall not overwhelm, but purify him and prepare him for heaven.  Isaiah 46:13 Psalms 38:1

title: Jeremiah 10:24
text: With judgment; the same as "in measure."   Isaiah 27:8

title: Jeremiah 10:25
text: The severity of the fatherly chastisements which God inflicts upon his own people, is a solemn warning to the ungodly of the utter destruction which awaits them.   Luke 23:31 I Peter 4:17-18

title: Jeremiah 11:1
text:
vv 1-17. 
 
God never fails to fulfil his promises to such as keep his covenant, whether nations or individuals; and he will certainly execute his threatenings upon all who break it.

title: Jeremiah 11:4
text: Do them; the "words of this covenant."

title: Jeremiah 11:5
text: So be it; may they thus obey thy covenant and inherit the land.

title: Jeremiah 11:9
text: A conspiracy; to break God's covenant,  Jeremiah 11:10 .

title: Jeremiah 11:15
text:
The holy flesh; the flesh of the sacrifices.   Haggai 2:12  
 
  Is passed from thee; is rejected by God as unclean, with the accessory idea that it shall cease to be offered during the approaching captivity.

title: Jeremiah 11:18
text:
The Lord hath given me knowledge; of the conspiracy of the men of Anathoth against my life.  To this the remainder of the present chapter relates. 
 
vv 18-23. 
 
God understands all the secret plots of the wicked against the righteous, and he can easily expose them, and deliver his servants from them; but they must not hesitate to declare his whole counsel, even at the hazard of life.
